eren-jager.name: Eren Yeager
eren-jager.role: Protagonist; member of the Survey Corps

debut.episodeTitle: To You, in 2000 Years: The Fall of Shiganshina, Part 1

eren-jager.notes: Arc names follow the Attack on Titan Wiki anime arc pages.
eren-jager.abilities: Discovers during the Battle of Trost that he can transform into a 15-metre Titan, and otherwise fights Titans with blades and vertical maneuvering equipment like the other cadets.

fate.detail: Mikasa kills him by decapitating him in his Titan form during the final battle (manga chapter 138, 2021; adapted in the anime's Final Chapters Special 2, 2023).

eren-jager.about: Eren Yeager grows up in Shiganshina, a town on the outer rim of the walled territory where humanity shelters from the Titans, and he hates the idea of living penned in. Inspired by a forbidden book Armin Arlert showed him, he wants to join the Survey Corps and see what lies beyond the Walls. After Titans break through and wreck his home, that wish turns into a vow to rid the world of them, and he enlists in the 104th Training Corps with his adoptive sister Mikasa and Armin. Eren is stubborn, hot-tempered and quick to act before thinking. His refusal to accept defeat is what pushes the people around him forward.

l-lawliet.name: L Lawliet
l-lawliet.role: Detective leading the investigation into Kira
l-lawliet.abilities: The world's greatest detective, who works anonymously through deduction, surveillance and psychological traps, often baiting suspects into revealing themselves.

fate.detail: L dies of a heart attack after the Shinigami Rem writes his name in her Death Note to protect Misa (anime episode 25, "Silence"; manga volume 7).

l-lawliet.about: L is the faceless investigator Interpol calls in when criminals across the globe begin dropping dead of heart attacks. He speaks to the police only through his aide Watari and a screen showing a single Gothic letter, and his first move is a televised bluff that tricks Kira into revealing he is based in the Kanto region. When he finally meets the Japanese task force in person, he turns out to be a pale, scruffy young man who sits crouched on chairs, goes barefoot and survives on cake and sugar cubes. His suspicion settles early on the student Light Yagami, and the polite, quietly ruthless duel of bluffs and probability guesses that follows drives the story's first half.

saitama.name: Saitama
saitama.role: Protagonist; hero who can defeat any opponent with one punch
saitama.notes: Chapter number refers to the Yusuke Murata manga; he also debuts in chapter 1 of ONE's webcomic.
saitama.abilities: So overwhelmingly strong that he defeats nearly every opponent with a single punch, a power he says came from a simple daily training routine.

fate.detail: Saitama is alive in both the anime and the ongoing manga (as of November 2026); no death has occurred.

saitama.about: Saitama is a bald, unremarkable-looking man in his mid-twenties who works as a hero mostly on his own terms. He claims a plain routine of push-ups, sit-ups, squats and daily running made him so strong that he now finishes almost any fight with a single punch. The catch is that easy victories have left him bored, and he keeps searching for an opponent who can actually challenge him. Outside battle he is deadpan and ordinary, more concerned with everyday errands than glory. He gains a devoted student in the cyborg Genos and later signs up with the Hero Association, where almost nobody realises how strong he is. That gap between power and recognition drives much of the comedy.

ken-kaneki.name: Ken Kaneki
ken-kaneki.role: Protagonist; university student who becomes a half-ghoul
ken-kaneki.notes: Chapter 1 per the Tokyo Ghoul Wiki; Wikipedia confirms he appears on the volume 1 cover. Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
ken-kaneki.abilities: After receiving a ghoul's organs he becomes a half-ghoul with superhuman strength and healing and a rinkaku kagune of tentacles that grows from his back.

fate.detail: Kaneki survives to the end of Tokyo Ghoul:re (2018), marrying Touka and having a daughter; the anime's :re season 2 ends the same way.

ken-kaneki.about: Ken Kaneki is a quiet Kamii University student who would rather read novels than go out, until a date with Rize, a woman he admires from the café, ends with her trying to eat him. A falling steel beam saves his life, and the doctors give him her organs. He wakes up half-ghoul: human food now tastes revolting, one eye turns red and black when he is hungry, and he craves the flesh he once feared. Hiding this from his cheerful best friend Hide, he finds reluctant help at Anteiku, a coffee shop run by ghouls. Viewers follow him for the gentle, conflicted way he tries to belong to two worlds that want each other dead.

mikasa-ackerman.name: Mikasa Ackerman
mikasa-ackerman.role: Eren Yeager's adoptive sister; member of the Survey Corps

debut.episodeTitle: To You, in 2000 Years: The Fall of Shiganshina, Part 1

mikasa-ackerman.abilities: The top graduate of the 104th Training Corps, with exceptional speed, strength and skill with vertical maneuvering equipment; she is described as worth a hundred ordinary soldiers.

fate.detail: Mikasa survives the series; the final chapter (139) and the anime's Final Chapters Special 2 show her living on and visiting Eren's grave.

mikasa-ackerman.about: Mikasa Ackerman joined the Yeager household as a young girl after Eren rescued her from kidnappers, and she has stayed by his side ever since. She still wears the red scarf he wrapped around her that day. Quiet and composed, she treats keeping Eren alive as her main purpose, often hauling him out of fights he starts. When he decides to become a soldier, she enlists too and finishes first in the 104th Training Corps, far ahead of her classmates in strength, speed and handling of vertical maneuvering equipment. Together with Armin Arlert the three form the friendship at the centre of the early story, and her calm lethality in combat makes her stand out.

sakura-haruno.name: Sakura Haruno
sakura-haruno.notes: Chapter 3 is confirmed by both sources. The episode 1 anime debut rests on Narutopedia; Wikipedia episode summaries first name her in episode 3. Arcs from Kazekage Rescue Mission on are in Naruto: Shippuuden.
sakura-haruno.abilities: A ninja-academy top student with excellent book knowledge and fine chakra control and a sharp eye for spotting genjutsu illusions, though she starts out weaker in combat than her teammates.

fate.detail: Sakura survives the Fourth Shinobi World War and is alive at the end of Naruto (chapter 700), married to Sasuke with a daughter, Sarada.

sakura-haruno.about: Sakura Haruno is the third member of Team 7, placed alongside Naruto Uzumaki and Sasuke Uchiha under the teacher Kakashi Hatake. At the start she is a bookish academy graduate with top marks on written work and fine control over her chakra, but little real combat experience. Most of her early energy goes into winning Sasuke's attention, which puts her at odds with her old friend Ino Yamanaka, while she brushes off Naruto's crush on her. What sets her apart early on is the gap between her polite outward manner and her loud 'Inner Sakura', a second voice that says exactly what she thinks, and her sharp eye for spotting illusions that fool her teammates.

kakashi-hatake.name: Kakashi Hatake

debut.episodeTitle: Sasuke and Sakura: Friends or Foes?

kakashi-hatake.notes: Chapter 3 is confirmed by both sources. Episode 3 rests on Narutopedia; the Wikipedia summary of episode 3 mentions the team's jonin instructor without naming him. Arcs from Kazekage Rescue Mission on are in Naruto: Shippuuden.
kakashi-hatake.abilities: Known as the Copy Ninja: his Sharingan eye lets him copy other ninjas' techniques, and his signature attack is the lightning-charged Chidori (Lightning Blade).

fate.detail: Kakashi dies of chakra exhaustion fighting Pain during the invasion of Konoha (Shippuden Pain's Assault arc) but is brought back to life when Nagato revives everyone killed in the attack; he survives the series and becomes the Sixth Hokage.

kakashi-hatake.about: Kakashi Hatake is the jonin put in charge of Team 7: Naruto Uzumaki, Sasuke Uchiha and Sakura Haruno. Soon after meeting them, he sets them a bell-stealing test that is really about teamwork, the value he stresses above all others. Kakashi seems lazy and easy-going. He turns up late with weak excuses, reads the adult Make-Out Paradise novels in public, and keeps most of his face behind a mask. Underneath, he ranks among the strongest ninja in Konoha, known as the Copy Ninja because the Sharingan in his covered left eye lets him copy other fighters' techniques. His own signature attack is the Chidori.

asahi-azumane.name: Asahi Azumane
asahi-azumane.role: Ace wing spiker of Karasuno High's volleyball team
asahi-azumane.notes: Chapter rests on the Haikyuu!! Wiki: briefly seen in chapter 17 ("Storm"), properly introduced in chapter 18. The wiki titles episode 8 "He Who Is Called 'Ace'".
asahi-azumane.abilities: Karasuno's ace wing spiker, the team's physically strongest player, whose powerful spikes can break through blocks.

fate.detail: Nobody dies in Haikyu!!; the manga's epilogue shows Asahi working as an apparel designer in Tokyo.

asahi-azumane.about: Asahi Azumane is the third-year wing spiker Karasuno's players call their ace, though when the story begins he has stopped coming to practice. Tall, bearded and wearing his hair in a bun, he looks like a delinquent, but he is anxious and soft-spoken, and he blames himself for a match where Date Tech's towering blockers stuffed his attacks again and again. His friend Yu Nishinoya, the team's libero, badly wants him back on the court, and captain Daichi and setter Suga keep the door open. His first-season story is about finding the nerve to swing again: he is a gentle giant whose problem was never power.

nate-river.name: Nate River
nate-river.role: Successor to L; head of the SPK
nate-river.notes: Episode 26 and chapter 59 ("Zero") rest on the Death Note Wiki; the Wikipedia summary of episode 26 shows two unnamed children and first names Near in episode 27.
nate-river.abilities: A child prodigy detective known as Near, raised at Wammy's House as one of L's potential successors; he solves cases through cold logic while playing with toys and puzzles.

fate.detail: Near survives: he exposes Light as Kira at the Yellow Box warehouse in the final arc and takes over the role of L (manga chapters 103-108; anime episodes 36-37).

nate-river.about: Nate River, who goes by the alias Near, is a young genius raised at Wammy's House, the English orphanage where candidates to succeed the detective L were trained. He arrives in the second part of Death Note as head of the SPK, a special unit formed in the United States to catch Kira. Near looks and behaves like a child: he sits hunched over, twirls his white hair, and thinks through problems while playing with dice, puzzles and toy figures. He approaches the investigation as a logic game and rarely shows emotion. His fellow Wammy's House candidate Mello pursues the same goal by far more reckless means, and their rivalry shapes the later story.

touka-kirishima.name: Touka Kirishima
touka-kirishima.role: Ghoul who works as a waitress at the Anteiku café
touka-kirishima.notes: Episode 1 and chapter 1 debut rest on the Tokyo Ghoul Wiki; Wikipedia episode summaries first name her in episode 3.
touka-kirishima.abilities: A ghoul with an ukaku kagune, a wing-like organ that lets her fight with great speed and fire crystallised shards at range.

fate.detail: Touka survives Tokyo Ghoul:re; by the final chapter she is married to Kaneki and has a daughter, Ichika.

touka-kirishima.about: Touka Kirishima is a high school student who spends her evenings waiting tables at Anteiku, a café in Tokyo's 20th Ward that quietly shelters ghouls. She is blunt, short-tempered and fiercely protective of the people she counts as her own, and she hides her nature from her human classmate Yoriko, even forcing down the home cooking Yoriko makes for her. When the newly changed Ken Kaneki arrives, she treats him with open contempt, yet she ends up teaching him how ghouls survive. In a fight she wears a rabbit mask and attacks with a fast, wing-like kagune. That mix of hostility and hidden care defines her early on.

lelouch-lamperouge.name: Lelouch Lamperouge
lelouch-lamperouge.role: Exiled Britannian prince who leads the Black Knights as Zero

debut.anime: Code Geass: Lelouch of the Rebellion
debut.episodeTitle: The Day a New Demon was Born

lelouch-lamperouge.notes: Code Geass is an original anime, so there is no source chapter.
lelouch-lamperouge.abilities: A brilliant strategist and chess player who gains the Geass of Absolute Obedience, which lets him give any person one command they must obey by making eye contact.

fate.detail: In the final episode of Code Geass R2 (episode 25, 2008), Suzaku, disguised as Zero, stabs Lelouch to death as part of the 'Zero Requiem' plan; the 2019 film Lelouch of the Re;surrection, set in an alternate continuity that follows the compilation films, brings him back to life through C.C.

lelouch-lamperouge.about: Lelouch Lamperouge is a sharp, aloof student at Ashford Academy in Area 11, the name the Holy Britannian Empire gave Japan after conquering it. He is really an exiled Britannian prince who was sent to Japan as a political hostage alongside Nunnally, his younger sister, and he resents his father, the Emperor, for casting them aside. When a mysterious girl called C.C. grants him the Geass, a power that forces anyone who meets his gaze to obey one command, he dons a mask as Zero and builds the Black Knights resistance. Proud, theatrical and a strong chess player, he plans several moves ahead. His friendship with Suzaku Kururugi, who serves the empire, drives much of the drama.

franky.name: Franky
franky.role: Shipwright of the Straw Hat Pirates

debut.episodeTitle: Pirate Abduction Incident! A Pirate Ship That Can Only Await Her End!

franky.notes: Arcs listed are those covered on the wiki's pre-timeskip history page; he also takes part in every later Straw Hat arc.
franky.abilities: A self-made cyborg shipwright who runs on cola: his rebuilt body hides weapons such as the Strong Right fist and the Fresh Fire breath, and he builds the Straw Hats' ship, the Thousand Sunny.

fate.detail: Franky is alive in the anime and in the ongoing manga (as of November 2026); he nearly died years earlier, rebuilding his body from scrap after being run over by a sea train.

franky.about: Franky first appears in the Water 7 arc as the loud, self-styled boss of the Franky Family, a gang that takes apart ships for scrap and hunts bounties, and that robs the Straw Hats of the money they planned to spend repairing their ship. He is a huge, blue-haired cyborg who wears little more than an open shirt and swimming trunks, powers his body with cola, and strikes a pose while shouting 'SUPER' whenever he is pleased. Beneath the swagger he cries easily at sad stories. He trained as a shipwright under the fishman Tom alongside Iceburg, and he still dreams of building a ship that can carry a crew to the end of the sea.

light-yagami.name: Light Yagami
light-yagami.role: Protagonist; student who uses the Death Note as Kira
light-yagami.abilities: A top-ranked, highly intelligent student who finds the Death Note, a notebook that kills anyone whose name is written in it while the writer pictures the person's face.

fate.detail: After Near exposes him at the Yellow Box warehouse and Matsuda shoots him, Ryuk writes Light's name in his own Death Note and Light dies of a heart attack (manga chapter 107; anime episode 37, where he dies alone on a staircase rather than at the warehouse).

light-yagami.about: Light Yagami is a top-ranked high school student in Tokyo and the son of a senior police officer, polite and popular but privately bored with a world he considers rotten. Everything changes when he finds the Death Note, a notebook dropped by the shinigami Ryuk that kills anyone whose name is written in it. Light decides to use it to purge criminals and build a new world ruled by himself, and the public soon gives the unseen killer the name Kira. He is brilliant, proud and coldly calculating behind his friendly manner. The battle of wits between Light and the eccentric detective L, each trying to unmask the other first, drives the first half of the series.

ryuk.name: Ryuk
ryuk.role: Shinigami who drops the Death Note into the human world
ryuk.notes: He also appears in the 2003 one-shot pilot chapter, before the serialized chapter 1.
ryuk.abilities: A Shinigami (death god) who can kill anyone by writing their name in his Death Note, sees people's names and lifespans, flies, and is invisible to anyone who has not touched his notebook.

fate.detail: Ryuk survives; at the end (anime episode 37, manga chapter 107) he writes Light's name in his own Death Note, as he promised at the start, and returns to the Shinigami Realm.

ryuk.about: Ryuk is the Shinigami who sets Death Note in motion. Bored by the empty, decaying realm of the death gods, he lets a spare notebook fall into the human world simply to see what happens, and it lands at the feet of the student Light Yagami. Ryuk then follows Light everywhere, invisible to anyone who has not touched the notebook. He explains the rules when it suits him, refuses to take sides, and treats Light's crusade as entertainment. Tall and grinning, with a crooked frame and bulging eyes, he is mostly remembered for his craving for apples, which in the human world he finds almost irresistibly delicious.

rintarou-okabe.name: Rintarou Okabe
rintarou-okabe.role: Protagonist; self-styled mad scientist who founded the Future Gadget Laboratory
rintarou-okabe.notes: Steins;Gate is adapted from a visual novel (not a manga or light novel), so source is null; the character appears from the start of the game. The wiki gives episode 1 as "Prologue of the Beginning and the End -Turning Point-".
rintarou-okabe.abilities: A self-styled mad scientist whose invention, the PhoneWave, can send text messages to the past; he alone keeps his memories when the timeline changes, an ability he calls Reading Steiner.

fate.detail: Okabe survives the series and reaches the Steins Gate world line in the final episode (24) of the 2011 anime.

rintarou-okabe.about: Rintarou Okabe is an 18-year-old university student in Akihabara who prefers to be called Hououin Kyouma, a self-styled mad scientist at war with an imaginary sinister organisation. He runs the Future Gadget Laboratory in a rented room above a CRT television shop, building mostly useless inventions with Mayuri Shiina, a friend since childhood, and hacker Itaru Hashida. When one gadget, a microwave hooked up to a phone, turns out to send text messages into the past, he and the young neuroscientist Kurisu Makise start testing what it can do. Okabe strikes poses, says El Psy Kongroo and talks into a phone with no one on the line. Behind the act he cares deeply about his friends.

meliodas.name: Meliodas
meliodas.role: Captain of the Seven Deadly Sins; owner of the Boar Hat tavern
meliodas.notes: Chapter 1 per the wiki; Wikipedia confirms he is on the volume 1 cover. Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
meliodas.abilities: Captain of the Seven Deadly Sins, a swordsman with enormous strength whose signature power, Full Counter, reflects magic attacks back at the attacker with double the force.

fate.detail: Meliodas is killed by Estarossa in the Revival of the Commandments arc, but a curse from the Demon King revives him every time he dies; he survives the series and becomes King of Liones.

meliodas.about: Meliodas looks like a cheerful blond boy who runs the Boar Hat, a travelling tavern carried on the back of a giant pig named Hawk, where his cooking is notoriously bad. When Princess Elizabeth Liones stumbles into his bar searching for the Seven Deadly Sins, a band of knights blamed for a coup a decade earlier, he reveals that he is their captain, the Dragon's Sin of Wrath. He agrees to help her find his scattered comrades and stop the Holy Knights who have taken over her kingdom. Easygoing and given to teasing, he becomes deadly serious in battle, where his Full Counter turns an enemy's magic back on them with twice the force.

kishou-arima.name: Kishou Arima
kishou-arima.role: Special Class Ghoul Investigator of the CCG
kishou-arima.notes: Episode 9 and chapter 29 debut rest on the Tokyo Ghoul Wiki; the Wikipedia summary of episode 9 does not name him. Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
kishou-arima.abilities: Called the CCG's 'Reaper' and considered undefeated, he is the strongest ghoul investigator, fighting with quinque weapons such as the lightning-firing IXA and Narukami.

fate.detail: After losing to Ken Kaneki in the Cochlea battle, Arima cuts his own throat with his quinque (Tokyo Ghoul:re chapter 82); the 2018 Tokyo Ghoul:re anime adapts his death, while in the earlier Root A anime he survives.

kishou-arima.about: Kishou Arima is a Special Class investigator of the CCG, the government agency that hunts ghouls, and he is close to a legend inside the organisation. Calm, white-haired and bespectacled, he is said never to have lost a fight, and his record has earned him the title of the CCG's Reaper. Younger investigators such as Koutarou Amon look up to him. In the first season he appears only briefly, yet his reputation shapes the story well before he acts. He fights with quinques, weapons made from ghoul organs, including the lightning-firing IXA and Narukami. What viewers remember is the gap between his soft-spoken, almost absent manner and how completely he dominates in battle.

killua-zoldyck.name: Killua Zoldyck
killua-zoldyck.role: Former assassin of the Zoldyck family; Gon's best friend
killua-zoldyck.notes: Chapter 6 is confirmed by both sources. Episode 3 is from the Hunter x Hunter Wiki; the Wikipedia summary introduces him in episode 4 ("Hope × and × Ambition").
killua-zoldyck.abilities: Raised as an assassin by the Zoldyck family, he is extremely fast, resistant to poison and electricity, and can turn his hands into blades.

fate.detail: Killua is alive in the 2011 anime and the manga so far (on hiatus as of November 2026); at the end of the anime he travels with his sister Alluka.

killua-zoldyck.about: Killua Zoldyck is a twelve-year-old with white hair and a skateboard who turns up at the Hunter Exam mainly because he is bored. He was born into the Zoldyck family, a household of professional assassins, and was trained from infancy to resist poison and kill without hesitation, but he has run away from home after deciding he does not want that life. Killua quickly befriends Gon Freecss, the first person his own age who treats him as an equal. He is playful, cocky and fond of chocolate, yet he can turn cold and frightening in an instant. That contrast, and his growing loyalty to Gon, define him.

gabi-braun.name: Gabi Braun
gabi-braun.role: Eldian Warrior candidate in Marley; Reiner Braun's cousin

debut.anime: Attack on Titan: The Final Season
debut.episodeTitle: The Other Side of the Sea

gabi-braun.notes: Episode 1 of The Final Season is episode 60 overall. Chapter 91 ("The Other Side of the Ocean") rests on the Attack on Titan Wiki only.
gabi-braun.abilities: A fiercely determined Warrior candidate in Marley's army, and the leading candidate to inherit the Armored Titan; she is athletic, quick-thinking and fearless.

fate.detail: Gabi survives the war and is among the survivors in the final chapter (139) and the anime's Final Chapters Special 2.

gabi-braun.about: Gabi Braun is a young Eldian girl from the Liberio internment zone in Marley, the nation across the sea from the island of Paradis. Eldians there must prove their loyalty, and Gabi trains as a Warrior candidate in Marley's army, the leading contender to inherit a Titan power from her cousin Reiner Braun. She is loud, athletic, fearless and completely convinced that the people of Paradis are devils who deserve punishment. She leads a small group of fellow candidates, including the gentler Falco Grice, who hopes to beat her to the title for her own sake. Many viewers see in her fierce certainty an echo of the young Eren from the first season.

osamu-dazai-5df9c678-bb69-4154-84e6-62ec.name: Osamu Dazai
osamu-dazai-5df9c678-bb69-4154-84e6-62ec.role: Member of the Armed Detective Agency; former Port Mafia executive
osamu-dazai-5df9c678-bb69-4154-84e6-62ec.abilities: An Armed Detective Agency member whose ability, No Longer Human, cancels any other supernatural ability he touches; he is also a brilliant strategist.

fate.detail: Dazai is alive in the anime (5 seasons) and the ongoing manga (as of November 2026).

osamu-dazai-5df9c678-bb69-4154-84e6-62ec.about: Osamu Dazai enters the story floating face-up in a Yokohama river, where the starving orphan Atsushi Nakajima pulls him out, only to learn he was trying to drown himself on purpose. Dazai works for the Armed Detective Agency, a firm that takes on cases too dangerous for the police, and he soon recruits Atsushi into it. He is bandaged, lazy and playful, talks often about finding a pleasant way to die, and drives his rule-bound partner Kunikida up the wall. His ability, No Longer Human, cancels any other supernatural power he touches. Behind the jokes he is the sharpest strategist in the room, and his past is something he rarely discusses.

taiga-aisaka.name: Taiga Aisaka
taiga-aisaka.role: Female lead; Ryuuji Takasu's classmate, nicknamed the Palmtop Tiger
taiga-aisaka.notes: The wiki gives chapter 1 of the first light novel; Wikipedia confirms she is on the volume 1 cover.
taiga-aisaka.abilities: Small but ferocious, she earns the nickname 'Palmtop Tiger' for her violent temper and is not afraid to swing a wooden sword at people.

fate.detail: Taiga is alive at the end of the series (episode 25 of the anime and the final light novel); no character dies in Toradora!.

taiga-aisaka.about: Taiga Aisaka is a second-year at Ohashi High School, tiny in build and ferocious in temper, which has earned her the nickname Palmtop Tiger. She lives alone in a luxury apartment right next to the home of Ryuuji Takasu, a gentle, house-proud boy whose sharp eyes make classmates think he is a delinquent. After a love letter meant for his best friend Yuusaku Kitamura ends up in Ryuuji's bag, the two strike a deal: he will help her win Kitamura, and she will help him with her best friend Minori Kushieda. Taiga is clumsy, blunt and quick to lash out, and she cannot cook for herself. Her prickly, increasingly dependent partnership with Ryuuji carries the story.

kurisu-makise.name: Kurisu Makise
kurisu-makise.role: Neuroscience researcher who joins the Future Gadget Laboratory
kurisu-makise.notes: Steins;Gate is adapted from a visual novel (not a manga or light novel), so source is null; the character appears from the start of the game. The wiki gives episode 1 as "Prologue of the Beginning and the End -Turning Point-". Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
kurisu-makise.abilities: An 18-year-old neuroscience researcher and genius scientist whose expertise in memory research becomes key to the lab's time-travel experiments.

fate.detail: Kurisu dies in the Beta world line (Okabe accidentally stabs her in episode 23 while trying to save her), but his final time leap rewrites events so she survives in the Steins;Gate world line (episode 24).

kurisu-makise.about: Kurisu Makise is an eighteen-year-old neuroscientist who finished university in the United States at seventeen and now researches memory at Viktor Chondria University's brain science institute. She is visiting Akihabara when her path crosses that of Rintaro Okabe, the self-proclaimed mad scientist who runs the tiny Future Gadget Laboratory, and her curiosity about his strange home-made gadgets soon makes her its fourth member. Kurisu is proud, sarcastic and quick to argue, but also openly curious and fair once the evidence is in front of her. Much of the early humour comes from her prickly back-and-forth with Okabe, who refuses to use her real name and keeps inventing nicknames such as 'Christina'.

kenny-ackerman.name: Kenny Ackerman
kenny-ackerman.role: Leader of the Anti-Personnel Control Squad serving the Reiss family
kenny-ackerman.notes: Season 3 episode 1 is episode 38 overall. Chapter 52 ("Krista Lenz") rests on the Attack on Titan Wiki only. Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
kenny-ackerman.abilities: A legendary serial killer and Ackerman with superhuman combat instincts who leads the Anti-Personnel Control Squad using guns attached to vertical maneuvering gear.

fate.detail: Fatally burned when Rod Reiss transforms, Kenny dies under a tree after revealing he is Levi's uncle and handing Levi the Titan serum (manga chapter 69; anime Season 3 episode 10, 'Friends').

kenny-ackerman.about: Kenny Ackerman commands the Anti-Personnel Control Squad, a Military Police unit trained to fight other people rather than Titans. Decades before the story he was Kenny the Ripper, a killer who slit the throats of Military Police officers in the capital until he faded into urban legend. Now he serves the Reiss family, and he hunts the Survey Corps with a squad that fires guns from modified vertical maneuvering gear. Lanky, wearing a wide-brimmed hat, he taunts his targets and plainly enjoys a fight. He also knew Levi long before Levi joined the Survey Corps, and that shared past makes their clashes personal.

gowther.name: Gowther
gowther.role: The Goat's Sin of Lust of the Seven Deadly Sins
gowther.notes: Episode 14 is where he is revealed (confirmed by both sources); the wiki also lists a brief cameo in episode 2. Chapter 53 rests on the wiki only.
gowther.abilities: The Seven Deadly Sins' Goat Sin of Lust, who can read and rewrite people's memories and minds with his Invasion power and fires arrows of light from his bow, Herritt.

fate.detail: Gowther survives to the end of the series; it is the original Gowther, the wizard who built him as a doll, who died 3,000 years earlier in the Holy War.

gowther.about: Known as the Goat's Sin of Lust, Gowther belongs to the Seven Deadly Sins, though the others have not seen him in years. When he finally steps out of a hulking suit of armour, he turns out to be a slim, pink-haired young man with round glasses. He speaks in a flat, literal way, does not grasp emotions, and often says hurtful things without realising it, so he studies friendship by watching how Meliodas and Ban treat each other. Gowther joins Elizabeth's quest out of a sense of duty rather than conviction. His power, Invasion, lets him read and rewrite people's memories, and he fights with Herritt, a bow that fires arrows of light.

koutaro-bokuto.name: Koutarou Bokuto
koutaro-bokuto.role: Captain and ace of Fukurodani Academy's volleyball team
koutaro-bokuto.notes: Second Season episode 4 is episode 29 overall. Episode and chapter 78 debut rest on the Haikyuu!! Wiki; the Wikipedia summary of that episode does not name him. He appears earlier in the OVA "Lev Genzan!".
koutaro-bokuto.abilities: Fukurodani's captain and ace, a powerful wing spiker ranked among the top five aces in Japan, though his mood swings can suddenly sink his performance.

fate.detail: Bokuto is alive throughout; Haikyu!! is a sports series and the manga ends with him playing professional volleyball for the MSBY Black Jackals.

koutaro-bokuto.about: Koutarou Bokuto is the third-year captain and ace of Fukurodani Academy, one of the strongest volleyball schools in Tokyo, and is ranked among Japan's five best high school aces. Loud, cheerful and childlike, he lives for the rush of a clean spike and wants everyone to see it. His great weakness is his mood: one blocked attack or small slight can send him into a sulk that drags his play down, and his calm setter Keiji Akaashi keeps a private list of ways to lift him back up. At the summer training camp, he and Nekoma's captain Tetsurou Kuroo coach Karasuno's Kei Tsukishima on blocking. His sudden swings between triumph and gloom are his best-known trait.

naruto-uzumaki.name: Naruto Uzumaki
naruto-uzumaki.role: Protagonist; ninja of Konohagakure who aims to become Hokage
naruto-uzumaki.notes: The last two arcs are in Naruto: Shippuuden.
naruto-uzumaki.abilities: A loud, never-give-up ninja who masters the Shadow Clone Jutsu early on and later the Rasengan; the Nine-Tailed Fox sealed inside him gives him vast chakra and stamina.

fate.detail: Naruto survives the series and becomes the Seventh Hokage; in the sequel manga Boruto, Kawaki seals him and Hinata away in a time-frozen dimension with Daikokuten, but he has not died.

naruto-uzumaki.about: Naruto Uzumaki is a loud, orange-clad orphan in the Hidden Leaf Village who plays pranks to get noticed, because most of the adults around him keep their distance. He fails his academy exams more than once, eats ramen whenever he can, and announces to anyone listening that he will become Hokage, the village's leader. In the first episode he learns why people avoid him: the Nine-Tailed Fox that once attacked the village is sealed inside his body. He is then placed on Team 7 with his rival Sasuke and his crush Sakura. His refusal to quit is his defining trait, and his favourite technique, the Shadow Clone Jutsu, which floods a fight with copies of himself, suits it perfectly.

sweet-mask.name: Amai Mask
sweet-mask.role: Top-ranked A-Class hero who is also an idol
sweet-mask.notes: Manga chapter left blank: the One Punch Man Wiki lists both chapter 25 and a separate titled chapter as his manga debut.
sweet-mask.abilities: The top-ranked A-Class hero, who refuses promotion to S-Class; he is also a famous idol and is fast and strong enough to destroy monsters with ease.

fate.detail: Amai Mask is alive in the anime and the ongoing manga (as of November 2026).

sweet-mask.about: Amai Mask, also known as Sweet Mask, holds the top rank in the Hero Association's A-Class and, away from hero work, is the most famous model, actor and singer in the world. Tall, slim and strikingly handsome, with light hair and a polished public smile, he is adored by fans. He is strong enough for S-Class but chooses to stay at the head of A-Class, where he can block heroes he considers too weak from climbing any higher. He believes a hero exists to protect people, and that anyone who cannot do so has no right to the title. That strict standard, and the cold efficiency with which he destroys monsters, set him apart from his peers.

chikara-ennoshita.name: Chikara Ennoshita
chikara-ennoshita.role: Second-year wing spiker of Karasuno High's volleyball team
chikara-ennoshita.notes: Episode 2 and chapter 10 ("Rookie Nerves") debut rest on the Haikyuu!! Wiki; the Wikipedia summary of episode 2 does not name him.
chikara-ennoshita.abilities: A second-year wing spiker who is a steady, calm substitute rather than a starter, with a level head and quiet leadership.

fate.detail: Nobody dies in Haikyu!!; Ennoshita becomes Karasuno's captain after the third-years graduate.

chikara-ennoshita.about: Chikara Ennoshita is a second-year at Karasuno High who plays wing spiker on the volleyball team, mostly as a substitute. Calm and soft-spoken, he is the steadiest of the second-years, the one who can rein in the noisy Tanaka and Nishinoya with a word. He gets good grades and has a knack for reading what teammates need, whether that is a joke or a push. On a team built around flashy players like Hinata and Kageyama, Ennoshita mostly works in the background in the first season. He serves as the quiet, dependable voice of reason in a loud locker room.

kaoru-hitachiin.name: Kaoru Hitachiin
kaoru-hitachiin.role: Host Club member; one of the Hitachiin twins

debut.episodeTitle: Starting Today, You Are a Host!

kaoru-hitachiin.notes: Episode 1 and chapter 1 debut rest on the Ouran Wiki; the Wikipedia summary of episode 1 refers to the Hosts without naming them.
kaoru-hitachiin.abilities: Performs the Host Club's popular 'forbidden brotherly love' act with his twin Hikaru; the twins are mischievous pranksters who are hard to tell apart.

fate.detail: Kaoru is alive at the end of the series; Ouran High School Host Club is a comedy with no character deaths.

kaoru-hitachiin.about: Kaoru Hitachiin is a first-year at the elite Ouran Academy and, with his slightly older brother Hikaru, one half of the Hitachiin twins. Rich, mischievous and nearly identical, the twins serve as the Host Club's 'little devil' hosts, and their staged displays of brotherly devotion delight the club's female guests. They love needling club president Tamaki Suou and take an instant interest in Haruhi Fujioka, the scholarship student who ends up working for the club as a host. Kaoru tends to be the calmer, more observant twin and often softens Hikaru's impulses. Their 'Which one is Hikaru?' guessing game, and how closed off they are from everyone else, recur through the series.

shiro-2.name: Shiro
shiro-2.role: Co-protagonist; half of the undefeated gamer duo Blank
shiro-2.notes: The light novel debut is volume 1; Wikipedia confirms she is on the volume 1 cover.
shiro-2.abilities: A gaming prodigy and half of the undefeated gamer duo Blank; she excels at calculation, chess and other strategy games with machine-like precision.

fate.detail: Shiro is alive in the anime (one season and the Zero film, which follows other characters) and the ongoing light novels.

shiro-2.about: Shiro is an eleven-year-old shut-in and a gaming genius who, with her eighteen-year-old stepbrother Sora, forms Blank, an online player whose record is completely unbeaten. She is the calm, calculating half of the pair: brilliant at chess and anything that rewards precise calculation, quiet, and almost helpless when she is apart from Sora. After the two win a chess game against a mysterious opponent, they are pulled into Disboard, a world ruled by the god Tet where every dispute, even war, is settled by games. There they set out to rebuild Elkia, the last human kingdom. Her deadpan bluntness is a counterweight to Sora's showmanship.

orihime-inoue.name: Orihime Inoue
orihime-inoue.role: Ichigo Kurosaki's classmate with healing powers
arcs: Arrancar: The Hueco Mundo Sneak Entry
orihime-inoue.notes: Chapter 2 is confirmed by both sources. Episode 2 rests on the Bleach Wiki; the Wikipedia summary of episode 2 does not name her. Arc names are mapped from the Bleach Wiki's manga arcs to the anime arcs in arcs.json.
orihime-inoue.abilities: Her hairpins hold the Shun Shun Rikka, six fairy-like spirits that let her raise barriers, heal injuries by 'rejecting' what happened, and launch a small cutting attack.

fate.detail: Orihime survives the series; the final chapter (686, 2016) shows her married to Ichigo with a son, Kazui.

orihime-inoue.about: Orihime Inoue is a cheerful, dreamy classmate of Ichigo Kurosaki at Karakura High School, known for strange food combinations, elaborate daydreams and saying whatever comes into her head. She lives on her own and rarely removes the pair of hairpins her older brother gave her. Her protective best friend, Tatsuki Arisawa, has watched over her since middle school, and Orihime quietly has feelings for Ichigo. Once she is drawn into his new double life as a Soul Reaper, her hairpins awaken as the Shun Shun Rikka, six tiny spirits that let her raise shields, mend injuries and strike back. She then joins the group that sets out to rescue Rukia Kuchiki.

tenya-iida.name: Tenya Iida
tenya-iida.role: Student in U.A. High School's Class 1-A
tenya-iida.notes: Episode 3 and chapter 3 debut rest on the My Hero Academia Wiki; the Wikipedia summary of episode 3 does not name him.
tenya-iida.abilities: Class 1-A's class representative; his Quirk, Engine, gives him engines in his calves for great running speed.

fate.detail: Iida survives the manga's Final War and is alive at the series ending (chapter 430, 2024).

tenya-iida.about: Tenya Iida is a tall, bespectacled first-year in U.A. High School's Class 1-A who comes from a family of professional heroes and idolises his older brother, the hero Ingenium. He takes rules extremely seriously, scolds classmates for small breaches of etiquette, and gestures with stiff chopping motions of his hand. His Quirk, Engine, gives him exhaust ports in his calves that let him run at great speed. Iida first eyes Izuku Midoriya with suspicion, then comes to respect him, and he ends up as class representative after keeping a panicking crowd calm during a security alarm. His earnest, overly formal manner and sincere wish to do right are the core of his character.

diego-brando.name: Diego Brando
diego-brando.role: British jockey and rival racer in the Steel Ball Run

debut.anime: Steel Ball Run: JoJo no Kimyou na Bouken

diego-brando.notes: Episode 1 (a 47-minute special that premiered on Netflix on 19 March 2026; episode 191 of the JoJo anime overall) is confirmed by both sources. Chapter 1 of Steel Ball Run rests on the JoJo Wiki only.
diego-brando.abilities: A champion British jockey and one of the race's fastest riders; early in the race he gains the Stand Scary Monsters, which lets him turn himself and others into dinosaurs.

fate.detail: Funny Valentine kills him during the fight on the train near the end of the race; an alternate Diego from a parallel world then takes his place and is destroyed when Lucy Steel forces him to merge with the original Diego's severed head (Steel Ball Run manga).

diego-brando.about: Diego Brando, usually called Dio, is an English jockey who rose from poverty to become a racing celebrity and a leading favourite in the Steel Ball Run, a horse race across North America with a huge cash prize. Handsome, ambitious and ruthless, he shows the public a charming face while doing whatever it takes to win. He sees the race as his route to wealth and status, and he treats other riders, Gyro Zeppeli and Johnny Joestar above all, as rivals to beat by any means. Long-time JoJo readers will recognise him as an alternate-universe version of the original Dio Brando, with a similar look and temperament but a separate life.

itaru-hashida.name: Itaru Hashida
itaru-hashida.role: Hacker and Lab Member 003 of the Future Gadget Laboratory
itaru-hashida.notes: Steins;Gate is adapted from a visual novel (not a manga or light novel), so source is null; the character appears from the start of the game. The wiki gives episode 1 as "Prologue of the Beginning and the End -Turning Point-". Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
itaru-hashida.abilities: Lab Member 003, nicknamed Daru: a super-hacker and electronics expert who builds and programs the lab's gadgets.

fate.detail: Daru survives the series in every world line shown; he is the future father of Suzuha.

itaru-hashida.about: Itaru Hashida, nicknamed Daru, is Rintaro Okabe's friend from high school, now a first-year at Tokyo Denki University and member 003 of the Future Gadget Laboratory. He is a heavy-set otaku who spends his days in front of a computer, drops crude remarks about girls real and animated, and is a regular at a maid café in Akihabara. He grumbles about Okabe's grand schemes yet carries out almost every request, and he is the one with the real technical skills: a hacker and programmer who keeps the lab's equipment running. His deadpan comebacks puncture Okabe's theatrics, and he is the practical engineer behind every wild idea.

kurapika.name: Kurapika
kurapika.role: Last survivor of the Kurta Clan, hunting the Phantom Troupe
kurapika.abilities: The last survivor of the Kurta Clan, whose eyes turn scarlet when he is enraged; during the Hunter Exam he fights with twin swords and stands out for his intelligence and calm analysis.

fate.detail: Kurapika is alive in the ongoing manga (Succession War arc, as of November 2026) and at the end of the 2011 anime, although his Emperor Time ability shortens his lifespan each time he uses it.

kurapika.about: Kurapika is a reserved, fair-haired young man who takes the Hunter Exam for one reason: a Hunter licence will help him pursue revenge. He is the last known survivor of the Kurta Clan, a people whose eyes turn a vivid scarlet when they feel strong emotion, and who were massacred by the thieves of the Phantom Troupe for those eyes. Calm, well-read and analytical, he fights with twin swords during the exam and forms close friendships with Gon Freecss, Leorio Paradinight and Killua Zoldyck. Beneath his courtesy lies a cold, single-minded drive to find the Troupe and recover his people's stolen eyes, and that pull between friendship and vengeance defines him.

alois-trancy.name: Alois Trancy
alois-trancy.role: Earl of the Trancy household and master of the butler Claude Faustus
alois-trancy.notes: Created for the Black Butler II anime; the wiki lists no manga debut. Black Butler II episode 1 is episode 25 overall. Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
alois-trancy.abilities: The young Earl Trancy, whose real weapon is his contract with the demon butler Claude Faustus, who carries out his orders with inhuman skill.

fate.detail: Claude kills Alois in Black Butler II episode 8, "Divulging Butler"; his soul then lives on inside the demon maid Hannah until the finale (anime-only character).

alois-trancy.about: Alois Trancy is the young earl who heads the Trancy household in Black Butler II, a character created for the anime. At fourteen he is blond, bratty and wildly changeable, swinging from childish affection to sudden cruelty toward his own staff. His butler, Claude Faustus, is a demon bound to him by contract, and the household also includes the silent maid Hannah and a set of identical triplet servants. Alois shows an intense interest in Ciel Phantomhive and his butler Sebastian, which pulls the two houses into conflict, while his relatives question whether he is truly who he claims to be. He serves as an unsettling, unpredictable rival to Ciel.

reiner-braun.name: Reiner Braun
reiner-braun.role: Eren's fellow trainee in the 104th Training Corps

debut.episodeTitle: That Day: The Fall of Shiganshina, Part 2

reiner-braun.notes: Episode 2 and chapter 2 debut rest on the Attack on Titan Wiki; Wikipedia episode summaries first name him in episode 3. Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
reiner-braun.abilities: One of the top graduates of the 104th Training Corps, admired by the other cadets for his physical strength, reliability and leadership.

fate.detail: Reiner survives the series; he is among the survivors after the final battle, when the power of the Titans disappears (manga chapter 139; anime Final Chapters Special 2, 2023).

reiner-braun.about: Reiner Braun is a cadet in the 104th Training Corps who graduates second in his class, just behind Mikasa Ackerman. Tall, broad-shouldered and dependable, he acts as a big brother to the other trainees, offering advice, keeping spirits up and helping Eren Yeager with hand-to-hand combat during training. He says he comes from a mountain village inside Wall Maria that was lost when the Titans broke through, and he is rarely seen without his quiet friend Bertolt Hoover, who grew up in the same area. Reiner speaks often about a soldier's duty and protecting his comrades. His steadiness makes him the person the other cadets lean on when things go wrong.

olivier-mira-armstrong.name: Olivier Mira Armstrong
olivier-mira-armstrong.role: Major General in command of Fort Briggs
olivier-mira-armstrong.notes: Chapter 63 rests on the Fullmetal Alchemist Wiki only. Arc names follow the wiki's story sections.
olivier-mira-armstrong.abilities: The commander of Fort Briggs, a master swordswoman and tactician with an iron will who runs the northern fortress with strict discipline.

fate.detail: Olivier survives the Promised Day battle and is alive at the end of the series, appearing in the epilogue photo collage.

olivier-mira-armstrong.about: Olivier Mira Armstrong is the major general who commands Fort Briggs, the fortress guarding Amestris's frozen northern border with Drachma. She is the eldest child of the aristocratic Armstrong family and openly scornful of her soft-hearted younger brother, Major Alex Louis Armstrong. Her creed at Briggs is that the strong survive, and her soldiers have standing orders to leave her behind if that is what the fortress needs; they follow her with fierce loyalty anyway. When Edward and Alphonse Elric arrive in the north, she treats them with open suspicion, judging them purely on whether they can be of use. One episode title calls her the Ice Queen, a name that fits her command style.

asuna-yuuki.name: Asuna Yuuki
asuna-yuuki.role: Female lead; sub-leader of the Knights of the Blood guild
asuna-yuuki.notes: Light novel debut is volume 1, chapter 5 (confirmed by both sources). Episode 2 is her first full appearance; the wiki also lists a brief cameo in episode 1.
asuna-yuuki.abilities: One of Aincrad's strongest players, nicknamed 'the Flash' for her lightning-fast rapier attacks, and sub-leader of the Knights of the Blood guild.

fate.detail: Asuna survives: her avatar's HP drops to zero when she shields Kirito from Heathcliff (anime episode 14), but Kirito clears the game and she wakes up in the real world; she is alive in all later arcs.

asuna-yuuki.about: Asuna Yuuki is among the 10,000 people trapped inside Sword Art Online, a virtual reality game in which losing all your hit points means dying in the real world. She pushes herself relentlessly from the start and becomes one of the best fighters in Aincrad, the game's floating castle of a hundred floors. Her speed with the rapier earns her the nickname the Flash, and she becomes second-in-command of the game's strongest guild, the Knights of the Blood. Serious and driven at first, she slowly loosens up after spending time with the solo player Kirito, who reminds her there is more to life in Aincrad than clearing floors.

all-might.name: All Might
all-might.role: Symbol of Peace; top Pro Hero and mentor to Izuku Midoriya
all-might.notes: Chapter 1 per the wiki; Wikipedia confirms he is on the volume 1 cover.
all-might.abilities: The Symbol of Peace and No. 1 Hero, whose Quirk One For All gives him overwhelming strength and speed; an old injury limits how long he can stay in his muscle form.

fate.detail: All Might survives; he retires after the Kamino battle and, despite being badly hurt fighting All For One in the Final War, is alive at the manga's ending (chapter 430) and in the anime's final season.

all-might.about: All Might is Japan's number-one hero, known as the Symbol of Peace, a towering figure with a permanent grin who rescues people while announcing that everything is fine because he is here. Young Izuku Midoriya has idolised him for years. When the two meet, Izuku learns that the hero is badly injured and can hold his muscular form for only a few hours a day, otherwise shrinking into a gaunt, coughing man. All Might sees heroic instinct in the Quirkless boy and offers to pass on his power, One For All, then trains him for U.A. High School, where he also starts teaching. The contrast between his public smile and his private frailty is central to his character.

yuzuru-nishimiya.name: Yuzuru Nishimiya
yuzuru-nishimiya.notes: There is no TV anime: Koe no Katachi (A Silent Voice) is a 2016 film, so episode is null. Chapter 8 rests on the Koe no Katachi Wiki only.
yuzuru-nishimiya.abilities: Shoko's sharp-tongued, fiercely protective younger sister, who goes everywhere with a camera taking photographs.

fate.detail: Yuzuru is alive at the end of both the manga and the 2016 film; no death occurs.

yuzuru-nishimiya.about: Yuzuru Nishimiya is the younger sister of Shouko Nishimiya, a deaf girl who was bullied at elementary school. A middle schooler who rarely goes to class, she roams town with a camera, dresses plainly and keeps her hair cropped short, so people often take her for a boy; Shouya Ishida at first assumes she is Shouko's boyfriend. She cut her hair years earlier so that their mother would leave Shouko's long hair alone, and she has kept it short ever since. Sharp-tongued and openly hostile to anyone who hurt her sister, she tries hard to keep Shouya away when he returns hoping to make amends. Her stubborn loyalty gives the story much of its edge.

shouhei-fukunaga.name: Shouhei Fukunaga
shouhei-fukunaga.role: Wing spiker of Nekoma High's volleyball team
shouhei-fukunaga.notes: Episode 11 and chapter 27 ("The Cat-Crow Reunion") debut rest on the Haikyuu!! Wiki; the Wikipedia summary of episode 11 does not name him.
shouhei-fukunaga.abilities: Nekoma's quiet second-year wing spiker, known for odd, unpredictable spikes and a quirky sense of humour.

fate.detail: Nobody dies in Haikyu!!; Fukunaga is alive through the series ending.

shouhei-fukunaga.about: Shouhei Fukunaga is a second-year wing spiker for Nekoma High, the Tokyo school whose volleyball club has a long-standing 'cat versus crow' rivalry with Karasuno. He first appears when Nekoma travels north for a practice match, wearing the number 6 alongside players such as captain Tetsuro Kuroo, setter Kenma Kozume and libero Morisuke Yaku. Fukunaga rarely speaks and blends into a team that already prizes calm, patient defence, but his attacks have an odd, hard-to-predict quality that opponents struggle to read. He also has a deadpan, slightly strange sense of humour that surfaces in small background moments. He is a minor player, so most of his personality comes through in brief scenes.

hayase-nagatoro.name: Hayase Nagatoro
hayase-nagatoro.role: Title character; first-year student who teases her senpai

debut.episodeTitle: Senpai is a bit... / Senpai, don't you ever get angry?

hayase-nagatoro.notes: Episode 1 has two segments; both titles are given. Chapter 1 rests on the Nagatoro Wiki only (she also appears in issue 1 of the original webcomic).
hayase-nagatoro.abilities: An athletic, quick-witted first-year whose main talent is relentlessly teasing her shy senpai.

fate.detail: Nagatoro is alive throughout; the series is a romantic comedy with no character deaths.

hayase-nagatoro.about: Hayase Nagatoro is in her first year of high school, with tanned skin, a mischievous grin and a knack for appearing wherever her shy upperclassman happens to be. After she and her friends discover the manga he has been drawing, she starts spending her afternoons in the art club room with the second-year she only ever calls Senpai, mocking his art, his hobbies and his timid manner. Athletic and quick-witted, she belongs to the swimming club and is keen on martial arts. Her teasing is relentless but rarely truly cruel, and it often covers moments when she is flustered herself. The series follows how her provocation gradually pushes Senpai to stand up for himself.

c-c.name: C.C.
c-c.role: Immortal witch who grants Lelouch the power of Geass

debut.anime: Code Geass: Lelouch of the Rebellion
debut.episodeTitle: The Day a New Demon was Born

c-c.notes: Code Geass is an original anime, so there is no source chapter.
c-c.abilities: An immortal witch who grants the power of Geass through contracts; she heals from any wound and is immune to ageing.

fate.detail: C.C. is shot dead in the first episode and revives because she is immortal, and she 'dies' repeatedly in the same way; she outlives Lelouch and is alive at the end of R2 (episode 25).

c-c.about: C.C. is a green-haired young woman who first appears sealed inside a capsule the Britannian military is transporting through the Shinjuku Ghetto. When the exiled prince Lelouch stumbles into the scene and is cornered by soldiers, she offers him a contract: the power of Geass in exchange for a wish of hers that she will name later. She calls herself a witch, answers almost every question with a riddle, and soon moves into Lelouch's room at Ashford Academy, where she spends her time sprawled on his bed, ordering pizza on his account and hugging a cheese-mascot plush. She keeps her dry, teasing calm in almost any situation and reveals very little about herself.

caster-ddbb69e1-54df-4a04-b1c3-767126bbb.name: Caster
caster-ddbb69e1-54df-4a04-b1c3-767126bbb.role: Caster-class Servant of Ryuunosuke Uryuu in the Fourth Holy Grail War
caster-ddbb69e1-54df-4a04-b1c3-767126bbb.notes: His true identity is Gilles de Rais. Episode 2 rests on the Wikipedia episode summary; the TYPE-MOON Wiki confirms him as the Fate/Zero Caster summoned by Ryuunosuke Uryuu but gives no episode. Light novel chapter not confirmed.
caster-ddbb69e1-54df-4a04-b1c3-767126bbb.abilities: A Caster-class Servant (Gilles de Rais) with little magecraft of his own; his grimoire, Prelati's Spellbook, lets him summon near-endless swarms of tentacled sea monsters.

fate.detail: After he summons a giant sea monster on the Mion River, Saber destroys it and him with Excalibur (Fate/Zero, second season, 2012), eliminating him from the Holy Grail War.

caster-ddbb69e1-54df-4a04-b1c3-767126bbb.about: Caster is the Servant summoned into the Fourth Holy Grail War by Ryuunosuke Uryuu, a young serial killer who completes the ritual by accident with the blood of a family he has murdered. Tall and gaunt, with bulging eyes and dark robes, Caster shares his Master's delight in cruelty and has no real interest in winning the Grail. His own magecraft is limited, but the grimoire he carries lets him call up seemingly endless swarms of tentacled sea monsters. He becomes fixated on Saber, insisting she is someone he once revered, and that obsession draws him into the wider war. The pair's crimes push the other participants into an uneasy truce to stop them.

ban-b502349e-2c23-449b-82d8-995b8f5f67f6.name: Ban
ban-b502349e-2c23-449b-82d8-995b8f5f67f6.role: The Fox's Sin of Greed of the Seven Deadly Sins
ban-b502349e-2c23-449b-82d8-995b8f5f67f6.notes: Chapter 7 rests on the Seven Deadly Sins Wiki only.
ban-b502349e-2c23-449b-82d8-995b8f5f67f6.abilities: The Fox Sin of Greed, made immortal by drinking from the Fountain of Youth; his power Snatch lets him steal physical strength and objects from opponents.

fate.detail: Ban survives the series; he later gives up his immortality to bring Elaine back to life, marries her and rules the Kingdom of Benwick.

ban-b502349e-2c23-449b-82d8-995b8f5f67f6.about: Known as the Fox's Sin of Greed, Ban belongs to the Seven Deadly Sins, and when the story finds him he is chained up deep in the Baste Dungeon, a royal prison run by the Holy Knights. Tall, silver-haired and grinning, he is a former bandit who is effectively immortal, so torture barely slows him down, and he leaves when he chooses. His power, Snatch, lets him steal objects, speed and strength straight from an opponent. Ban greets his old captain Meliodas with a brawl that both of them treat as a friendly hello. He is laid-back, fond of ale and a far better cook than Meliodas, and he keeps his personal reasons for living close to his chest.

tobio-kageyama.name: Tobio Kageyama
tobio-kageyama.role: Setter for Karasuno High's volleyball team
tobio-kageyama.notes: Wikipedia notes his sister Miwa appears only in the manga.
tobio-kageyama.abilities: A genius setter once called the 'King of the Court', with pinpoint-accurate tosses, a powerful serve and lightning-quick reactions.

fate.detail: Kageyama is alive at the end of the manga (chapter 402, 2020), playing professional volleyball; Haikyu!! has no character deaths.

tobio-kageyama.about: Tobio Kageyama is a first-year setter at Karasuno High who arrives with a fearsome reputation from middle school, where teammates called him the King of the Court for the way he bossed them around. His sets are fast and precise, his serve is powerful and he reads the game several moves ahead, but his demand for perfection once left him isolated on court. At Karasuno he is forced to work with Shouyou Hinata, a short, explosive spiker his team beat in a middle school tournament, and together they build a lightning-fast attack that depends on complete trust. Blunt, intense and socially awkward, Kageyama slowly learns to read and support his hitters.

suguha-kirigaya.name: Suguha Kirigaya
suguha-kirigaya.role: Kirito's younger sister; plays ALfheim Online as Leafa

relatives.name: Kazuto Kirigaya
relatives.relation: cousin, raised as her older brother

suguha-kirigaya.notes: Episode 15 is her first full appearance (confirmed by both sources); the wiki also lists a brief cameo in episode 1. Light novel volume 3 (prologue) rests on the wiki only.
suguha-kirigaya.abilities: A national-level kendo competitor; in the game ALfheim Online she plays Leafa, a fast Sylph swordswoman and flier.

fate.detail: Suguha is alive through every adapted arc and the ongoing light novels.

suguha-kirigaya.about: Suguha Kirigaya is Kazuto Kirigaya's younger sister, a fifteen-year-old junior high student who has practised kendo since early childhood and competes at the national level. While her brother lies unconscious in hospital, his mind held captive by the game Sword Art Online, she tries to understand the world that took him by logging into another game, ALfheim Online. There she plays Leafa, a blonde Sylph swordswoman known for her speed and skill in flight. During the Fairy Dance arc, she meets a newcomer named Kirito and agrees to guide him toward the World Tree at the centre of the map. She is athletic, earnest and kind, and her arc gives the game-world adventure a quieter, family-centred side.

armin-arelet.name: Armin Arlert
armin-arelet.role: Childhood friend of Eren and Mikasa; member of the Survey Corps

debut.episodeTitle: To You, in 2000 Years: The Fall of Shiganshina, Part 1

armin-arelet.notes: Episode 1 and chapter 1 debut rest on the Attack on Titan Wiki; Wikipedia episode summaries first name him in episode 2.
armin-arelet.abilities: Physically the weakest of his friends, but a brilliant strategist whose quick thinking repeatedly finds a way out against the Titans.

fate.detail: Armin survives the series; he is badly burned and close to death in the Battle of Shiganshina (manga chapter 84) but is saved with the Titan serum, and in the final chapter (139) he leads the Allied peace delegation.

armin-arelet.about: Armin Arlert grew up in Shiganshina as the closest friend of Eren Yeager and Mikasa Ackerman, a small, gentle boy often picked on for his curiosity about the outside world. A forbidden book he shared with Eren, describing oceans and lands of ice and sand beyond the Walls, gave both boys the dream of exploring. When the three enlist in the 104th Training Corps, Armin is physically the weakest and constantly doubts himself, yet he excels in classroom subjects and has a gift for reading situations and forming plans under pressure. More than once his quick thinking finds a way out where strength alone cannot. His growth from self-doubting boy to trusted strategist is a key thread.

karma-akabane.name: Karma Akabane
karma-akabane.role: Student of Class 3-E at Kunugigaoka Junior High School
karma-akabane.notes: Episode 3 is his proper introduction (confirmed by both sources); the wiki also lists a cameo in episode 2. Chapter 3 rests on the wiki only.
karma-akabane.abilities: The cleverest troublemaker in Class 3-E, a skilled street fighter and cunning strategist who is one of the class's best assassins.

fate.detail: Karma survives the series; in the seven-years-later epilogue he has passed the exams to become a government official.

karma-akabane.about: Karma Akabane is a red-haired student who comes back to Kunugigaoka Junior High's Class 3-E, the school's dumping ground, after a suspension for fighting. He is clever enough to earn top marks, but he enjoys provoking people far more than following rules, and he treats the class's assignment to assassinate their tentacled teacher, Koro-sensei, as a personal game. On his first day back he becomes the first student to actually wound the creature, hiding anti-teacher knife fragments in his hand during a friendly handshake. Karma is an old classmate of Nagisa Shiota, and their friendship anchors much of the early story. His mischievous grin hides a mind willing to go to creative, reckless lengths to win.

alphonse-elric.name: Alphonse Elric
alphonse-elric.role: Co-protagonist; Edward Elric's younger brother, whose soul is bound to a suit of armor
alphonse-elric.abilities: A gifted alchemist whose soul is bound to a giant suit of armour; the armour makes him a powerful hand-to-hand fighter who never tires, eats or sleeps.

fate.detail: Al survives: in the final battle he trades his soul to restore Edward's arm, and Edward then gives up his own alchemy to bring Al back with his original body (manga chapter 108; Brotherhood episode 63).

alphonse-elric.about: Alphonse Elric is the younger of the two Elric brothers from the country village of Resembool. As children, he and Edward tried to use alchemy to bring their mother back, a forbidden act that cost Alphonse his whole body; Edward saved him by binding his soul to an empty, oversized suit of armour. Now about fourteen, he travels with his brother in search of the Philosopher's Stone, which they hope can restore what they lost. Inside the armour he cannot eat, sleep or feel touch, yet he is the gentler, more patient brother, fond of stray cats and quick to see the good in people. Strangers regularly mistake the towering Al for the Fullmetal Alchemist.

ami-kawashima.name: Ami Kawashima
ami-kawashima.role: Teen fashion model and Yusaku Kitamura's childhood friend who transfers into Ryuuji's class
ami-kawashima.notes: Episode 5 is confirmed by both sources. Light novel volume 2 rests on the Toradora! Wiki only.
ami-kawashima.abilities: A popular teen fashion model who hides a sharp, manipulative personality behind a sweet 'perfect girl' act, and is very perceptive about other people's feelings.

fate.detail: Nobody dies in Toradora!; Ami is alive at the end of the anime and light novels.

ami-kawashima.about: Ami Kawashima, a teenage fashion model and childhood friend of class president Yusaku Kitamura, joins Ryuuji Takasu's class as a transfer student about a month after term begins. In public she plays a sweet, slightly scatterbrained 'perfect girl', but Ryuuji and Taiga Aisaka quickly see the sharp, self-serving personality underneath, and Taiga in particular clashes with her at once. Ami left her old school partly to escape a stalker, and she tends to hide in a narrow gap between vending machines when she wants to be alone. She becomes one of the most perceptive people in the group, reading others' feelings faster than they read their own, which gives her some of the series' most pointed lines.

argo.name: Argo
argo.role: Information broker in Sword Art Online, nicknamed "Argo the Rat"
argo.notes: Episode 3 rests on the Sword Art Online Wiki; the Wikipedia summary of episode 3 does not name her. Light novel volume left blank: the wiki says she is first mentioned in volume 2 and first appears in person in Progressive volume 1.
argo.abilities: An information broker nicknamed 'the Rat' who sells intel about Aincrad; she is quick, stealthy and hard to catch.

fate.detail: Argo survives Sword Art Online and is logged out when Kirito clears the game.

argo.about: Argo, known in Aincrad as Argo the Rat, is an information broker inside the deadly virtual reality game Sword Art Online. Small, quick and hard to pin down, she has painted whisker marks on her cheeks, which earned her the nickname. Argo will sell almost any piece of information if the price is right, supposedly including the reason she wears those whiskers, yet she also writes free strategy guides that are stocked in shops to help newcomers survive. She keeps up a teasing, businesslike rapport with Kirito, and each suspects the other of having played in the game's beta test. Her network of tips and rumours makes her useful to the players fighting on the front lines.

asia-argento.name: Asia Argento
asia-argento.role: Former nun with the healing Sacred Gear Twilight Healing; member of the Occult Research Club
asia-argento.notes: Episode 2 (she is bumped into at the end) and light novel volume 1 rest on the High School DxD Wiki; Wikipedia episode summaries first name her in episode 3.
asia-argento.abilities: A gentle former nun whose Sacred Gear, Twilight Healing, can heal any wound, including those of devils.

fate.detail: Asia dies when Raynare rips out her Sacred Gear (light novel volume 1, adapted in the first anime season), and Rias revives her as a Devil and her Bishop; she is alive afterwards.

asia-argento.about: Asia Argento is a gentle young nun who arrives in Kuoh Town lost and searching for the local church. Issei Hyoudou, newly reborn as a devil, helps her find her way, and she shows him her Sacred Gear, Twilight Healing, by mending a child's scraped knee with soft green light. Asia grew up as an orphan and was revered by the Church for her gift, until she was cast out for healing a wounded devil. Naive about everyday life but sincere to the core, she longs most of all to have a real friend. Her innocent warmth and steady faith stand out sharply against the show's cast of devils.

atomic-samurai.name: Atomic Samurai
atomic-samurai.role: S-Class swordsman hero of the Hero Association
atomic-samurai.notes: His real name is Kamikaze. Chapter number refers to the Yusuke Murata manga.
atomic-samurai.abilities: An S-Class hero and master swordsman whose signature Atomic Slash cuts an enemy into countless pieces in an instant.

fate.detail: Atomic Samurai is alive in the anime and in the ongoing manga (as of November 2026).

atomic-samurai.about: Atomic Samurai, whose real name is Kamikaze, is one of the Hero Association's S-Class heroes and a master swordsman who trains three sword-wielding disciples of his own. He wears a hooded cloak marked with an atom symbol over a samurai gi, has long black hair and carries a katana at his hip. His signature technique, the Atomic Slash, cuts an opponent into countless pieces in an instant. Proud and blunt, he respects strength above everything else; at their first meeting he refuses to shake Saitama's hand, saying he only acknowledges people who prove themselves at the top. He treats a fight partly as a performance of skill and enjoys showing off.

barry-the-chopper.name: Barry the Chopper
barry-the-chopper.role: Serial killer whose soul is bound to a suit of armor guarding the Fifth Laboratory
barry-the-chopper.notes: Episode 7 (where he attacks Alphonse as "66") and chapter 11 rest on the Fullmetal Alchemist Wiki; Wikipedia episode summaries first name him in episode 8.
barry-the-chopper.abilities: A serial killer's soul bound to a suit of armour, fighting with meat cleavers; as an armour body he feels no pain and cannot tire.

fate.detail: In Brotherhood and the manga, Lust slashes his armour apart beneath Laboratory 3 and his dying original body then scratches out his blood seal, killing body and soul together; in the 2003 anime he survives longer.

barry-the-chopper.about: Barry the Chopper is a notorious Central City serial killer whom the military 'executed' on paper and then reused in an experiment, binding his soul to a suit of armour. Edward and Alphonse Elric meet him as Number 66, one of the guards posted at the abandoned Fifth Laboratory with orders to kill intruders. He fights with a meat cleaver, talks about butchering people with gleeful enthusiasm, and in a fight against Alphonse he uses his own situation to raise unsettling doubts about whether Al's memories are real. His cheerful, chatty manner makes him an unusually lively villain in a dark chapter of the story, and he carries a strange reputation as a killer who is also good company.

bertolt-hoover.name: Bertolt Hoover
bertolt-hoover.role: Reserved member of the 104th Training Corps and Reiner Braun's close friend

debut.episodeTitle: That Day: The Fall of Shiganshina, Part 2

bertolt-hoover.notes: Episode 2 (a brief appearance) rests on the Attack on Titan Wiki episode page; Wikipedia episode summaries first name him in episode 3. Manga chapter left blank because the listed debut chapter would spoil a plot reveal. Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
bertolt-hoover.abilities: A quiet, highly ranked cadet of the 104th Training Corps with strong all-round skills, though he lacks initiative and tends to follow Reiner.

fate.detail: Armin, turned into a mindless Titan, eats him to inherit the Colossal Titan during the Battle of Shiganshina (manga chapter 84; anime season 3 episode 18, 'Midnight Sun').

bertolt-hoover.about: Bertolt Hoover is a tall, quiet cadet in the 104th Training Corps who graduates third in his class, behind Mikasa Ackerman and his longtime friend Reiner Braun. The two grew up in the same area and are almost always seen together, with Bertolt usually following Reiner's lead. He performs well at nearly everything in training, but his instructors remark that he has little initiative and rarely puts himself forward. Bertolt confesses that he first meant to join the Military Police and live safely in the interior, and that Eren's determination made him feel like a coward for it. Polite, nervous and soft-spoken, he is one of the more reserved members of the class.

bishamon.name: Bishamon
bishamon.role: Goddess of war and fortune who holds a grudge against Yato
bishamon.notes: Episode 5 and chapter 6 rest on the Noragami Wiki; the Wikipedia summary of episode 5 does not name her. She is also called Bishamonten and Veena.
bishamon.abilities: One of the Seven Lucky Gods, a powerful war goddess who fights with a large retinue of regalia, including guns, a whip and a lion.

fate.detail: Bishamon is alive at the end of the manga (concluded 2023) and in the anime.

bishamon.about: Bishamon is a goddess of war and fortune, one of Japan's Seven Gods of Fortune, with a huge following of worshippers. She fights from the back of a great lion that is one of her many shinki, the spirits gods turn into weapons, and she keeps an unusually large household of them because she takes in nearly every lost soul she finds. Proud, formidable and protective of her followers, she reserves a burning hatred for the minor god Yato, whom she attacks on sight for reasons rooted in their shared past. Her clashes with him drive much of the first season's tension, and they show both her grandeur and her fierce loyalty to her own.

caynz.name: Caynz
caynz.role: Former member of the Golden Apple guild and Yolko's boyfriend
caynz.notes: Episode 5 is confirmed by both sources. Light novel volume 8 ("A Murder Case in the Area") rests on the Sword Art Online Wiki only.

fate.detail: His apparent murder inside a safe zone (anime episode 5, 'Murder in the Safe Zone') is staged with Yolko to catch a killer; he survives and is logged out when Kirito clears the game.

caynz.about: Caynz is a player trapped in Sword Art Online and a former member of Golden Apple, a small guild that broke up after losing its leader, Griselda. He is also the boyfriend of Yolko, another of its former members. His story begins when he is seen hanging from a church window, run through by a short spear, inside a town where the game's safety code is supposed to make harming players impossible. The incident alarms the front-line players, since it suggests someone has found a way to kill inside safe zones, and Kirito and Asuna join forces to investigate. Their search leads them into Golden Apple's past and a quarrel over a rare ring.

chainsaw-man-aki-hayakawa.name: Aki Hayakawa
chainsaw-man-aki-hayakawa.role: Public Safety Devil Hunter in Tokyo Special Division 4 and Denji's senior partner
chainsaw-man-aki-hayakawa.notes: Episode 2 is confirmed by both sources. Chapter 3 rests on the Chainsaw Man Wiki only.
chainsaw-man-aki-hayakawa.abilities: A Public Safety devil hunter who fights with a katana and contracts with devils, chiefly the Fox Devil, which he summons to bite enemies.

fate.detail: In the Gun Devil arc of the manga's Part 1 the Gun Devil takes over his body, turning him into the Gun Fiend, and Denji kills him; this has not been animated yet as of November 2026.

chainsaw-man-aki-hayakawa.about: Aki Hayakawa is a devil hunter in Public Safety's Tokyo Special Division 4, working under Makima. When she brings in Denji, a broke teenager fused with a chainsaw devil, she assigns him to Aki as a junior partner, and the pair start with a fistfight on day one. Aki is disciplined and reserved, wears his hair in a topknot, smokes, and fights with a katana and a contract with the Fox Devil, whose giant head he summons to bite through enemies. He joined Public Safety with a personal grudge against the Gun Devil. Soon he is sharing his apartment with Denji and Power, and his weary efforts to keep that household in order fill much of the first season.

charlotte-265064b8-abef-46a5-a01f-fc929b.name: Charlotte
charlotte-265064b8-abef-46a5-a01f-fc929b.role: Princess of Albion, fourth in line to the throne, who works with a team of spies at Queen's Mayfair School
charlotte-265064b8-abef-46a5-a01f-fc929b.notes: Usually called "Princess". Princess Principal is an original anime, so there is no source chapter. Episodes air out of story order; episode 1 is "Case 13". Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
charlotte-265064b8-abef-46a5-a01f-fc929b.abilities: A princess of Albion, fourth in line to the throne, who works alongside a team of spies; her strengths are political skill, composure and resolve rather than combat.

fate.detail: Charlotte is alive at the end of the TV series and in the Crown Handler film chapters released so far.

charlotte-265064b8-abef-46a5-a01f-fc929b.about: Charlotte, usually called simply the Princess, belongs to the royal family of Albion, a steampunk kingdom whose capital has been split in two by a wall since a revolution, and she is fourth in line to the throne. She attends Queen's Mayfair School, where she secretly works with a small team of spies for Control, the intelligence agency of the rival Commonwealth. Poised, gracious and politically shrewd, she can seem dreamy or playful in conversation but rarely loses her composure. She knew the spy Ange when they were children, and she counts on Ange's help with a bold goal: to become queen herself and bring down the wall dividing the country.

chihiro-ogino.name: Chihiro Ogino
chihiro-ogino.role: Protagonist; ten-year-old girl who works in Yubaba's bathhouse to free her parents
chihiro-ogino.notes: Spirited Away is a 2001 film with an original story, so episode and source are null. She is called Sen for most of the film.
chihiro-ogino.abilities: An ordinary 10-year-old girl with no powers who shows courage, hard work and loyalty while working in the spirits' bathhouse.

fate.detail: Chihiro survives and returns to the human world with her parents at the end of the film.

chihiro-ogino.about: Chihiro Ogino is a sulky ten-year-old who spends the opening of Spirited Away slumped in the back seat, unhappy that her family is relocating. When her father takes a wrong turn, the family wanders through a tunnel into what looks like an abandoned theme park. Her parents help themselves to food left out on a stall and turn into pigs, and Chihiro finds herself stranded in a town of spirits at nightfall. A boy named Haku tells her that the only way to survive is to ask for work at the bathhouse run by the witch Yubaba, who takes away her name and calls her Sen. Her story follows a timid child slowly finding her own nerve.

claude-faustus.name: Claude Faustus
claude-faustus.role: Demon butler of the Trancy household, bound by contract to Alois Trancy
