claude-faustus.notes: Created for the Black Butler II anime; the wiki lists no manga debut. Black Butler II episode 1 is episode 25 overall. Arc name follows Alois Trancy's entry.
claude-faustus.abilities: A demon butler bound to Alois Trancy, flawless at household duties and a fighter on Sebastian's level who uses golden cutlery as weapons and spider-like threads.

fate.detail: In the Black Butler II finale (episode 12), Sebastian stabs him with the demon sword Laevatein during their duel, and he dies beside Hannah.

claude-faustus.about: Claude Faustus serves as butler to the Trancy household in Black Butler II and, like Sebastian Michaelis, a demon bound by contract to serve a young earl. His master is the spoiled, volatile Alois Trancy, and Claude performs every household duty without a single mistake while showing almost no emotion. Tall, with black hair, glasses and gold eyes, he speaks in a flat, measured tone and does not react even to Alois's most childish provocations. He fights with golden cutlery and threads like a spider's web, which earns him the name Spider Butler, and he is a close match for Sebastian in a fight. His cold, impassive manner makes him a sharp contrast to Sebastian.

emilia-3.name: Emilia
emilia-3.role: Main heroine; half-elf candidate in the royal selection for the throne of Lugunica

debut.episodeTitle: The End of the Beginning and the Beginning of the End

emilia-3.notes: Episode 1 is confirmed by both sources. Light novel volume 1 rests on the Re:Zero Wiki; Wikipedia gives her web novel debut in the prologue. Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
emilia-3.abilities: A half-elf spirit arts user who fights with ice magic, aided by her contracted great spirit, the cat Puck.

fate.detail: Emilia is alive in the anime (through season 3) and the ongoing light novels; she is killed in some of the timelines that Subaru erases with Return by Death, but those deaths are undone.

emilia-3.about: Emilia, a half-elf with long silver hair, is the girl Subaru Natsuki meets on his first day in another world, while she is chasing a thief through the capital of Lugunica. The stolen item is an insignia she needs as a candidate in the royal selection, the contest to choose the kingdom's next ruler. Many people distrust her on sight because half-elves are associated with a feared witch from legend, yet she helps strangers anyway and insists she is only doing it for selfish reasons. She fights with ice magic alongside Puck, a small cat-shaped spirit who lives in a crystal she wears. Subaru, smitten at once, resolves to protect her, and that promise drives the story.

erina-nakiri.name: Erina Nakiri
erina-nakiri.role: Granddaughter of Totsuki Culinary Academy's dean, known for her "God Tongue"
erina-nakiri.notes: Episode 2 is her full introduction (confirmed by both sources); the wiki also lists a cameo in episode 1 and chapter 1. Chapter 2 and the Elite Ten seat rest on the Food Wars! Wiki only. Other relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
erina-nakiri.abilities: She has the 'God Tongue', a palate so refined it detects every flaw in a dish, and is a prodigy chef and member of Totsuki's Elite Ten.

fate.detail: Erina is alive at the end of the manga and anime (Food Wars! The Fifth Plate, 2020).

erina-nakiri.about: Erina Nakiri is a first-year at Totsuki Culinary Academy, Japan's most exclusive cooking school, and the granddaughter of its dean, Senzaemon Nakiri. She has the God Tongue, a palate so precise that it detects every flaw in a dish, and she is already a member of the Elite Ten Council, the group of students who run the school's affairs. Proud, regal and quick to dismiss anything she considers common, she fails Souma Yukihira's transfer exam by refusing to admit she enjoyed his dish. She treats his diner-style cooking with open contempt from then on. Their prickly rivalry, and her reliance on her devoted aide Hisako Arato, shape much of the series.

finnian.name: Finnian
finnian.role: Gardener of the Phantomhive household with superhuman strength
finnian.notes: Usually called Finny. Chapter 1 per the wiki; Wikipedia confirms he appears in the first manga volume.
finnian.abilities: The Phantomhive gardener, a clumsy-seeming boy with monstrous superhuman strength, the result of experiments done on him, who helps defend the manor.

fate.detail: Finnian is alive in the anime and in the ongoing manga (as of November 2026).

finnian.about: Finnian, usually called Finny, is the gardener at the Phantomhive manor and part of its chaotic staff alongside the chef Bardroy, the maid Mey-Rin and the elderly steward Tanaka. He is cheerful, sweet-natured and endlessly enthusiastic, with strawberry-blond hair pinned back by red clips, but nearly every job he attempts ends in disaster, from flattening hedges to killing the lawn with the wrong spray. The butler Sebastian is constantly cleaning up after him. What sets Finny apart from an ordinary comic servant is his freakish physical strength, which lets him lift objects far heavier than he is. That mix of innocence and raw power defines him.

finral-roulacase.name: Finral Roulacase
finral-roulacase.role: Black Bulls Magic Knight who uses Spatial Magic for transport
arcs: Eye of the Midnight Sun Encounter
finral-roulacase.notes: Episode 4 and chapter 2 rest on the Black Clover Wiki; the Wikipedia summary of episode 4 does not name him. Arcs follow mentions in his wiki biography.
finral-roulacase.abilities: A Black Bulls spatial mage whose Spatial Magic opens portals for instant travel, making him the squad's transport and escape route.

fate.detail: Finral is alive in the anime and in the ongoing manga (as of November 2026).

finral-roulacase.about: Finral Roulacase is a member of the Black Bulls, the most unruly squad of the Clover Kingdom's Magic Knights, and a nobleman of House Vaude. His Spatial Magic opens portals between places, which makes him the squad's driver: he carries members to missions and whisks them out of danger in an instant. He has little in the way of attack magic and gets nervous when a fight turns serious. Finral is a cheerful, self-confessed flirt who tries, and nearly always fails, to charm any woman he meets. Beneath the jokes he is protective of his teammates, and his portals often turn a hopeless situation into a successful retreat.

genos.name: Genos
genos.role: Cyborg hero who becomes Saitama's disciple
genos.notes: Episode 2 is his first full appearance (confirmed by both sources); the wiki also lists a brief appearance at the end of episode 1. Chapter 5 of the Murata manga rests on the One Punch Man Wiki only.
genos.abilities: A teenage cyborg and Saitama's self-declared disciple who fights with incineration cannons in his arms and constantly upgraded parts.

fate.detail: Genos is alive in the anime and the ongoing manga (as of November 2026); his body is wrecked in many fights, but Dr. Kuseno rebuilds him each time.

genos.about: Genos is a nineteen-year-old cyborg who first appears battling a swarm of monster mosquitoes, only to have the fight ended for him by Saitama, a bald hero who wins with a single punch. Stunned, Genos begs to become Saitama's disciple and starts following him everywhere, studying his teacher's every habit in search of the secret behind that strength. He was rebuilt by the scientist Dr. Kuseno and is hunting a rogue cyborg who destroyed his hometown. He is earnest, intense and humourless, prone to long speeches that Saitama asks him to cut down to twenty words or less. Much of his comedy comes from how seriously he takes everything.

gon-freecss.name: Gon Freecss
gon-freecss.role: Protagonist; boy who sets out to become a Hunter and find his father
gon-freecss.abilities: A boy raised on Whale Island with keen animal-like senses, huge stamina and agility; at the start he fights with a fishing rod.

fate.detail: Gon survives: his forced transformation against Neferpitou in the Chimera Ant arc leaves him near death, Alluka heals him in the Election arc, and he loses access to Nen.

gon-freecss.about: Gon Freecss is a twelve-year-old from Whale Island who has grown up fishing and exploring the forests, raised by his relative Mito. He discovers that his father, Ging, whom he had never known, is alive and a renowned Hunter who left to pursue his work, and Gon resolves to pass the dangerous Hunter Exam to follow his path and find him. Cheerful, honest and almost reckless in his determination, he has sharp, animal-like senses and fights with a fishing rod. During the exam he befriends Kurapika, Leorio Paradinight and, most closely, Killua Zoldyck, a boy from a family of assassins. His simple, stubborn honesty drives the adventure.

gray-fullbuster.name: Gray Fullbuster
gray-fullbuster.role: Ice-Make wizard of the Fairy Tail guild and member of Team Natsu
gray-fullbuster.notes: Episode 2 and chapter 2 rest on the Fairy Tail Wiki; the Wikipedia summary of episode 2 does not name him. Debut is in the 2009 series. Arc names follow the wiki synopsis. Other relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
gray-fullbuster.abilities: A Fairy Tail wizard who uses Ice-Make magic to shape ice into weapons and shields, and has a habit of stripping off his clothes without noticing.

fate.detail: Gray is killed shielding Juvia during the dragon attack at the end of the Grand Magic Games arc, but Ultear's time-reversal spell, Last Ages, undoes his death; he is alive at the end of Fairy Tail.

gray-fullbuster.about: Gray Fullbuster is an ice wizard of the Fairy Tail guild whose Ice-Make magic lets him shape ice into weapons, walls and bridges in seconds. He wears the guild's mark on his chest, which is often on display because he has a habit of stripping off his clothes without noticing, much to the embarrassment of whoever is nearby. Cool-headed and sarcastic, he is a long-standing rival of the fire wizard Natsu Dragneel, and the two pick fights over anything. Even so, Gray readily joins Natsu, Lucy and Erza on their missions and becomes one of the core members of the team. His dry calm makes a good foil for Natsu's recklessness.

haku-e244892b-b626-4c5f-a509-b7c600052bf.name: Haku
haku-e244892b-b626-4c5f-a509-b7c600052bf.role: Boy at the witch Yubaba's bathhouse who helps Chihiro after she enters the spirit world
haku-e244892b-b626-4c5f-a509-b7c600052bf.notes: Spirited Away is a film, so episode is null; it is an original Studio Ghibli story with no manga or light novel source. His true identity is left out to avoid spoilers.
haku-e244892b-b626-4c5f-a509-b7c600052bf.abilities: Yubaba's apprentice, a boy who uses magic and can transform into a white dragon.

fate.detail: Haku is alive at the end of the film after Chihiro helps him remember his true name.

haku-e244892b-b626-4c5f-a509-b7c600052bf.about: Haku is a boy with a neat bob haircut and a calm, serious manner who serves as apprentice to the witch Yubaba at the spirit world's bathhouse. He is the first to help Chihiro Ogino after she wanders into that world and finds her parents under a spell, warning her to leave before nightfall and then explaining how to survive: ask for work at the bathhouse and never forget her name. Haku is unusually kind to Chihiro, though Yubaba has taken his own real name and he can no longer remember it. Gentle with Chihiro but cold and obedient when serving Yubaba, he runs errands for the witch that he never explains.

heen.name: Heen
heen.notes: Howl's Moving Castle is a film, so episode is null; it adapts Diana Wynne Jones's prose novel, so source is null. The Ghibli Wiki notes he was created for the film and does not appear in the novel.
heen.abilities: Madame Suliman's wheezing old dog, sent as a spy, who later loyally helps Sophie and her companions.

fate.detail: Heen survives the film and stays with Sophie's household at the end.

heen.about: Heen is the elderly, wheezing dog who serves Madame Suliman, the king's chief sorceress in Howl's Moving Castle. He was created for the film and does not appear in Diana Wynne Jones's novel. Heen turns up when Sophie travels to the royal palace to speak to Suliman on Howl's behalf; seeing an odd dog trailing after her, Sophie wonders whether it might be Howl in disguise. He makes a short, breathy 'hin' sound in place of a bark, moves slowly, and is so heavy that Sophie ends up hauling him up the palace's long staircase. Though Suliman uses him to keep watch, he ends up attaching himself to Sophie, which makes him a small, quietly funny presence in the film.

hero-6e47f7e6-abaf-453a-9b48-41ec706bdb9.name: Ren Amamiya
hero-6e47f7e6-abaf-453a-9b48-41ec706bdb9.role: Protagonist; transfer student at Shujin Academy who leads the Phantom Thieves of Hearts as Joker

debut.episodeTitle: I Am Thou, Thou Art I

hero-6e47f7e6-abaf-453a-9b48-41ec706bdb9.notes: He is the protagonist of the video game Persona 5, so source is null; the name Ren Amamiya is the one used in the anime. Episode 1 rests on the Wikipedia episode summary. A separate TV special, The Day Breakers, aired in 2016 before the series.
hero-6e47f7e6-abaf-453a-9b48-41ec706bdb9.abilities: A transfer student who awakens the Persona Arsène and leads the Phantom Thieves of Hearts; unlike his friends, he can switch between multiple Personas.

fate.detail: Ren survives the series; Akechi's attempt to kill him in the interrogation room is foiled by the Phantom Thieves' plan, so his death is only faked.

hero-6e47f7e6-abaf-453a-9b48-41ec706bdb9.about: Ren Amamiya is a high school student sent to Tokyo on probation after a conviction for assault; he stepped in when a man was harassing a woman, and the man pressed charges. He transfers to Shujin Academy, where rumours of his record make him an outcast, and lodges at Café Leblanc under the eye of its owner, Sojiro Sakura. When a strange phone app pulls him into the Metaverse, a world shaped by people's twisted desires, he awakens the Persona Arsène. With Ryuji Sakamoto, Ann Takamaki and the talking cat Morgana he forms the Phantom Thieves of Hearts, taking the codename Joker. Quiet and composed, he hides a rebellious streak.

hinami-fueguchi.name: Hinami Fueguchi
hinami-fueguchi.role: Young ghoul who comes to the 20th Ward with her mother and grows close to Ken Kaneki at Anteiku
hinami-fueguchi.notes: Episode 3 and chapter 10 debut rest on the Tokyo Ghoul Wiki; the Wikipedia summary of episode 3 does not name her. Wikipedia mentions her mother and father; their names rest on the wiki. Arc names follow the wiki's plot sections; the last four are in Tokyo Ghoul:re.
hinami-fueguchi.abilities: A young ghoul with an exceptionally keen sense of smell, even for a ghoul; she starts out sheltered and unwilling to fight.

fate.detail: Hinami survives to the end of Tokyo Ghoul:re.

hinami-fueguchi.about: Hinami Fueguchi is a shy young ghoul who comes to Tokyo's 20th Ward with her mother, Ryouko, hoping the staff of the Anteiku café can help them stay safe. She is gentle and timid, and very unlike the violent ghouls Ken Kaneki has met so far. Because she cannot go to school, she loves books and sets out to learn kanji, and Kaneki happily becomes her reading tutor. She is also known for a sense of smell sharp even by ghoul standards. Through her and Ryouko, the first season shows ordinary ghoul families who simply want to live quietly while investigators hunt them. Hinami's innocence makes the show's moral questions feel personal.

hisashi-igou.name: Hisashi Igou
hisashi-igou.role: Fujimi High School student; Takashi Komuro's best friend and Rei Miyamoto's boyfriend
hisashi-igou.notes: Wikipedia spells his surname Igo. Episode 1 rests on the Wikipedia episode summary; the wiki gives no episode. Manga chapter not confirmed.
hisashi-igou.abilities: An athletic Fujimi High student, loyal to his best friend Takashi and his girlfriend Rei.

fate.detail: Bitten by one of 'them' in the first episode ('Spring of the DEAD'), he dies of the infection before Takashi can kill him and turns into one of the undead.

hisashi-igou.about: Hisashi Igou attends Fujimi High School, where he is Takashi Komuro's best friend and is dating Rei Miyamoto, the girl Takashi has known since childhood. Calm, athletic and decisive, he comes across as the natural leader in a crisis. When people at the school suddenly start attacking others like the walking dead, Hisashi is among the very first to react, helping Takashi and Rei escape from the classroom. He is also credited as the first to call the attackers 'them', the name the survivors keep using. His bond with Rei, and Takashi's lingering feelings for her, set up the emotional tension of the opening chapters.

hiyori-iki.name: Hiyori Iki
hiyori-iki.role: Middle school girl who becomes a half-phantom after saving Yato from a bus accident

debut.episodeTitle: A Housecat, a Stray God, and a Tail

hiyori-iki.notes: Episode 1 is confirmed by both sources. Chapter 2 rests on the Noragami Wiki only. Relatives are listed only on the wiki, so they are left out.
hiyori-iki.abilities: After an accident she becomes a half-phantom whose soul can leave her body, letting her move with great agility and see gods and phantoms; she also practises kick-heavy fighting.

fate.detail: Hiyori is alive at the end of the Noragami manga (concluded 2023) and in the anime.

hiyori-iki.about: Hiyori Iki is a middle school girl from a well-off family who spends her free time watching martial arts and copying her favourite fighter's kicks. One day she leaps to push a scruffy stranger in a tracksuit out of the path of a bus. The stranger is Yato, a little-known god, and the accident leaves her a half-phantom: whenever she dozes off, her spirit slips out of her body, trailing a tail-like cord that ties it to her. Hiyori tracks Yato down to make him fix her, paying his five-yen fee, and ends up tangled in the world of gods and phantoms. She is kind, practical and willing to tell a god he is being petty.

howl.name: Howl
howl.role: Wizard whose moving castle Sophie enters; he dodges the king's summons to fight in the war
howl.notes: Howl's Moving Castle is a film, so episode is null; it adapts Diana Wynne Jones's prose novel, so source is null. Wikipedia notes he uses the aliases Jenkins and Pendragon.
howl.abilities: A powerful, vain wizard who lives in a walking castle, goes by several aliases, and can transform into a bird-like creature.

fate.detail: Howl survives the film; Sophie returns his heart and he lives on with her.

howl.about: Howl is a vain, flamboyant wizard whose giant walking castle roams the hills around the town of Market Chipping. Rumour says he steals the hearts of pretty young women, so townsfolk treat him with dread. In person he is charming, theatrical and often childish, fussing endlessly over his hair and sulking dramatically when things go wrong. Sophie, a young hatmaker cursed into the body of an old woman, meets him by chance and later moves into the castle as its self-appointed cleaning lady. Howl lives there with his young apprentice Markl and the fire demon Calcifer, using several names to dodge the king's demands that he serve in the war.

izuku-midoriya.name: Izuku Midoriya
izuku-midoriya.role: Protagonist; U.A. High School student training to become a Pro Hero
izuku-midoriya.abilities: A born-Quirkless boy who inherits All Might's One For All, a power so strong it breaks his own bones at first; he is also an analytical hero nerd who studies other Quirks.

fate.detail: Deku survives the Final War and the series; the manga's ending (chapter 430) shows him losing One For All, teaching at U.A., and eight years later returning to hero work in a powered suit.

izuku-midoriya.about: Izuku Midoriya is a fourteen-year-old who wants more than anything to be a hero in a society where most people are born with a superpower called a Quirk, but he was born without one. He fills notebooks with analysis of every hero he sees, idolises All Might, and puts up with constant scorn from his childhood friend Katsuki Bakugo, who calls him Deku. When he runs headlong to help Bakugo against a villain despite having no power at all, All Might sees in him the instincts of a true hero and offers to pass on his Quirk. Izuku's tearful, stubborn determination and habit of thinking out loud define his early story.

jibril.name: Jibril
jibril.role: Flügel who lives in Elkia's library and serves Sora and Shiro after losing a game to them
jibril.notes: Light novel debut is volume 2 (the wiki, and Wikipedia cites volume 2 for her introduction). Episode 5 is her first full appearance; the wiki also lists a cameo in episode 1.
jibril.abilities: A Flügel, one of a warlike angelic race; she has immense magical power, can teleport, and is obsessed with collecting knowledge and books.

fate.detail: Jibril is alive in the anime and the ongoing light novels.

jibril.about: Jibril is a Flügel, a member of an angel-like race created long ago as weapons in a war between gods, and she is the youngest of her kind. She left the Flügel's floating homeland, won the national library of Elkia, the last human kingdom, from its former king in a game, and has lived among its books ever since. Polite, eloquent and obsessed with knowledge, she will wager almost anything for a book she has not yet read. When the gamer siblings Sora and Shiro challenge her to a word-chain game with the library at stake, she loses and, as agreed, pledges herself to their service. She takes to the role with obvious relish.

jonathan-joestar.name: Jonathan Joestar
jonathan-joestar.role: Protagonist of Part 1, Phantom Blood; son of the Joestar family who becomes rivals with his adoptive brother Dio Brando
jonathan-joestar.notes: Descendants are left out to avoid spoilers.
jonathan-joestar.abilities: A strong, gentlemanly rugby player who learns Hamon (the Ripple), a breathing technique that channels sunlight energy to destroy vampires and zombies.

fate.detail: At the end of Part 1, Phantom Blood (1889; anime episode 9), Jonathan dies of a wound from Dio's severed head on his honeymoon ship, using his last Ripple to save Erina.

jonathan-joestar.about: Jonathan Joestar, nicknamed JoJo, is the gentle, well-meaning son of a wealthy English nobleman in the late nineteenth century. His life changes when his father takes in Dio Brando, the son of a man who once claimed to have saved the family, and Dio immediately sets out to humiliate and isolate him, from turning his friends against him to cruelly targeting his dog. Jonathan grows into a large, strong young man who plays rugby, studies archaeology and holds himself to the standards of a true gentleman. Phantom Blood, his part of the saga, is built on the rivalry between the brothers, with Jonathan's patient decency set squarely against Dio's cruelty and ambition.

jujutsu-kaisen-nobara-kugisaki.name: Nobara Kugisaki
jujutsu-kaisen-nobara-kugisaki.role: First-year student at Tokyo Jujutsu High alongside Yuji Itadori and Megumi Fushiguro
jujutsu-kaisen-nobara-kugisaki.notes: Chapter 3 is confirmed by both sources (the wiki also notes she is on the chapter 1 cover). Episode 2 rests on the Jujutsu Kaisen Wiki; the Wikipedia summaries first name her in episode 3.
jujutsu-kaisen-nobara-kugisaki.abilities: A first-year sorcerer who uses the Straw Doll Technique, hammering cursed nails with her hammer and using Resonance to strike enemies through a straw doll.

fate.detail: Mahito's Idle Transfiguration hits her face in the Shibuya Incident (manga chapter 125; anime season 2), leaving her fate unknown for years; she returns alive, missing her left eye, in chapter 253 (2024) and is alive at the series' end (chapter 271).

jujutsu-kaisen-nobara-kugisaki.about: Nobara Kugisaki joins Tokyo Jujutsu High as a first-year after moving to the capital from a small country town she was eager to leave behind. Under their teacher, Satoru Gojo, she trains with Yuji Itadori and Megumi Fushiguro. Brash, confident and fashion-conscious, she says what she thinks, refuses to shrink herself for anyone, and is quick to call out people who look down on her. She fights curses with the Straw Doll Technique, hammering cursed nails into her targets, and with Resonance, which lets her strike an enemy through a straw doll linked to a piece of them. Her bluntness and nerve set the tone for much of the trio's banter.

jujutsu-kaisen-yuji-itadori.name: Yuji Itadori
jujutsu-kaisen-yuji-itadori.role: Protagonist; high schooler who becomes the vessel of Ryomen Sukuna and joins Tokyo Jujutsu High
jujutsu-kaisen-yuji-itadori.notes: Other relatives are left out to avoid spoilers.
jujutsu-kaisen-yuji-itadori.abilities: A boy with superhuman physical strength and speed who becomes the vessel of the curse Sukuna after eating one of his fingers, and fights with powerful cursed-energy punches.

fate.detail: Yuji dies in the Cursed Womb arc (anime episode 5) when Sukuna tears out his heart, but Sukuna revives him; he survives to the manga's ending (chapter 271, 2024).

jujutsu-kaisen-yuji-itadori.about: Yuji Itadori is a high schooler in Sendai with absurd physical ability, the kind of student who can throw a shot put across the field yet spends his afternoons in the Occult Research Club because it lets him leave early to visit his grandfather. His grandfather urges him to help other people and to die surrounded by them, advice Yuji takes to heart. When his clubmates unseal a cursed relic and draw out monsters, Yuji swallows the object, a rotting finger of the demon Ryomen Sukuna, to protect everyone. He survives as Sukuna's host and is enrolled at Tokyo Jujutsu High under Satoru Gojo. His cheerful, plainspoken decency anchors the series.

juliet-persia.name: Juliet Persia
juliet-persia.role: Female lead; first-year leader of the White Cat Dormitory at Dahlia Academy
juliet-persia.notes: Chapter 1 per the wiki; Wikipedia confirms she is on the volume 1 cover. Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
juliet-persia.abilities: Leader of the White Cats first-years (West Rhombus) at Dahlia Academy, a skilled swordswoman and fighter who wants to end the rivalry between the two dorms.

fate.detail: Juliet is alive at the end of the manga; the series is a romantic comedy with no character deaths.

juliet-persia.about: Juliet Persia is a first-year at Dahlia Academy, a boarding school shared by students from two feuding countries, and she leads the first-years of the White Cat dormitory, home to students from the Principality of West. Her family is a noble house that cannot pass its title to a daughter, and as its only child she has trained relentlessly to prove she is every bit as capable as a man, and she is a formidable fencer. Proud and stern in public, she is privately kind and somewhat sheltered. Her sworn rival is Romio Inuzuka, leader of the Black Dog first-years, who has loved her for years; after he confesses, the two begin a relationship both dorms must never discover.

justin.name: Turnip Head
justin.role: Enchanted living scarecrow who leads Sophie to Howl's castle
justin.notes: Howl's Moving Castle is a film, so episode is null; it adapts Diana Wynne Jones's prose novel, so source is null. His true identity is left out to avoid spoilers.
justin.abilities: A silent, hopping scarecrow with a turnip head who is cursed; despite having no voice, he guides and helps Sophie on her journey.

fate.detail: He survives; Sophie's kiss breaks his curse at the end of the film, revealing him as Prince Justin of the neighbouring kingdom.

justin.about: Turnip Head is a scarecrow whose head is a large turnip with a painted grin, and who stands on a single wooden pole. Sophie Hatter finds him stuck upside down in a bush while she trudges into the hills, newly cursed into the body of an old woman, and she pulls him free. From then on he hops after her in silence, fetches her a walking stick, and leads her to Howl's moving castle when she needs shelter for the night. Sophie is wary of him at first and tries to send him away, but he keeps turning up when she needs help. He never says a word, so his bouncing loyalty does the talking.

kaede-kayano.name: Kaede Kayano
kaede-kayano.role: Student of Class 3-E at Kunugigaoka Junior High School and close friend of Nagisa Shiota
kaede-kayano.notes: Episode 1 is confirmed by both sources. Chapter 1 rests on the wiki only. She also appears in the earlier Jump Festa event anime (both sources list its voice actress). Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
kaede-kayano.abilities: A cheerful Class 3-E student who loves sweets and gives Koro-sensei his name; she starts out looking like an ordinary member of the class.

fate.detail: In the final battle she is impaled through the chest by the second Reaper while protecting Koro-sensei; he preserves her blood and cells, rebuilds the damage and restarts her heart, bringing her back to life (anime season 2), and she survives the series.

kaede-kayano.about: Kaede Kayano belongs to Class 3-E at Kunugigaoka Junior High, the school's lowest-ranked class, which has been handed an odd assignment: assassinate its new teacher, a yellow, tentacled creature who has vowed to destroy the Earth within a year. Bright, chatty and easygoing, she quickly becomes one of Nagisa Shiota's closest friends. She is the one who names their teacher Koro-sensei, a pun on the Japanese for a teacher who cannot be killed. Kayano loves sweets, pudding above all, is touchy about her small figure, and is not particularly athletic. She often helps Nagisa compile notes on Koro-sensei's weaknesses.

kaori-miyazono.name: Kaori Miyazono
kaori-miyazono.role: Violinist who pushes Kousei Arima to return to performing
kaori-miyazono.notes: Chapter 1 ("Monotone") per the wiki; Wikipedia confirms she is on the volume 1 cover. Relatives are listed only on the wiki, so they are left out.
kaori-miyazono.abilities: A free-spirited violinist who ignores the score to play with bold, emotional expression that wins audiences over.

fate.detail: Kaori dies during a risky operation for her illness while Kousei plays in the Eastern Japan Piano Competition finals (final episode 22; end of the manga).

kaori-miyazono.about: Kaori Miyazono is a fourteen-year-old violinist who bursts into Kousei Arima's grey routine one April. She is in Tsubaki's class and asks her to introduce her to Kousei's friend Watari, so Kousei first meets her as a bright, blunt girl playing a melodica with children in a park. Kaori is impulsive, loud and quick to hit or kick, and she eats enormous amounts of sweets. On stage she plays with total freedom, ignoring the score in ways that irritate judges but move audiences. After learning who Kousei used to be, she drafts him as her accompanist and refuses to let him hide from music. Her energy is what sets the story in motion.

katsuki-bakugou.name: Katsuki Bakugou
katsuki-bakugou.role: Izuku Midoriya's childhood friend and rival; student in U.A. High School's Class 1-A
katsuki-bakugou.notes: Chapter 1 is confirmed by both sources. Episode 1 rests on the My Hero Academia Wiki; the Wikipedia summary of episode 1 does not name him.
katsuki-bakugou.abilities: His Quirk, Explosion, ignites the nitroglycerin-like sweat from his palms, giving him blasts for attacks and mobility; he is also a combat prodigy with sharp instincts.

fate.detail: In the final war Shigaraki bursts his heart and he dies briefly, but Edgeshot repairs his heart and he is revived (manga, 2022; anime season 7, 2024); he survives the series.

katsuki-bakugou.about: Katsuki Bakugou has known Izuku Midoriya since early childhood. While Izuku was born without a Quirk, Bakugou grew up praised for his powerful one, Explosion, which ignites the nitroglycerin-like sweat from his palms. All that praise made him arrogant, aggressive and determined to come first at everything; he bullied Izuku for years and expects to become the greatest hero of all. He passes the entrance exam for U.A. High School, the country's top hero academy, and joins Class 1-A, where Izuku also ends up. Beneath his temper lie sharp combat instincts and genuine drive. His furious, competitive relationship with Izuku is one of the central threads of My Hero Academia.

kazu-ishi.name: Kazu Ishii
kazu-ishi.role: Fujimi student who stays with the school nurse Shizuka Marikawa and tries to protect her when the outbreak starts
kazu-ishi.notes: Both sources spell his surname Ishii (AniLumi lists him as Kazu Ishi). Debut episode and chapter not confirmed: neither source gives them, and the English Wikipedia episode summaries do not name him. Role confirmed by the Highschool of the Dead Wiki and the Japanese Wikipedia character list.

fate.detail: In the first episode (and the manga's opening), Kazu is bitten while fleeing the school, and Saeko Busujima kills him at his request before he can turn into one of Them.

kazu-ishi.about: Kazu Ishii is a nervous Fujimi Academy student who often helps the school nurse, Shizuka Marikawa, with errands such as carrying her supplies, and he is in her office when a sudden outbreak sends the infected, known as 'Them', through the campus. As the halls fill with the walking dead, Kazu helps her tend to injured students and then tries to get her safely out of the building, standing up to the attackers himself even though he is no fighter. His path then crosses that of Saeko Busujima, the kendo club captain. His brief scenes show an ordinary student trying to be brave in the disaster's first hours.

kenma-kozume.name: Kenma Kozume
kenma-kozume.role: Setter for Nekoma High's volleyball team
kenma-kozume.notes: Episode 11 is confirmed by both sources (the wiki titles it "Decision"). Chapter 24 ("Go, Team Karasuno!") rests on the Haikyuu!! Wiki only.
kenma-kozume.abilities: Nekoma's setter and the team's 'brain': calm, observant and quick to read opponents' habits and weaknesses, though not physically strong.

fate.detail: Kenma is alive at the end of the manga (chapter 402, 2020), running his own business and gaming career; Haikyu!! has no character deaths.

kenma-kozume.about: Kenma Kozume is the second-year setter for Nekoma High, a Tokyo volleyball team with a long-standing rivalry with Karasuno. Quiet and introverted, he would rather be playing video games, and he stays in volleyball largely because his childhood friend Tetsurou Kuroo, Nekoma's captain, keeps him involved. He avoids unnecessary effort and dislikes attention, but he notices everything: his teammates rely on him as the team's brain because he picks up opponents' habits and steers the game from the setter's position. Shouyou Hinata meets him by chance in Miyagi and the two get along before realising they are about to face each other in a practice match.

kirei-kotomine.name: Kirei Kotomine
kirei-kotomine.role: Priest chosen as a Master in the Fourth Holy Grail War
kirei-kotomine.notes: Episode 1 rests on the Wikipedia episode summary; the TYPE-MOON Wiki confirms his Fate/Zero role but gives no episode. Light novel chapter not confirmed. He first appeared in the Fate/stay night visual novel (2004), where he oversees the Fifth Holy Grail War. Other relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
kirei-kotomine.abilities: A former Church executor who fights with Black Keys (thrown blade-hilts) and Bajiquan martial arts, and is a skilled healer; he is a Master in the Fourth Holy Grail War.

fate.detail: Kiritsugu shoots him through the heart in their final duel (Fate/Zero episode 24), but the corrupted Grail revives him (episode 25); he then dies for good in all three routes of the sequel, Fate/stay night.

kirei-kotomine.about: Kirei Kotomine is a soft-spoken priest and former Church executor who finds himself chosen as a Master in the Fourth Holy Grail War, a secret battle between seven mages and their summoned heroes. His father, Risei, is the war's official overseer, and Kirei studies magecraft under Tokiomi Tohsaka, quietly working to help his teacher win while summoning the Servant Assassin. Outwardly he is disciplined and devout, a skilled fighter with thrown Black Keys and martial arts, yet he feels nothing in pursuits that satisfy other people and does not know what he truly wants. That emptiness draws his attention to Kiritsugu Emiya, a rival Master he senses may share it.

koma-enji.name: Enji Koma
koma-enji.role: Ghoul waiter at the Anteiku café
koma-enji.notes: Episode 3 and chapter 14 debut rest on the Tokyo Ghoul Wiki; the Wikipedia episode summaries do not name him.
koma-enji.abilities: A playful Anteiku waiter who, as a ghoul, is a strong hand-to-hand fighter able to hold his own against top CCG investigators.

fate.detail: Koma survives the Owl Suppression Operation and reappears alive in Tokyo Ghoul:re as a member of Goat (manga), but the anime cuts him from :re; the series wiki lists him as deceased without describing a death.

koma-enji.about: Enji Koma is a ghoul who works as a waiter at Anteiku, a coffee shop in Tokyo's 20th Ward that quietly serves as a refuge where ghouls look out for one another. Playful and talkative, he brews excellent coffee and likes to play the grand senior employee in front of newcomers such as Ken Kaneki, though his boasts are rarely taken seriously. He works alongside the calmer Kaya Irimi under the café's manager, Yoshimura. Easygoing as he seems, he is a capable fighter who can hold his own against experienced CCG investigators. He is one of the familiar faces who help make Anteiku feel like a home for Kaneki.

konata-izumi.name: Konata Izumi
konata-izumi.role: Protagonist; otaku high school girl at the centre of the Lucky Star friend group
konata-izumi.notes: Wikipedia confirms she is on the volume 1 cover. The manga is a four-panel strip, so no chapter number is given.
konata-izumi.abilities: An otaku with a gift for games and anime trivia who is also surprisingly athletic and skilled at martial arts, though she avoids clubs to play games.

fate.detail: Nobody dies in Lucky Star; Konata is alive throughout the anime and manga.

konata-izumi.about: Konata Izumi is a short high school girl with long blue hair and a stray sprouting lock who lives with her father, a novelist, in Saitama Prefecture. She is a devoted otaku who stays up all night with games and anime, then copies homework from her friend Kagami Hiiragi or crams the night before a test. She is athletic and quick but refuses to join a sports club because it would cut into her viewing schedule. Konata spends her days chatting with Kagami, Kagami's twin Tsukasa and the polite Miyuki Takara about everyday trivia, such as the right way to eat a chocolate cornet. Her lazy, teasing humour gives Lucky Star its voice.

koneko-toujou.name: Koneko Toujou
koneko-toujou.role: Rook of Rias Gremory's peerage; Kuoh Academy student in the Occult Research Club
koneko-toujou.notes: Episode 1 rests on the High School DxD Wiki episode page; the Wikipedia episode summaries first name her in episode 2. Light novel volume not confirmed.
koneko-toujou.abilities: A member of Rias Gremory's peerage with the Rook's monstrous strength and defence, fighting with her bare fists.

fate.detail: Koneko is alive in the anime (High School DxD Hero, 2018) and the light novels.

koneko-toujou.about: Koneko Toujou is a first-year at Kuoh Academy who belongs to the Occult Research Club, a club that secretly serves as the base of the devil Rias Gremory and her servants. Small, quiet and nearly expressionless, she speaks only when she must and is almost always snacking on sweets, and other students treat her as a kind of school mascot. In Rias's peerage she holds the position of Rook, which grants her tremendous strength and durability, and she fights with her fists. She has little patience for the lecherous Issei Hyoudou after he joins the club, and her flat, one-line put-downs aimed at him become a running joke.

kousei-arima.name: Kousei Arima
kousei-arima.role: Protagonist; former child piano prodigy who stopped playing after his mother died
kousei-arima.notes: Chapter 1 ("Monotone") per the wiki; Wikipedia confirms he is on the volume 1 cover.
kousei-arima.abilities: A former child prodigy pianist, nicknamed the 'human metronome' for his precise playing, who can no longer hear his own piano after his mother's death.

fate.detail: Kousei survives the series and keeps playing the piano.

kousei-arima.about: Kousei Arima was once a famous child pianist who won competitions across Japan and was dubbed the 'human metronome' for his exact, mechanical playing under his mother's strict coaching. After her death he froze mid-performance, found that he could no longer hear the notes he played, and quit. Now fourteen, he lives a muted life in which everything seems monochrome, spending time with his neighbour Tsubaki and his friend Watari. Then he meets Kaori Miyazono, a violinist whose playing breaks every rule, and she drags him back toward the stage as her accompanist. His story deals with grief, pressure and finding a reason to play again, often shown through colour.

krul-tepes.name: Krul Tepes
krul-tepes.role: Third Progenitor and vampire queen of Japan
krul-tepes.notes: Role is confirmed by both sources. Episode 1 and chapter 1 of the main Vampire Reign manga rest on the Seraph of the End Wiki; the Wikipedia summary of episode 1 does not name her. Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
krul-tepes.abilities: The vampire queen of Japan and a Third Progenitor, vastly stronger and faster than ordinary vampires.

fate.detail: The anime (2015) ends with her alive, but in the ongoing manga (chapter 138) she is devoured by Ferid Bathory after drinking Guren's blood and survives only as a consciousness trapped inside Ferid, where she vanishes in chapter 150.

krul-tepes.about: Krul Tepes, a Third Progenitor, is the queen of the vampires in Japan, ruling from the underground city of Sanguinem after a virus has wiped out most of the adult human population. She looks like a small girl, but she is far older and far stronger than ordinary vampires. Like most of her kind, she regards humans as livestock to be kept for their blood, and the human orphans held in her city are no exception. Calm, proud and calculating, she spends as much effort navigating the politics of the vampire nobility as she does dealing with humans. Her interest in the orphan Mikaela Hyakuya ties her closely to the main story.

leorio-paladiknight.name: Leorio Paradinight
leorio-paladiknight.role: Hunter Exam applicant who wants to become a doctor; friend of Gon, Killua and Kurapika
leorio-paladiknight.notes: Episode 1 is confirmed by both sources; chapter 2 rests on the Hunter x Hunter Wiki only. Arcs follow the wiki's plot sections.
leorio-paladiknight.abilities: A Hunter Exam candidate who wants to become a doctor; he is tough, loyal and quick-tempered, and fights with a knife and briefcase.

fate.detail: Leorio is alive in the 2011 anime and the manga so far (on hiatus as of November 2026).

leorio-paladiknight.about: Leorio Paradinight is a tall, suit-wearing teenager who looks a decade older than he is and sails to the Hunter Exam claiming he wants nothing but money. He soon admits the real reason: a close friend died of an illness that could have been treated, and Leorio wants to become a doctor who helps people who cannot pay. He becomes a travelling companion of Gon Freecss and Kurapika from the very start, though he and Kurapika bicker almost constantly. Leorio is hot-headed, loud and quick to throw a punch, but warm and loyal underneath, and he fights with a knife from his briefcase. He gives the group its most down-to-earth perspective.

levi.name: Levi Ackerman
levi.role: Survey Corps captain who leads the Special Operations Squad; called humanity's strongest soldier

debut.episodeTitle: The Night of the Closing Ceremony: Humanity's Comeback, Part 2

levi.notes: Episode 4 debut rests on the Attack on Titan Wiki; Wikipedia episode summaries first name him in episode 9. His manga debut is the 2010 side story "Captain Levi" rather than a numbered chapter (both sources), so chapter is null. Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
levi.abilities: Known as humanity's strongest soldier: captain of the Survey Corps' Special Operations Squad, unmatched with vertical maneuvering equipment and blades.

fate.detail: Levi survives the series, though he loses two fingers and an eye; the final chapter (139) and Final Chapters Special 2 show him in a wheelchair after the war.

levi.about: Levi is a captain in the Survey Corps and the leader of its elite Special Operations Squad, and he is widely called humanity's strongest soldier. Short, sharp-eyed and blunt to the point of rudeness, he comes across as cold and unapproachable, and he is fixated on cleanliness, demanding spotless rooms, gear and uniforms from his subordinates. Rumour says he came from the criminal underworld before joining the military. When the Survey Corps takes custody of Eren Yeager, Levi's squad is given the job of watching and protecting him. His skill with vertical maneuvering equipment and blades is unmatched, and for all his gruffness he takes the lives of his soldiers seriously.

lord-yupa.name: Lord Yupa
lord-yupa.role: Wandering swordsmaster of the Valley of the Wind and Nausicaä's teacher

debut.anime: Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind

lord-yupa.notes: Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind is a 1984 film, not a TV series, so episode is null. He also appears in Hayao Miyazaki's manga; chapter not confirmed.
lord-yupa.abilities: Known as the greatest swordsman in the Periphery, a wandering warrior and scholar who investigates the Sea of Corruption.

fate.detail: Yupa survives the 1984 film; in Miyazaki's manga, however, he dies sacrificing himself to protect Kushana from an attack.

lord-yupa.about: Lord Yupa is a travelling swordsman widely regarded as the finest in the land, a grey-bearded warrior and scholar who has spent years roaming the ruined world trying to learn what lies behind the Sea of Corruption, the poisonous forest spreading across it. He is an old friend of the people of the Valley and of their ailing king, Jhil, and a teacher figure to Nausicaä, the princess who shares his curiosity. Yupa returns to the valley at the start of the film, and a fox-squirrel rescued during his arrival becomes Nausicaä's companion, Teto. When anger drives Nausicaä to violence, he steps between her and her enemies and lets her blade pierce his arm to end the fight.

lucy-steel.name: Lucy Steel
lucy-steel.role: Fourteen-year-old wife of Steel Ball Run organizer Steven Steel

debut.anime: Steel Ball Run: JoJo no Kimyou na Bouken

lucy-steel.notes: Wikipedia lists her in the anime cast, but neither source gives an anime debut episode, so episode is null. Chapter 1 of Steel Ball Run rests on the JoJo Wiki only.
lucy-steel.abilities: The 14-year-old wife of race promoter Steven Steel; with no Stand or fighting skills at first, she relies on nerve and quick thinking.

fate.detail: Lucy survives the story; after the race she defeats the alternate Diego and returns safely to Steven (Steel Ball Run manga).

lucy-steel.about: Lucy Steel is the fourteen-year-old wife of Steven Steel, the showman who organises the Steel Ball Run, a horse race across North America. Young, gentle and devoted to her much older husband, she stays at his side as the race gets underway, attending its public events and following the news of each stage with him. She has no special powers or fighting skills, and she can come across as shy and nervous. Even so, she is intelligent, observant and far braver than she looks, and she acts quickly whenever she senses that someone she cares about may be in danger. She is one of the few major figures in the story who is not competing in the race.

mami-tomoe.name: Mami Tomoe
mami-tomoe.role: Veteran magical girl and third-year student who mentors Madoka and Sayaka

debut.episodeTitle: I First Met Her in a Dream... or Something.

mami-tomoe.notes: Episode title as in the Wikipedia episode list; her Wikipedia article renders it "As If I Met Her in My Dream...". Madoka Magica is an original anime (the manga adapts it), so there is no source chapter. Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
mami-tomoe.abilities: A veteran magical girl who fights with summoned muskets and her signature finishing attack, Tiro Finale.

fate.detail: The witch Charlotte bites off her head in episode 3; after Madoka's wish remakes the universe in episode 12 she exists again in the new world, and she returns in the Rebellion film.

mami-tomoe.about: Mami Tomoe is a third-year student at Mitakihara Middle School and an experienced magical girl who has been fighting witches alone for some time. She first appears rescuing Madoka Kaname and Sayaka Miki from a witch's nightmarish labyrinth, conjuring rows of flintlock muskets out of ribbons and finishing the fight with a giant cannon blast she calls Tiro Finale. Afterwards she invites the girls to her apartment for tea and cake and offers to let them follow her on patrols, so they can see what the work involves before agreeing to Kyubey's offer to make them magical girls. Elegant, warm and encouraging, she quickly becomes a big-sister mentor to both of them.

markl.name: Markl
markl.notes: Howl's Moving Castle is a 2004 film, so episode is null. The film is based on Diana Wynne Jones's novel (not a manga or light novel), so source is null.
markl.abilities: Howl's young apprentice, who looks after the castle's door and uses a cloak spell to look like an old man when dealing with customers.

fate.detail: Markl is alive at the end of the film.

markl.about: Markl is the young apprentice who lives in Howl's moving castle, an orphan boy who runs errands, does the shopping and answers the castle's magic door. When customers call asking for the wizard's services, Markl throws on a hooded cloak whose spell makes him look like a bearded old man which is one of the film's recurring comic touches. His magical training consists mostly of chores, but he takes the job seriously and is proud to serve Howl. Markl is wary of Sophie when she first turns up uninvited, yet he warms to her quickly once she starts cooking and cleaning, and the two soon become close friends.

mayoi-hachikuji.name: Mayoi Hachikuji
mayoi-hachikuji.role: Elementary school girl Koyomi Araragi meets while she is lost
mayoi-hachikuji.notes: Wikipedia titles episode 3 "Mayoi Mai Mai, Part One". Her story is part of the Bakemonogatari light novel; volume and chapter not confirmed. Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
mayoi-hachikuji.abilities: A ghost girl, the snail apparition that makes people lost on their way, and a quick-witted talker known for mangling Araragi's name.

fate.detail: Mayoi is already dead when introduced, the ghost of a girl killed in a traffic accident 11 years earlier; she passes on in Onimonogatari, then meets Araragi in hell (Owarimonogatari, Mayoi Hell) and returns to become the goddess of the North Shirahebi Shrine.

mayoi-hachikuji.about: Mayoi Hachikuji is a fifth-grader with twin pigtails and an oversized backpack whom Koyomi Araragi spots in a park on Mother's Day, staring at a map. She says she is trying to reach her mother's house, but every route the two of them take somehow loops back on itself, and the reason sits at the centre of the Mayoi Snail story. Mayoi is cheeky, quick and very good at banter: she bites Araragi when he gets too familiar, and she mangles his name into increasingly strange variations, then claims she simply stumbled over the word. That rapid, playful sparring with Araragi becomes a running feature of the wider Monogatari series.

mayuri-shiina.name: Mayuri Shiina
mayuri-shiina.role: Rintarou Okabe's childhood friend and Lab Member 002 of the Future Gadget Laboratory
mayuri-shiina.notes: Steins;Gate is adapted from a visual novel (not a manga or light novel), so source is null. The wiki gives episode 1 as "Prologue of the Beginning and the End -Turning Point-". Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
mayuri-shiina.abilities: Okabe's cheerful childhood friend and lab member, a skilled cosplay costume maker who works part-time at a maid cafe.

fate.detail: She dies again and again in the Alpha worldline from episode 12 onward no matter what Okabe changes, but he finally reaches the Steins;Gate worldline where she survives (episode 24).

mayuri-shiina.about: Mayuri Shiina is a sixteen-year-old high school student and Rintarou Okabe's childhood friend, as well as the second member of his Future Gadget Laboratory. Gentle, cheerful and a little spacey, she greets people in a sing-song voice, adores anything cute, and happily loses track of complicated science talk. She works part-time at the maid café MayQueen+Nyan² and sews elaborate cosplay costumes for herself and her friends. Mayuri hates arguments and tries to keep the peace whenever tempers flare in the lab. Okabe, who jokingly calls her his hostage, is fiercely protective of her, and their long friendship is one of the emotional anchors of the story.

mikuru-asahina.name: Mikuru Asahina
mikuru-asahina.role: Time traveler from the future who is pulled into the SOS Brigade

debut.episodeTitle: The Adventures of Mikuru Asahina Episode 00

mikuru-asahina.notes: Episode 1 follows the 2006 broadcast order, which opens with the SOS Brigade's film; the Wikipedia summary of the first episode in chronological order also names her. Light novel debut is the first novel, The Melancholy of Haruhi Suzumiya (both sources).
mikuru-asahina.abilities: A timid time traveller from the future who can travel back through time (with Kyon in tow), though she is forbidden to reveal most details about it.

fate.detail: Mikuru is alive throughout the anime and the light novels (the series has had no new volume since 2020).

mikuru-asahina.about: Mikuru Asahina is a shy, sweet-natured second-year at North High whom Haruhi Suzumiya drags out of the calligraphy club and into her new SOS Brigade, mostly because Haruhi has decided every club needs a cute mascot. From then on Mikuru is dressed up in bunny-girl and maid costumes, serves tea in the clubroom, and stars in the brigade's amateur film. She frightens easily and spends much of the first arc on the verge of tears, which makes Kyon feel protective of her. Before long she quietly tells Kyon she has travelled back in time from the future, though nearly every question he asks afterwards gets the same reply: that information is classified.

milly-ashford.name: Milly Ashford
milly-ashford.role: Student Council president of Ashford Academy and granddaughter of its superintendent

debut.anime: Code Geass: Lelouch of the Rebellion
debut.episodeTitle: The Day a New Demon was Born

milly-ashford.notes: Code Geass is an original anime, so there is no source chapter. Episode 1 rests on the Code Geass Wiki; the Wikipedia summary of episode 1 does not name her. Her grandfather's name comes from the wiki; Wikipedia describes him as the school superintendent.
milly-ashford.abilities: President of the Ashford Academy student council, a cheerful, outgoing organiser of school festivals and events.

fate.detail: Milly survives the series and becomes a newscaster by the end of R2.

milly-ashford.about: Milly Ashford is the president of the student council at Ashford Academy and the granddaughter of its superintendent, Ruben K. Ashford. Outgoing, playful and seemingly tireless, she dreams up elaborate school events, festivals and costume days on a whim, and loves roping the rest of the council, Lelouch Lamperouge included, into her schemes. She teases her friends constantly, the shy Shirley Fenette most of all, and is curious enough about Lelouch's secrets to set the entire student body chasing after a cat she thinks is carrying something of his. A year older than the others, she acts as the council's ringleader, and her energy makes the school scenes a bright counterweight to the war outside.

minori-kushieda.name: Minori Kushieda
minori-kushieda.role: Taiga Aisaka's best friend and Ryuuji Takasu's crush; captain of the girls' softball club
minori-kushieda.notes: The wiki gives chapter 1 of the first light novel; Wikipedia cites volume 1 for her introduction.
minori-kushieda.abilities: A hyperactive, endlessly cheerful girl who captains the girls' softball team and juggles several part-time jobs.

fate.detail: Nobody dies in Toradora!; Minori is alive at the end of the anime and light novels.

minori-kushieda.about: Minori Kushieda, often called Minorin, is Taiga Aisaka's best friend and the girl Ryuuji Takasu has secretly liked for some time. She is boundlessly energetic: she captains the girls' softball club, holds down several part-time jobs at once, and fills conversations with odd jokes and sudden bursts of enthusiasm. Ryuuji and Taiga agree to help each other with their crushes, so a large part of the early story is Ryuuji clumsily trying to get closer to Minori while she cheerfully bounces from one topic to the next. She is warm and fiercely loyal to Taiga, yet her constant brightness can make her hard to read, which is part of what makes her interesting.

mitsuha-miyamizu.name: Mitsuha Miyamizu
mitsuha-miyamizu.role: Female protagonist; high school girl in rural Itomori who swaps bodies with Taki Tachibana
mitsuha-miyamizu.notes: Kimi no Na wa. (Your Name) is a 2016 original film, so episode is null and source is null; Makoto Shinkai's tie-in novel came out a month before the film. Later relationships left out to avoid spoilers.
mitsuha-miyamizu.abilities: A shrine maiden from rural Itomori who performs her family's traditions, such as braid-weaving and making kuchikamizake, and who starts swapping bodies with Taki.

fate.detail: In the original timeline she is killed when a fragment of the comet destroys Itomori in 2013, but Taki's warning gets the town evacuated; she survives and meets him years later in Tokyo.

mitsuha-miyamizu.about: Mitsuha Miyamizu is a seventeen-year-old high school girl in Itomori, a small lakeside town in the mountains, where she lives with her grandmother Hitoha and her younger sister Yotsuha. As the elder daughter of the family shrine, she carries out traditional duties such as ritual dances, braiding cords and making kuchikamizake, rice wine prepared by chewing, which embarrasses her in front of classmates. Her father, the town's mayor, lives apart from the family. Tired of rural life, she shouts a wish to be reborn as a handsome Tokyo boy, and soon afterwards she starts waking up on some mornings in the body of Taki Tachibana, a Tokyo high school student, while he wakes up in hers.

miyoko-sahara.name: Miyoko Sahara
miyoko-sahara.role: Kind elementary school classmate who tried to befriend Shouko Nishimiya
miyoko-sahara.notes: There is no TV anime: Koe no Katachi (A Silent Voice) is a 2016 film, so episode is null. Chapter 1 rests on the Koe no Katachi Wiki only.
miyoko-sahara.abilities: A kind classmate who learns sign language to befriend Shouko, and later studies fashion design.

fate.detail: Miyoko is alive at the end of the film and manga.

miyoko-sahara.about: Miyoko Sahara is a classmate of Shouya Ishida and Shouko Nishimiya at their elementary school, introduced in the early part of A Silent Voice that follows Shouko's arrival as a deaf transfer student. While most of the class treats Shouko as a burden or a target, Miyoko is the one child who decides to learn sign language so the two of them can actually talk. That small act of kindness sets her apart and draws teasing from the rest of the class. Miyoko is gentle, nervous and easily hurt, but sincere in her wish to be a good friend. In a story about cruelty and regret, she stands for the simple kindness the others failed to show.

nagisa-shiota.name: Nagisa Shiota
nagisa-shiota.role: Protagonist and narrator; student of Class 3-E at Kunugigaoka Junior High School
nagisa-shiota.notes: Episode 1 is confirmed by both sources; chapter 1 rests on the wiki only.
nagisa-shiota.abilities: Small and easily overlooked, he keeps detailed notes on Koro-sensei's weaknesses and shows a hidden, unsettling talent for assassination.

fate.detail: Nagisa survives the series and becomes a teacher in the epilogue.

nagisa-shiota.about: Nagisa Shiota is the narrator of Assassination Classroom and a member of Class 3-E, the dead-end class at Kunugigaoka Junior High. When a yellow, tentacled creature that has blown away most of the Moon becomes their homeroom teacher and promises to destroy the Earth the following March, the class is tasked with killing him for an enormous reward. Small, soft-spoken and often mistaken for a girl, Nagisa looks like the least threatening person in the room. He keeps a notebook of their teacher's weaknesses and watches people closely. The adults around him soon notice that he can approach a target without anyone sensing a threat, an unsettling knack that grows as the school year continues.

nanachi.name: Nanachi
nanachi.role: Hollow (Narehate) living in the Abyss who helps Riko and Reg
nanachi.notes: Episode 10 is confirmed by both sources. Chapter 19 rests on the Made in Abyss Wiki only.
nanachi.abilities: A Narehate, transformed by the Abyss's curse yet clear-minded, with deep knowledge of the Abyss's creatures, plants and medicine, plus the ability to sense the curse's force field.

fate.detail: Nanachi is alive in the anime (two seasons and the Dawn of the Deep Soul film) and in the ongoing manga (as of November 2026).

nanachi.about: Nanachi is one of the Narehate, people reshaped by the Abyss's curse into a furry, rabbit-like creature, who lives in a hidden shelter deep inside the enormous pit. Unlike most Narehate, Nanachi kept a clear mind, along with expert knowledge of the Abyss's plants, creatures and medicine. They first appear when Riko is badly poisoned and Reg is desperate for help, and Nanachi steps in to treat her. Nanachi is dry, sarcastic and guarded, and gets embarrassed when people fuss over how soft their fur is, yet they quickly prove kind and protective. They also have a distinctive habit of punctuating sentences with a soft 'nnaa' sound.

nidaime-raikage.name: A (Second Raikage)
nidaime-raikage.role: Second Raikage of Kumogakure; former bodyguard of the First Raikage
nidaime-raikage.notes: Episode 269 and chapter 527 debut rest on Narutopedia; the Wikipedia summary of episode 269 mentions the Second Raikage in a flashback about the Gold and Silver Brothers. His service as the First Raikage's bodyguard rests on Narutopedia only.

fate.detail: He died before the series began; he appears only as a spirit, summoned from the Pure Land with the other dead Kage by Hagoromo Otsutsuki to help undo the Infinite Tsukuyomi at the end of the Fourth Shinobi World War.

nidaime-raikage.about: A is the Second Raikage, a former leader of Kumogakure, the Village Hidden in the Clouds, who appears in Naruto Shippuden through a flashback told during the Fourth Shinobi World War. Before taking office he served as a bodyguard to the First Raikage. As Raikage he worked to build peace with the other hidden villages and agreed to a formal alliance with Konohagakure, negotiated with the Second Hokage, Tobirama Senju. That ceremony was thrown into chaos when Kinkaku and Ginkaku, the Gold and Silver Brothers from his own village, launched a coup and ambushed both leaders. The episode explains the long, tangled history between the two villages and the brothers' notoriety.

noelle-silva.name: Noelle Silva
noelle-silva.role: Royal of House Silva and Water Magic user in the Black Bulls squad
noelle-silva.notes: Chapter 4 ("The Black Bulls") is confirmed by both sources. Episode 4 rests on the Black Clover Wiki; the Wikipedia summary of episode 4 does not name her.
noelle-silva.abilities: A royal of House Silva with enormous mana and water magic that she at first cannot control; her first controlled spell is the protective water sphere Sea Dragon's Nest.

fate.detail: Noelle is alive in the anime and in the manga's ongoing final arc (as of November 2026).

noelle-silva.about: Noelle Silva comes from House Silva, a royal house of the Clover Kingdom, and she joins the Black Bulls squad on the same day as Asta. She has enormous reserves of mana but cannot control her water magic, and her spells tend to fly off in the wrong direction, often straight at her teammates. Her siblings treat her as a disgrace for it, which is why she ends up in the Black Bulls, the squad for misfits. Noelle covers her insecurity with haughty royal pride and sharp, embarrassed remarks, especially toward Asta, but she works hard to gain control. Her first real success, the protective Sea Dragon's Nest, marks an early turning point.

ochako-uraraka.name: Ochaco Uraraka
ochako-uraraka.role: Student in U.A. High School's Class 1-A; hero name Uravity
ochako-uraraka.notes: Chapter 3 ("Entrance Exam") is confirmed by both sources. Episode 3 rests on the My Hero Academia Wiki; the Wikipedia summary of episode 3 does not name her.
ochako-uraraka.abilities: Her Quirk, Zero Gravity, makes anything she touches with her fingertip pads weightless, though overusing it makes her nauseous.

fate.detail: Uraraka survives the final war against Toga and is alive at the series' end (manga final chapter 430, 2024).

ochako-uraraka.about: Ochaco Uraraka is a first-year at U.A. High School, the country's leading academy for heroes, and a member of its Class 1-A. She meets Izuku Midoriya at the entrance exam, where she stops him from falling with her Quirk, Zero Gravity, which makes anything she touches with the pads of her fingertips float; overusing it leaves her dizzy and nauseous. Cheerful, upbeat and sometimes blunt without realising it, she quickly becomes one of Izuku's closest friends and starts calling him 'Deku' as a term of encouragement rather than an insult. She openly admits she wants to become a pro hero to earn money for her parents, who run a struggling construction company.

phosphophyllite.name: Phosphophyllite
phosphophyllite.role: Protagonist; youngest of the Lustrous, assigned to compile a natural history encyclopedia
phosphophyllite.notes: Chapter 1 per the wiki; Wikipedia confirms Phos is on the volume 1 cover.
phosphophyllite.abilities: The youngest and most fragile gem, too brittle to fight, who is given the task of compiling a natural history encyclopedia.

fate.detail: As an immortal gem Phos never simply dies: in the manga's ending (2024) Phos becomes a god-like being who prays the other gems and Lunarians away and, after the sun swallows the Earth, lives on only as a small gem shard; the anime (2017) ends long before this.

phosphophyllite.about: Phosphophyllite, called Phos, is the youngest of the Lustrous, a family of living gem people who protect their island from the Lunarians, raiders who come from the Moon to shatter and steal them. At about three hundred years old, Phos is pale mint-green, cheerful, talkative and lazy, and so brittle that they cannot fight or even manage simple chores without breaking. Their teacher, the monk-like Kongo, gives Phos the job of writing an encyclopedia of natural history, which Phos sees as a consolation prize. While looking for something more useful to do, Phos meets the isolated, poisonous gem Cinnabar and promises to find them a better job, starting a story about worth.

rei-kiriyama.name: Rei Kiriyama
rei-kiriyama.role: Protagonist; teenage professional shogi player who lives alone

debut.episodeTitle: Rei Kiriyama / The Town Along the River

rei-kiriyama.notes: Episode 1 has two segments; both titles are given. Chapter 1 per the wiki; Wikipedia confirms he is on the volume 1 cover. Other relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
rei-kiriyama.abilities: A 17-year-old professional shogi player, one of the few ever to turn pro in middle school.

fate.detail: Rei is alive in the anime and in the ongoing manga (as of November 2026).

rei-kiriyama.about: Rei Kiriyama is a seventeen-year-old professional shogi player in Tokyo, one of only a handful ever to turn pro while still in middle school. Taken in as a child by a friend of his father, a professional player who made him his apprentice, he grew up in a household where his success bred resentment, and he now lives on his own in a nearly empty apartment. Withdrawn, lonely and often worn out, Rei juggles high school classes with his official matches. His life slowly changes after he meets the Kawamoto sisters, Akari, Hinata and little Momo, whose warm, noisy home across the river becomes a refuge where he is fed and fussed over.

riko-brzenska.name: Rico Brzenska
riko-brzenska.role: Team leader in the Garrison's elite squad

debut.episodeTitle: Whereabouts of His Left Arm: The Struggle for Trost, Part 5

riko-brzenska.notes: Episode 9 and chapter 10 ("Where's the Left Arm?", volume 3) debut rest on the Attack on Titan Wiki; Wikipedia episode summaries first name her in episode 11. Arc names follow the wiki's anime page.
riko-brzenska.abilities: An elite Garrison squad captain and skilled soldier with vertical manoeuvring equipment, known for her strict, by-the-book attitude.

fate.detail: Rico survives the Battle of Trost (where she leads Eren's escort) and is listed as alive at the end of the series.

riko-brzenska.about: Rico Brzenska is a squad leader in the Garrison's elite forces, the soldiers who guard the walls of humanity's last cities. She is short, silver-haired and wears glasses, and she is strict, sceptical and blunt, with little patience for wishful thinking. During the fight to retake the Trost District, she is assigned to protect the newly discovered Titan shifter Eren Yeager while he tries to carry a boulder to seal a breach in the wall. Rico makes it clear she does not trust a plan built on a boy she barely understands, but she carries out her orders anyway. Her role is small, but she is the soldier who fires the flare when the operation succeeds.

rin-hoshizora.name: Rin Hoshizora
rin-hoshizora.role: Athletic first-year student at Otonokizaka Academy and member of the school idol group μ's
rin-hoshizora.notes: Love Live! is a multimedia project rather than an adaptation of a manga or light novel, so source is null. The episode 1 debut rests on the Love Live! Wiki; Wikipedia episode summaries first name her in episode 4.
rin-hoshizora.abilities: An energetic, athletic first-year and member of the idol group mu's, known for her cat-like 'nya' and boundless stamina.

fate.detail: Rin is alive at the end of the series and the 2015 movie; Love Live! has no character deaths.

rin-hoshizora.about: Rin Hoshizora is a first-year at Otonokizaka Academy, an old girls' school threatened with closure, and a member of the school idol group μ's. Sporty, energetic and full of stamina, she often finishes her sentences with a cat-like 'nya'. She loves ramen, dislikes fish, and as a child was a tomboy who played sports and rarely wore skirts. Rin has been best friends with the shy Hanayo Koizumi since they were small and is almost always by her side. When Hanayo hesitates to chase her dream of becoming an idol, Rin pushes her to go for it, and the two join μ's together. Her bounce and enthusiasm make her one of the group's liveliest members.

rin-okumura.name: Rin Okumura
rin-okumura.role: Protagonist; son of Satan who trains as an exorcist at True Cross Academy

debut.episodeTitle: The Devil Resides in Human Souls

rin-okumura.notes: Arc names follow the Blue Exorcist Wiki (manga arcs). Other relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
rin-okumura.abilities: The son of Satan, whose demonic powers are sealed in the sword Kurikara; drawing it gives him blue flames, demonic strength and fast healing.

fate.detail: Rin is alive in the anime and the ongoing manga (as of November 2026).

rin-okumura.about: Rin Okumura is a fifteen-year-old with a short temper who has been raised, along with his studious twin brother Yukio, by the exorcist priest Shiro Fujimoto at a small monastery. Rin cannot hold down a job and keeps getting into fights, but he cares about his family more than he lets on. When he starts seeing demons, he learns that he is the son of Satan, and that his demonic power has been sealed inside a sword called Kurikara. Drawing the blade wraps him in blue flame. Rin decides to fight demons instead of joining them and enrolls in the exorcist cram school at True Cross Academy, where he finds Yukio teaching his class.

rin-tohsaka.name: Rin Tohsaka
rin-tohsaka.role: Master in the Fifth Holy Grail War who summons Archer; heir to the Tohsaka magecraft
rin-tohsaka.notes: Fate/stay night is a visual novel, so source is null. Episode 0 ("Prologue") opens the Unlimited Blade Works TV series from her point of view. Other relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
rin-tohsaka.abilities: A gifted mage of the Tohsaka family and Archer's Master, who stores mana in jewels for gem magecraft and fires Gandr curse shots.

fate.detail: Rin survives the Fifth Holy Grail War in Unlimited Blade Works and leaves for the Clock Tower in London with Shirou.

rin-tohsaka.about: Rin Tohsaka is a second-year at Homurahara Academy, admired by classmates as a poised, top-of-the-class model student. In secret she is the young head of the Tohsaka family of mages and one of the Masters fighting the Fifth Holy Grail War, a battle royale between seven mages and the heroic spirits they summon. She calls up Archer as her Servant, though not in the way she intended. Proud and competitive, she is kinder than she lets on, prone to blunders at the worst moments, and hopeless with modern electronics. She fights with gems charged with stored magical energy and fires Gandr curse shots. When her classmate Shirou Emiya stumbles into the war, she forms an uneasy alliance with him.

robin-nico.name: Nico Robin
robin-nico.role: Archaeologist of the Straw Hat Pirates; formerly Miss All Sunday of Baroque Works

debut.episodeTitle: Deliver Princess Vivi! The Luffy Pirates Set Sail!

robin-nico.notes: Arcs listed are pre-timeskip arcs from the wiki's history page; she also takes part in later Straw Hat arcs.
robin-nico.abilities: An archaeologist who can read the ancient Poneglyphs; her Hana Hana no Mi Devil Fruit lets her sprout copies of her body parts, such as arms, on any surface.

fate.detail: Robin is alive in the anime and the ongoing manga (as of November 2026); she nearly dies at Enies Lobby but is rescued by the Straw Hats.

robin-nico.about: Nico Robin first appears as Miss All Sunday, the calm, mysterious partner of the head of Baroque Works, the criminal organisation the Straw Hats run up against while escorting Princess Vivi home to Alabasta. She is tall, dark-haired and almost unreadable, smiling faintly while she quietly pursues goals of her own. Her Devil Fruit power lets her sprout extra arms and other body parts on any surface, making her dangerous at close range and from afar. Robin is also a scholar who can read the ancient Poneglyphs, stone records nobody else can decipher, and her search for what they say drives her choices. That poise and secrecy make her stand out from the rest of the crew.

sanji.name: Sanji
sanji.role: Cook of the Straw Hat Pirates; former sous-chef of the Baratie

debut.episodeTitle: Famous Cook! Sanji of the Sea Restaurant!

sanji.notes: Arcs listed are pre-timeskip arcs from the wiki's history page; he also takes part in later Straw Hat arcs. Birth family left out to avoid spoilers.
sanji.abilities: The Straw Hats' cook, who fights only with powerful kicks (Black Leg Style) to keep his hands safe for cooking.

fate.detail: Sanji is alive in the anime and in the ongoing manga (as of November 2026).

sanji.about: Sanji works as second-in-command in the kitchen of the Baratie, a floating restaurant on the open sea, when Monkey D. Luffy crashes into it and is made to work off the damage. A chain-smoking, sharply dressed cook, he holds that nobody who is hungry should ever be turned away. He fights only with powerful kicks so that his hands stay safe for cooking, and he falls head over heels for nearly every woman he meets. Sanji owes his life and his training to Zeff, the restaurant's gruff owner, and he dreams of finding the All Blue, a legendary sea where fish from all four oceans swim together. He joins Luffy's crew as its cook.

satoru-fujinuma.name: Satoru Fujinuma
satoru-fujinuma.role: Protagonist; struggling manga artist with a time-travel ability called Revival
satoru-fujinuma.notes: Arc names follow the Boku Dake ga Inai Machi Wiki.
satoru-fujinuma.abilities: A struggling manga artist with "Revival", an involuntary ability that sends him back a few minutes in time to prevent an imminent tragedy.

fate.detail: Satoru survives: the killer throws him into a river and he spends years in a coma, but he wakes up, helps catch the culprit and finally succeeds as a manga artist (anime and manga endings differ in details).

satoru-fujinuma.about: Satoru Fujinuma is a twenty-nine-year-old manga artist whose career has stalled, so he pays the bills delivering pizza. He keeps people at arm's length and rarely says what he feels. He also has a strange involuntary ability he calls Revival: when something terrible is about to happen nearby, he is thrown back a few minutes in time and keeps reliving the moment until he spots and prevents the danger. When a far more serious crisis hits close to home, Revival sends him back eighteen years instead, into his own eleven-year-old body in 1988, shortly before a classmate, Kayo Hinazuki, went missing. The story follows him trying to change that winter.

satoshi-mashiba.name: Satoshi Mashiba
satoshi-mashiba.role: High school boy who joins Shoya Ishida's group of friends
satoshi-mashiba.notes: There is no TV anime: Koe no Katachi (A Silent Voice) is a 2016 film, so episode is null. Chapter 24 rests on the Koe no Katachi Wiki only.

fate.detail: Mashiba is alive at the end of both the manga and the 2016 film.

satoshi-mashiba.about: Satoshi Mashiba is a high school classmate of Shouya Ishida and Tomohiro Nagatsuka who joins their circle partway through the story. He takes an interest when he learns the friends are making an amateur film for a contest, and he wants the lead role, which his good looks and easy charm seem to suit. Calm, polite and generally even-tempered, he gets along with almost everyone in the group. Mashiba was lonely and picked on as a child, and as a result he has no tolerance at all for bullying in any form, reacting sharply whenever he sees it. That stance makes him an uneasy presence for Shouya, who is still haunted by his own past as a bully.

shidou-itsuka.name: Shido Itsuka
shidou-itsuka.role: Protagonist; high school student recruited by Ratatoskr to seal the powers of Spirits
shidou-itsuka.notes: Light novel debut is volume 1. Other relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
shidou-itsuka.abilities: An ordinary high-schooler with a mysterious power to seal a Spirit's powers by making her fall in love with him and kissing her, plus rapid regeneration from wounds.

fate.detail: Shido survives to the end of the Date A Live light novels (concluded 2020) and is alive in the anime.

shidou-itsuka.about: Shido Itsuka is an ordinary high school student at Raizen High who lives with his cheerful adoptive younger sister, Kotori, in a city that is regularly hit by spacequakes, sudden explosions that occur when beings called Spirits cross into our world. When he runs into the Spirit later named Tohka, he learns that Kotori secretly commands Ratatoskr, an organisation that wants to save the Spirits rather than kill them. Shido, it turns out, can seal a Spirit's power, but only after winning her heart and kissing her, so he is pushed into dating practice with gal games and live coaching. He is kind, flustered and patient, which suits the job.

shinji-ikari.name: Shinji Ikari
