shinji-ikari.notes: Neon Genesis Evangelion is an original anime, so source is null; the Yoshiyuki Sadamoto manga, which began in 1994, runs alongside it and also opens with "Angel Attack". Other relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
shinji-ikari.abilities: A 14-year-old who, despite no training, shows a remarkably high synch ratio piloting Evangelion Unit-01 against the Angels.

fate.detail: Shinji survives both endings: The End of Evangelion leaves him alive with Asuka after Third Impact, and Evangelion: 3.0+1.0 (2021) ends with him alive as an adult.

shinji-ikari.about: Shinji Ikari is a fourteen-year-old boy summoned to the fortified city of Tokyo-3 by his estranged father, Gendo Ikari, who sent him away to be raised elsewhere when he was small. On arrival he learns why: Gendo commands the special agency Nerv and wants Shinji to pilot Evangelion Unit-01, a giant humanoid war machine, against monstrous beings known as Angels. With no training and little real choice, Shinji agrees. Withdrawn, anxious and starved for approval, he retreats into his music player, tends to run from conflict, and still keeps climbing back into the cockpit. He moves in with his guardian, Misato Katsuragi, and his struggle to connect with others sits at the heart of the series.

shizuka-marikawa.name: Shizuka Marikawa
shizuka-marikawa.role: School nurse at Fujimi High School who escapes with the student survivors
shizuka-marikawa.notes: Episode 1 rests on the Highschool of the Dead Wiki; Wikipedia episode summaries first name her in episode 2. Manga chapter not confirmed.
shizuka-marikawa.abilities: Fujimi High's ditzy school nurse, whose medical knowledge makes her the group's doctor; she also drives them out of the school.

fate.detail: Shizuka is alive at the end of the anime and of the manga, which was left unfinished after writer Daisuke Satō died in 2017.

shizuka-marikawa.about: Shizuka Marikawa is the school nurse at Fujimi Academy, a gentle, scatterbrained woman in her twenties who is in her office when the outbreak of the walking dead begins. Separated from the other staff, she is rescued by the swordswoman Saeko Busujima and soon falls in with Takashi Komuro's group of student survivors. As the only adult, she is often the least composed person in the room and the target of much of the show's broad fan-service comedy, but her medical training makes her the group's doctor, and she is the one who drives them out of the school. She also offers her friend's apartment as a refuge.

shouko-nishimiya.name: Shouko Nishimiya
shouko-nishimiya.role: Co-lead; deaf girl who was bullied by Shoya Ishida in elementary school
shouko-nishimiya.notes: There is no TV anime: Koe no Katachi (A Silent Voice) is a 2016 film, so episode is null. Chapter 1 per the wiki; Wikipedia confirms she is on the volume 1 cover.
shouko-nishimiya.abilities: A deaf girl who communicates through a notebook and sign language, and who stays kind even toward people who hurt her.

fate.detail: Shoko attempts suicide by jumping from her balcony, but Shoya saves her (manga and 2016 film); she survives the series.

shouko-nishimiya.about: Shouko Nishimiya is a deaf girl who transfers into Shouya Ishida's sixth-grade class, carrying a notebook so that classmates can write to her. Despite her warmth and constant apologies, she becomes the target of escalating bullying led by Shouya, who mocks her and turns the class against her, until she leaves the school. Five years later, Shouya, now isolated and filled with regret, tracks her down, having learnt sign language, to try to make amends. Gentle, persistent and quick to blame herself, Shouko struggles to make herself understood and tends to hide her own feelings behind a smile. Their reunion drives the story's exploration of guilt and forgiveness.

shura-kirigakure.name: Shura Kirigakure
shura-kirigakure.role: Upper First Class Exorcist of the True Cross Order who trained under Shiro Fujimoto
shura-kirigakure.notes: She first appears disguised as the student "Yamada" (episode 3, chapter 2 per the Blue Exorcist Wiki only); Wikipedia confirms her reveal as herself in episode 12. Arc names follow the wiki. Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
shura-kirigakure.abilities: An Upper First Class Exorcist and Vatican inspector, a Meister-level Knight (swordswoman) and Doctor who draws a demon sword from a seal on her body and trains Rin.

fate.detail: Shura is alive in the anime and the ongoing manga (as of November 2026); the Beyond the Snow arc deals with the family curse that dooms her at age 30.

shura-kirigakure.about: Shura Kirigakure, an exorcist of the Upper First Class rank, reports to the Vatican and is sent to inspect True Cross Academy and its handling of a certain new student, Rin Okumura. She was trained by the paladin Shiro Fujimoto, Rin's adoptive father, and treats his sons with a mix of affection and mockery. Shura is loud, lazy, fond of beer and indifferent to dress codes, but in a fight she is a master swordswoman who draws a demonic blade from a seal on her own body. She takes over Rin's training in controlling his sword and flames, pushing him hard while hiding her own concern, and her brash teaching style sets her apart.

sora-2.name: Sora
sora-2.role: Co-protagonist; half of the undefeated gamer duo Blank
sora-2.notes: The light novel debut is volume 1; Wikipedia confirms he is on the volume 1 cover. Later family members left out to avoid spoilers.
sora-2.abilities: Half of the undefeated gamer duo 'Blank' with his sister Shiro; he excels at reading people, bluffing and long-term strategy.

fate.detail: Sora is alive in the anime, the 2017 film and the ongoing light novels.

sora-2.about: Sora is an eighteen-year-old shut-in gamer who, together with his young stepsister Shiro, forms Blank, an anonymous duo that has never lost a game. He is the half who reads people, bluffing, provoking and planning many moves ahead, while Shiro excels at calculation. Lazy, crude and badly awkward with strangers in real life, he falls apart whenever he is separated from Shiro. After the siblings beat a mysterious challenger at chess, they are pulled into Disboard, a world ruled by the god Tet where every dispute must be settled through games. There they set out to help Imanity, the weakest of its races, starting with a bid for the throne of Elkia.

stephanie-dora.name: Stephanie Dola
stephanie-dora.role: Granddaughter of the previous king of Elkia who becomes the aide of Sora and Shiro
stephanie-dora.notes: Episode 1 is confirmed by both sources. Light novel volume 1 and her grandfather's name rest on the No Game No Life Wiki; Wikipedia mentions the grandfather without naming him.
stephanie-dora.abilities: The granddaughter of Elkia's late king, a noble with good schooling but poor luck at games, who handles the kingdom's administration.

fate.detail: Steph is alive in the anime and the ongoing light novels.

stephanie-dora.about: Stephanie Dola, nicknamed Steph, is the granddaughter of the late king of Elkia, the last human kingdom left in a world where every dispute is settled by games. She is gambling for the throne when Sora and Shiro first see her, losing a high-stakes card game to a rival who is secretly cheating. Steph is emotional, earnest and hopelessly easy to read, which makes her terrible at games, and she is fiercely loyal to her grandfather's belief that humans can win. After a quick wager with Sora goes badly wrong for her, she ends up working as the siblings' aide. Much of the show's comedy comes from how often she becomes the butt of their schemes.

suzaku-kururugi.name: Suzaku Kururugi
suzaku-kururugi.role: Japanese-born soldier in the Britannian Army who pilots the Lancelot; Lelouch's childhood friend

debut.anime: Code Geass: Lelouch of the Rebellion
debut.episodeTitle: The Day a New Demon was Born

suzaku-kururugi.notes: Code Geass is an original anime, so there is no source chapter.
suzaku-kururugi.abilities: A Japanese-born Britannian soldier with superhuman reflexes and athleticism, and the pilot of the advanced Knightmare Frame Lancelot.

fate.detail: Suzaku is publicly declared dead, but he survives and wears the mask of Zero to kill Lelouch in the Zero Requiem (R2 episode 25), living on as Zero.

suzaku-kururugi.about: Suzaku Kururugi, whose father led Japan as its final prime minister, was a close friend of Lelouch and Nunnally when the two Britannian children lived in Japan. After Britannia conquered the country, Suzaku became an Honorary Britannian and joined the occupying army, convinced that the only fair way to change the system is from inside it. He is upright, idealistic and self-sacrificing to a fault, and he rejects any victory won by unjust means. His extraordinary reflexes earn him the role of pilot for the Lancelot, an experimental Knightmare Frame. He then enrols at Ashford Academy and reunites with Lelouch, unaware that his old friend is Zero, the masked rebel he is fighting.

suzuha-amane.name: Suzuha Amane
suzuha-amane.role: Part-time worker for the landlord of the Future Gadget Laboratory's building
suzuha-amane.notes: Debut is in the first Steins;Gate series, not Steins;Gate 0. Steins;Gate is adapted from a visual novel, so source is null. Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
suzuha-amane.abilities: A time traveller from a dystopian 2036 with excellent fighting skills, who works part-time at the shop below the lab and rides a bicycle everywhere.

fate.detail: On one Alpha world line she reaches 1975 with amnesia and later takes her own life out of guilt, which Okabe's D-Mail undoes; in the final Steins;Gate world line she is alive.

suzuha-amane.about: Suzuha Amane is a part-time worker at the CRT television shop directly below the Future Gadget Laboratory, run by the building's gruff landlord, whom Okabe calls Mr. Braun. She is energetic and athletic, rides her bicycle everywhere, and likes to drop oddly formal, military-sounding words into casual chat. Suzuha is friendly with Okabe and the others but takes an instant, unexplained dislike to Kurisu Makise. She seems to be in Akihabara for reasons she keeps to herself. Her mix of easy friendliness and sudden seriousness makes her one of the mysteries the first half of the series quietly sets up.

tachikoma.name: Tachikoma
tachikoma.role: AI-equipped multi-legged think tanks used by Public Security Section 9

debut.anime: Ghost in the Shell: Stand Alone Complex

tachikoma.notes: The role is confirmed by both sources. The episode 1 debut rests on Wikipedia; the Ghost in the Shell Wiki gives no first episode. Tachikomatic Days is a set of shorts that aired alongside Stand Alone Complex. The original manga has the earlier Fuchikoma design, so no manga chapter is given.
tachikoma.abilities: Spider-like AI think-tanks used by Section 9, armed with machine guns and grenade launchers, with thermo-optic camouflage and the habit of sharing memories each night.

fate.detail: In Stand Alone Complex episode 25 the three remaining Tachikoma sacrifice themselves to save Batou; their AIs survive on a satellite and they return in 2nd GIG.

tachikoma.about: Tachikoma are the spider-like think tanks used by Public Security Section 9, the squad that handles cybercrime and terrorism. Each is about as big as a compact car, painted blue, with four legs ending in wheels, room for a person to ride inside, a machine gun, a grenade launcher and thermo-optic camouflage. They are run by artificial intelligences that speak in high, childlike voices and approach everything with eager curiosity, debating philosophy, books and what makes them different from humans. Every night their memories are synchronised so all units share the same experiences, yet they keep developing individual quirks. Batou has a favourite unit, which he spoils with natural oil.

takashi-komuro.name: Takashi Komuro
takashi-komuro.role: Protagonist; second-year student at Fujimi Academy who leads the survivors
takashi-komuro.notes: Wikipedia calls the school Fujimi High School; both sources cite chapter (Act) 1 for his opening scenes.
takashi-komuro.abilities: An ordinary student who becomes the group's leader in the zombie outbreak, fighting with a baseball bat and later firearms.

fate.detail: Takashi is alive at the end of the anime and of the manga, which was left unfinished after writer Daisuke Satō died in 2017.

takashi-komuro.about: Takashi Komuro is a second-year at Fujimi Academy who is skipping class outside the classroom when he sees a man at the school gate attack a teacher, and the teacher get back up. He reacts faster than almost anyone else, grabbing a baseball bat and rushing to get his childhood friend Rei Miyamoto, who is dating his friend Hisashi, out of the building. As the outbreak spreads through the city, Takashi becomes the reluctant leader of a small group of survivors that includes the genius Saya Takagi, the swordswoman Saeko Busujima and the gun enthusiast Kohta Hirano. He is impulsive and unsure of himself, but he keeps making the hard calls.

takumi-aldini.name: Takumi Aldini
takumi-aldini.role: Transfer student from Florence at Totsuki Culinary Academy who specialises in Italian cuisine

debut.episodeTitle: A Concerto of Concept and Creation

takumi-aldini.notes: Episode 8 is his first full appearance (confirmed by both sources); the wiki also lists a cameo in episode 3 and chapter 4. Chapter 15 rests on the Shokugeki no Soma Wiki only.
takumi-aldini.abilities: An Italian chef from his family's trattoria, a specialist in Italian cuisine who works with a custom mezzaluna knife.

fate.detail: Takumi is alive at the end of the manga and anime.

takumi-aldini.about: Takumi Aldini is a first-year transfer student at Totsuki Culinary Academy who grew up cooking at Trattoria Aldini, the family-run restaurant in Florence. Half Japanese, blond and polished, he specialises in Italian cuisine, works with a custom mezzaluna knife and has admirers both at school and back home. He cooks alongside his younger twin brother, Isami, who usually takes the supporting role in the kitchen. Proud and competitive, Takumi quickly fixes on Souma Yukihira, another chef raised in a family restaurant, as his rival, and he is eager to settle the matter in a formal cooking duel. His fierce pride, mixed with growing respect for Souma, keeps their rivalry running through the series.

tamaki-suoh.name: Tamaki Suou
tamaki-suoh.role: Co-founder and president of the Ouran Academy Host Club

debut.episodeTitle: Starting Today, You Are a Host!

tamaki-suoh.notes: Episode 1 is confirmed by both sources; chapter 1 rests on the Ouran Wiki. A manga-epilogue marriage is left out to avoid spoilers.
tamaki-suoh.abilities: The flamboyant founder and 'King' of the Host Club, whose charm makes him the club's top host; he is also a talented pianist.

fate.detail: Nobody dies in Ouran; Tamaki is alive at the end of the anime and manga.

tamaki-suoh.about: Tamaki Suou, a second-year with a French mother and a Japanese father, founded the Ouran Academy Host Club with his friend Kyoya Ootori and rules over it as its self-styled King. The club exists to entertain the school's rich girls, and Tamaki is its most popular host, showering every guest with sincere, theatrical compliments. When the scholarship student Haruhi Fujioka breaks an expensive vase in the club's music room, Tamaki declares she must work off the debt as a host, having at first assumed she was a boy. He is dramatic, easily wounded and absurdly earnest, and often sulks in a corner when teased. He also plays the piano well.

tomura-shigaraki.name: Tomura Shigaraki
tomura-shigaraki.role: Leader of the League of Villains; main antagonist of the series
tomura-shigaraki.notes: Episode 8 and chapter 11 rest on the My Hero Academia Wiki; the Wikipedia summary of episode 8 mentions unnamed villains, and Wikipedia cites chapter 13 for him leading the attack on the U.S.J. Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
tomura-shigaraki.abilities: Leader of the League of Villains, whose Quirk, Decay, disintegrates anything he touches with all five fingers.

fate.detail: In the final battle Deku destroys All For One within him and his body disintegrates into ash (manga, 2024; anime final season, 2025).

tomura-shigaraki.about: Tomura Shigaraki heads the League of Villains. He is a gaunt, pale figure with ragged light-blue hair who wears severed hands clinging to his face and body. His Quirk, Decay, makes anything he grips with all five fingers crumble to dust. He means to murder All Might, the hero known as the Symbol of Peace, and to tear down the hero society he represents. He makes his first move by attacking a U.A. High School rescue-training exercise, bringing a hulking creature called a Nomu with him. Childish, petulant and given to scratching at his neck when frustrated, he treats the fight like a video game and sulks when it does not go his way.

tsubaki-sawabe.name: Tsubaki Sawabe
tsubaki-sawabe.role: Kousei Arima's childhood friend and next-door neighbour
tsubaki-sawabe.notes: Episode 1 is confirmed by both sources; chapter 1 ("Monotone") rests on the Your Lie in April Wiki.
tsubaki-sawabe.abilities: Kousei's athletic childhood friend, a member of the softball team.

fate.detail: Tsubaki survives the series; after Kaori's death she resolves to stay by Kousei's side.

tsubaki-sawabe.about: Tsubaki Sawabe is Kousei Arima's next-door neighbour and friend since early childhood, now in her last year at Sumiya Junior High and a player on its softball team. She is outgoing, sporty and bossy, and she treats Kousei like a younger brother who needs looking after, dragging him outside and scolding him for shutting himself away since he gave up the piano. Tsubaki is also the one who introduces the violinist Kaori Miyazono to their friend Watari, which is how Kousei first meets her. She wants Kousei to stop drifting and decide what he wants, even if that means pushing him somewhere she cannot follow. Her honest, fiery manner keeps Kousei tied to ordinary life.

tsutomu-goshiki.name: Tsutomu Goshiki
tsutomu-goshiki.role: First-year wing spiker and up-and-coming ace of Shiratorizawa Academy's volleyball team
tsutomu-goshiki.notes: The role is confirmed by both sources. Chapter 150 ("Greetings", volume 17 per Wikipedia's chapter list), where he appears unnamed, rests on the Haikyuu!! Wiki. Anime debut left blank: the wiki's character infobox gives Second Season episode 14 ("Growing Fast"), but that episode's own wiki page does not list him.
tsutomu-goshiki.abilities: Shiratorizawa's first-year wing spiker, with powerful straight and cross shots and a burning desire to become the team's ace.

fate.detail: Goshiki is alive at the end of the manga (chapter 402, 2020); Haikyu!! has no character deaths.

tsutomu-goshiki.about: Tsutomu Goshiki plays wing spiker as a first-year at Shiratorizawa Academy, the powerhouse volleyball school that has long dominated Miyagi Prefecture, and the only first-year in its starting line-up. Sporting a neat bowl cut and a big ambitious streak, he is determined to be recognised as the team's ace and openly measures himself against Wakatoshi Ushijima, the star whose role he hopes to inherit. Earnest and easily flattered, he brightens instantly whenever his seniors praise him, which they sometimes do to steady his nerves. On court he hits powerful straight and cross shots. His eager rivalry with Ushijima, more one-sided than he would like, gives Shiratorizawa much of its personality.

usopp.name: Usopp
usopp.role: Sniper of the Straw Hat Pirates

debut.episodeTitle: Who is the Victor? Devil Fruit Power Showdown!

usopp.notes: Chapter 23 is confirmed by both sources. Episode 8 rests on the One Piece Wiki; the Wikipedia summaries first name him in episode 9. Arcs are from the wiki's pre-timeskip history page.
usopp.abilities: The Straw Hats' sniper and a habitual liar, a sharpshooter with a slingshot who invents trick ammunition and gadgets.

fate.detail: Usopp is alive in the anime and the ongoing manga (as of November 2026).

usopp.about: Usopp is a long-nosed teenager from Syrup Village who runs through the streets every morning shouting that pirates are coming, a lie the villagers have long stopped believing. He leads a gang of three small boys he calls the Usopp Pirates and secretly visits Kaya, a sickly rich girl, to cheer her up with outrageous stories about his adventures. Usopp is a crack shot with a slingshot and a handy inventor, but also an admitted coward whose knees shake in a fight. His dream is to sail out and prove himself as brave as his father, Yasopp, who sails with Shanks. When his bravery does appear, it is a choice he makes despite real fear.

vanessa-enoteca.name: Vanessa Enoteca
vanessa-enoteca.role: Witch and Black Bulls member who uses Thread Magic
vanessa-enoteca.notes: Episode 6 and chapter 3 rest on the Black Clover Wiki; the Wikipedia summary of episode 6 mentions two fighting Black Bulls without naming them. Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
vanessa-enoteca.abilities: A Black Bulls mage whose Thread Magic binds enemies and lets her move allies like puppets.

fate.detail: Vanessa is alive in the anime and in the ongoing manga (as of November 2026).

vanessa-enoteca.about: Vanessa Enoteca belongs to the Black Bulls, the rowdiest squad of the Clover Kingdom's Magic Knights, and a witch who comes from the Witches' Forest. She is usually found with a drink in hand, lounging around the squad's hideout and teasing her teammates, and she loves gossiping about romance, especially when it involves Asta or the other Black Bulls. Her Thread Magic lets her bind enemies in place and control allies' movements like a puppeteer, which makes her a valuable support fighter. Laid-back and affectionate beneath the heavy drinking, she treats the squad as family and the hideout as home. She is one of the first Black Bulls to welcome Asta into their chaotic ranks.

yato.name: Yato
yato.role: Stray god who takes on any wish for a five-yen offering as a "delivery god"

debut.episodeTitle: A Housecat, a Stray God, and a Tail

yato.notes: Chapter 1 per the wiki; Wikipedia confirms he is on the volume 1 cover. Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
yato.abilities: Once a god of calamity, now a minor shrine-less god who takes any wish for 5 yen; a deadly swordsman when wielding his Regalia (Shinki) as a blade, he can cut phantoms and even people's ties.

fate.detail: Yato is alive at the end of the Noragami manga (concluded 2023) and in the anime.

yato.about: Yato is a minor god with no shrine and almost no worshippers. He wears a cheap tracksuit and advertises himself as a 'delivery god', scrawling his phone number on walls and promising to handle any wish for a five-yen offering. He dreams of millions of followers and a grand temple, but spends his days chasing lost cats. At the start of the story his weapon-spirit quits on him, so he needs a new shinki to fight the phantoms preying on people. After a girl named Hiyori Iki is hit by a bus while saving him, she demands that he fix what happened to her. Yato is vain, childish and broke, yet unexpectedly capable once a fight begins.

yotsuha-miyamizu.name: Yotsuha Miyamizu
yotsuha-miyamizu.notes: Kimi no Na wa. (Your Name) is a 2016 original film, so episode and source chapter are null. An in-law relation shown only after the story is left out to avoid spoilers.
yotsuha-miyamizu.abilities: Mitsuha's sharp, cheeky younger sister, who helps at the family shrine.

fate.detail: In the original timeline she dies when the comet destroys Itomori in 2013, but after the evacuation that Taki sets in motion she survives and appears as a teenager in the epilogue.

yotsuha-miyamizu.about: Yotsuha Miyamizu is Mitsuha Miyamizu's younger sister, an elementary school pupil in the mountain town of Itomori who lives with Mitsuha and their grandmother Hitoha. She helps at the family shrine, braiding kumihimo cords and taking part in rituals such as preparing kuchikamizake, and she is next in line after her sister to serve as shrine maiden. Sharp-tongued and practical well beyond her years, she is quick to notice when her big sister behaves strangely, and lately Mitsuha has been acting oddly on certain mornings, forgetting things and carrying herself like a different person. Yotsuha's deadpan reactions to those changes supply much of the film's early comedy.

yui-hirasawa.name: Yui Hirasawa
yui-hirasawa.role: Lead guitarist and vocalist of the Sakuragaoka High School Light Music Club
affiliations: Sakuragaoka High School Light Music Club
yui-hirasawa.notes: The manga debut is volume 1; Wikipedia confirms she is on the volume 1 cover. Chapter left blank because the wiki labels it chapter 0.
yui-hirasawa.abilities: A carefree, clumsy girl who joins the Light Music Club with no experience and turns out to learn the guitar quickly, with a good ear (perfect pitch); she plays her guitar 'Gīta' (a Gibson Les Paul).

fate.detail: Nobody dies in K-On!; Yui is alive at the end of the anime and manga.

yui-hirasawa.about: Yui Hirasawa is a cheerful, scatterbrained first-year at Sakuragaoka High School who has never stuck with anything. She signs up for the Light Music Club because she imagines 'light music' must mean something easy and only then learns it is a rock band about to fold for lack of members. Despite never having touched an instrument, she joins, buys a Gibson Les Paul she names Gitah, and turns out to have a good ear and to pick up songs fast, though new chords tend to push older lessons out of her head. Her capable younger sister, Ui, looks after her at home. Yui's easygoing warmth sets the tone of the series.

yuno-kurosurii.name: Yuno
yuno-kurosurii.role: Asta's rival and fellow orphan from Hage; Golden Dawn Magic Knight
arcs: Eye of the Midnight Sun Encounter
yuno-kurosurii.notes: Chapter 1 per the wiki; Wikipedia confirms he is on the volume 1 cover. He also appears in the 2016 Jump Festa special. His birth family is left out to avoid spoilers.
yuno-kurosurii.abilities: Asta's fellow orphan and rival, a prodigy mage whose Wind Magic is strengthened when he receives a legendary four-leaf grimoire and the wind spirit Sylph.

fate.detail: Yuno is alive in the anime and in the ongoing manga (as of November 2026).

yuno-kurosurii.about: Yuno was abandoned as a baby at the church in Hage, a poor village on the edge of the Clover Kingdom, together with Asta. The two grew up like brothers and became rivals, each vowing to become the Wizard King, the kingdom's greatest mage. Where Asta has no magic at all, Yuno is a prodigy with Wind Magic: calm, quiet and seemingly aloof, though he cares deeply about his home village and about Asta. At fifteen he receives a rare four-leaf clover grimoire, an event of legendary significance, and soon draws the attention of the wind spirit Sylph. He then earns a place in the Golden Dawn, the kingdom's most elite squad of Magic Knights.

yuriko-aoki.name: Yuriko Aoki
yuriko-aoki.role: Manga artist, pen name Ko Aoki, who moves from shōjo to Weekly Shōnen Jump
yuriko-aoki.notes: Her Hideout Door partner is Takuro Nakai. A later engagement is left out to avoid spoilers.
yuriko-aoki.abilities: A talented manga writer with a strong literary, novel-like style of storytelling, though she struggles at first with drawing and pacing for a weekly series.

fate.detail: Nobody dies in Bakuman; Aoki is alive at the end of the manga and anime.

yuriko-aoki.about: Yuriko Aoki is a manga writer who first worked for a shoujo magazine before an editor suggested she try her hand at Weekly Shonen Jump, where she publishes under the pen name Ko Aoki. Educated at the elite To-Oh University, she writes in a literary, almost novelistic style, and she is paired with the artist Takuro Nakai to create the series Hideout Door. Aoki first comes across as cool, formal and hard to approach. She takes her work very seriously and initially struggles with the weekly pace and the boys' manga market. She is a rival and peer to Moritaka Mashiro and Akito Takagi.

zeke-5bb8f171-4101-4129-9b75-7d516ef3753.name: Zeke
zeke-5bb8f171-4101-4129-9b75-7d516ef3753.role: War chief of Marley's Warrior Unit and holder of the Beast Titan
zeke-5bb8f171-4101-4129-9b75-7d516ef3753.notes: Season 2 episode 1 is episode 26 overall; Wikipedia's summary has the Beast Titan appear there. Chapter 34 ("Soldiers Dance", end of volume 8) rests on the Attack on Titan Wiki; Wikipedia only says he is introduced around volume 9. Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
zeke-5bb8f171-4101-4129-9b75-7d516ef3753.abilities: The Beast Titan: a large ape-like Titan that can speak, command mindless Titans and hurl boulders with deadly accuracy.

fate.detail: During the final battle, Levi decapitates him after he emerges from Eren's Titan (manga chapter 137; anime Final Chapters Special 2, 2023).

zeke-5bb8f171-4101-4129-9b75-7d516ef3753.about: Zeke is the man inside the Beast Titan, a towering, fur-covered, ape-like Titan that suddenly appears inside Wall Rose. Unlike the mindless Titans around it, the Beast Titan can speak, shows a calm, almost scholarly curiosity about the humans it meets, and seems able to direct other Titans as though commanding troops. It even questions soldiers about their equipment before deciding what to do with them. In battle he hurls boulders and debris with devastating accuracy, a tactic modelled on pitching a ball. In human form he is a bearded man with glasses, and the other Titan shifters who fight alongside him address him as their war chief.

jujutsu-kaisen-satoru-gojou.name: Satoru Gojou
jujutsu-kaisen-satoru-gojou.role: Special grade jujutsu sorcerer and teacher at Tokyo Jujutsu High; Megumi Fushiguro's mentor
jujutsu-kaisen-satoru-gojou.notes: Both sources agree he first appeared in chapter 1 of the prequel Jujutsu Kaisen 0 (2017). The main-series chapter 1 rests on the Jujutsu Kaisen Wiki, which says he is only heard and seen on the cover there and appears in full in chapter 2. Episode 1 rests on the wiki; the Wikipedia summaries first name him in episode 2. Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
jujutsu-kaisen-satoru-gojou.abilities: Called the strongest jujutsu sorcerer, he has the Limitless technique, an untouchable barrier of 'infinity', and the Six Eyes, which let him perceive cursed energy in fine detail.

fate.detail: Gojo is sealed in the Prison Realm during the Shibuya Incident (anime season 2), freed later, and then killed by Sukuna in their duel in manga chapter 236 (2023); the anime has not reached that chapter as of November 2026.

jujutsu-kaisen-satoru-gojou.about: Satoru Gojo holds the rare special grade rank among jujutsu sorcerers, is generally considered the strongest alive, and a teacher at Tokyo Jujutsu High. Tall, white-haired and usually blindfolded, he is flippant, playful and fond of sweets, and he openly mocks the conservative elders who run the jujutsu world. Gojo turns up in Sendai to collect a cursed object and finds that Yuji Itadori has swallowed it, becoming the host of Ryomen Sukuna. Rather than carry out the order to execute Yuji, he persuades the higher-ups to postpone it and enrolls him at the school alongside his student Megumi Fushiguro. His Limitless technique keeps attacks from ever reaching him, which reinforces his reputation for unmatched power.

luffy-monkey-d.name: Monkey D. Luffy
luffy-monkey-d.role: Protagonist; captain of the Straw Hat Pirates who wants to become King of the Pirates

debut.episodeTitle: I'm Gonna Be King of the Pirates!

luffy-monkey-d.notes: Arcs listed are the East Blue arcs; he is in every arc of the series. Episode title as in the Wikipedia season 1 list. Family left out to avoid spoilers.
luffy-monkey-d.abilities: He ate the Gum-Gum Fruit, which gave him a stretchy rubber body that he uses for punches and kicks, backed by huge strength and resilience.

fate.detail: Luffy is alive in the anime and in the ongoing manga (as of November 2026).

luffy-monkey-d.about: Monkey D. Luffy is a cheerful, reckless teenager who sets out to sea from a small village with one goal: to claim the legendary treasure called One Piece and earn the title King of the Pirates. As a boy he ate the Gum-Gum Fruit, a Devil Fruit that made his whole body rubbery, which lets him stretch his limbs for punches and kicks but leaves him unable to swim. He treasures the straw hat given to him by the pirate Shanks, his childhood hero, and has promised to return it once he becomes a great pirate. Simple-minded, endlessly hungry and fiercely loyal, Luffy recruits his crew mostly on instinct, and he has a habit of turning former enemies into friends.

zoro-roronoa.name: Roronoa Zoro
zoro-roronoa.role: Swordsman of the Straw Hat Pirates; former pirate hunter

debut.episodeTitle: I'm Gonna Be King of the Pirates!

zoro-roronoa.notes: Chapter 3 ("Introducing Pirate Hunter Zoro") is confirmed by both sources. Episode 1 rests on the One Piece Wiki; the Wikipedia summary of episode 1 does not name him. Arcs listed are the East Blue arcs. Family left out.
zoro-roronoa.abilities: A master swordsman who fights with his three-sword style, holding a third blade in his mouth, and aims to become the world's greatest swordsman; he has a terrible sense of direction.

fate.detail: Zoro is alive in the anime and the ongoing manga (as of November 2026).

zoro-roronoa.about: Roronoa Zoro is a green-haired swordsman whom Monkey D. Luffy finds tied to a post in the yard of a navy base, where he is going without food to keep a bargain made with the base captain's spoiled son. Feared as a pirate hunter, he has no interest in becoming a pirate until Luffy recovers his swords and asks him to join, and he agrees on the condition that nothing gets in the way of his goal of becoming the world's greatest swordsman. Zoro fights with three swords at once, one held in his teeth. He is gruff, disciplined and loyal, naps whenever he can, and has a famously terrible sense of direction.

arataka-reigen.name: Arataka Reigen
arataka-reigen.role: Self-proclaimed psychic who runs the Spirits and Such Consultation Office; Mob's boss and mentor
arataka-reigen.notes: Episode 1 is confirmed by both sources. Chapter 1 rests on the Mob Psycho 100 Wiki; Wikipedia's character list gives no chapter.
arataka-reigen.abilities: A self-proclaimed great psychic with no real powers, who gets by on charisma, quick talk, common sense, table salt and genuinely good massages.

fate.detail: Reigen is alive at the end of the manga (2017) and the anime's third season (2022).

arataka-reigen.about: Arataka Reigen owns a small exorcism business, Spirits and Such Consultation Office, and bills himself as the 21st century's greatest psychic. He has no supernatural powers at all. Instead he gets by on fast talk, know-how picked up from many past jobs, table salt and a genuinely excellent massage technique, while quietly letting his part-time employee, the enormously powerful middle schooler Shigeo 'Mob' Kageyama, handle the real spirits for a meagre wage. Reigen is vain, opportunistic and quick to bluff his way out of trouble. He also gives Mob grounded advice about being a decent person and never using his powers against other people.

guts.name: Guts
guts.role: Protagonist; wandering swordsman known as the Black Swordsman
guts.notes: Episode 1 is confirmed by both sources. His manga debut is the opening "The Black Swordsman" chapter, which Wikipedia numbers A0 and the Berserk Wiki numbers 0-1, so chapter is null. The 1997 anime covers only the Black Swordsman and Golden Age arcs; arc names follow the Berserk Wiki. Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
guts.abilities: A hardened mercenary of extraordinary strength and battle experience who swings a huge greatsword that ordinary men cannot even lift.

fate.detail: Guts survives the Eclipse at the end of the 1997 anime, losing an arm and an eye, and is alive in the ongoing manga (continued by Studio Gaga after Kentaro Miura's death).

guts.about: Guts is a huge, scarred swordsman who carries a slab-like greatsword that most men could not lift, and the 1997 anime opens with him as the grim, solitary Black Swordsman. The series then jumps back to his younger years as a hired soldier in a long medieval-style war, a man who has fought for survival since childhood and trusts nobody. That changes when he meets Griffith, the charismatic leader of the mercenary Band of the Hawk, who wins him over in a duel and brings him into the company. Guts becomes a fearsome battlefield commander there. The story is driven by his search for a reason to fight beyond survival.

chainsaw-man-makima.name: Makima
chainsaw-man-makima.role: High-ranking Public Safety Devil Hunter who takes Denji in and recruits him
chainsaw-man-makima.notes: Relatives and her other affiliations are left out to avoid spoilers.
chainsaw-man-makima.abilities: A high-ranking Public Safety devil hunter and Denji's boss, who commands contracted devils and can kill targets from a distance just by pointing and saying 'bang'.

fate.detail: In the climax of Part 1 (manga chapters 96-97, 2020), Denji kills her with a chainsaw made from Power's blood and eats her to get around her immortality; the Control Devil is reborn as a girl named Nayuta. The anime has not reached this yet.

chainsaw-man-makima.about: Makima is a senior figure in Japan's Public Safety Devil Hunters, a calm, soft-spoken woman with striking ringed golden eyes. She finds Denji right after he has merged with his devil Pochita and gives him a choice: be killed as a devil, or work for her as her dog, with regular meals and a roof over his head in exchange. Denji, desperate for even a scrap of a normal life, is smitten at once. Makima leads an experimental unit in Tokyo Special Division 4, where she places Denji alongside the stern Aki Hayakawa and the fiend Power. Polite and unhurried, she rarely raises her voice and seldom explains her reasons.

mai-sakurajima.name: Mai Sakurajima
mai-sakurajima.role: Teenage actress at Sakuta's high school whom he meets in a library dressed as a bunny girl, unseen by everyone else

debut.anime: Seishun Buta Yarou wa Bunny Girl Senpai no Yume wo Minai
debut.episodeTitle: My Senpai is a Bunny Girl

mai-sakurajima.notes: Light novel volume 1 per the Rascal Does Not Dream Wiki; Wikipedia confirms she is on the volume 1 cover. Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
mai-sakurajima.abilities: A famous teenage actress on hiatus who becomes invisible to everyone around her because of Adolescence Syndrome; she is also a strong student and quick-witted.

fate.detail: In the film Rascal Does Not Dream of a Dreaming Girl (2019), Mai is killed by a car while saving Sakuta, but Sakuta changes the past with Shoko's help so the accident never happens; she is alive afterwards.

mai-sakurajima.about: Mai Sakurajima, in her final year at Minegahara High School, is a well-known actress who stepped away from show business. Sakuta Azusagawa, a second-year, first sees her wandering through the public library in a bunny-girl costume, and he realises that nobody else in the room has noticed her. Mai is suffering from Adolescence Syndrome, a strange condition that has made people around her stop seeing or remembering her, and the costume was her test of how far it went. She is calm, sharp-tongued and used to keeping her classmates at a distance, and she enjoys teasing Sakuta when he gets flustered. Their witty, grounded banter carries the first story arc.

chainsaw-man-denji.name: Denji
chainsaw-man-denji.role: Protagonist; indebted young devil hunter who merges with his chainsaw devil Pochita
chainsaw-man-denji.notes: Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
chainsaw-man-denji.abilities: Fused with the Chainsaw Devil Pochita, he becomes Chainsaw Man when he pulls the cord on his chest, sprouting chainsaws from his head and arms, and recovers from injuries by drinking blood.

fate.detail: He is killed by the Zombie Devil's yakuza in the first chapter and episode, and revived when Pochita becomes his heart; he is alive in the latest manga chapters (as of November 2026), where Pochita erases himself to create a new timeline as Denji is being killed.

chainsaw-man-denji.about: Denji is a poor teenager working off the huge debt his father owed the yakuza by hunting devils, selling his own organs and taking any job they hand him. His only companion is Pochita, a small, dog-like chainsaw devil. When the yakuza turn on him, Pochita fuses with Denji to save him, and he becomes a hybrid who can sprout chainsaws from his head and arms whenever he yanks the starter cord in his chest. Recruited by the Public Safety officer Makima, he joins Tokyo Special Division 4. Crude, impulsive and driven by very simple dreams, such as decent food, a proper bed and a girlfriend, he is frank about those wants, which fuels much of the humour.

shigeo-kageyama.name: Shigeo Kageyama
shigeo-kageyama.role: Protagonist; middle schooler nicknamed Mob who holds immense psychic power and suppresses his emotions
shigeo-kageyama.abilities: An immensely powerful esper with telekinesis and exorcism skills who suppresses his emotions; if his feelings reach 100 percent, his power explodes uncontrollably.

fate.detail: Mob is alive at the end of the manga (2017) and the anime's third season (2022).

shigeo-kageyama.about: Shigeo Kageyama, nicknamed Mob, is a plain, bowl-haired middle schooler at Salt Middle School who happens to have psychic powers strong enough to bend reality. Because his abilities grow more dangerous when he feels too much, he has learned to keep his emotions flat, and a counter in the story tracks his rising feelings toward an explosive 100 percent. He works part-time as the assistant of Arataka Reigen, a self-proclaimed psychic who is mostly a con man but gives him sincere advice, and he joins his school's Body Improvement Club to become a better person without relying on his powers. Mob is polite, awkward and kind, and refuses to use his power on people.

chainsaw-man-power.name: Power
chainsaw-man-power.role: Blood Fiend and Public Safety Devil Hunter assigned as Denji's partner
chainsaw-man-power.abilities: A Blood Fiend who shapes her own blood into weapons such as hammers and scythes, and is as reckless as she is strong.

fate.detail: Makima kills her (manga chapter 81, Part 1); her Blood Devil form briefly returns to give Denji her blood, and in the new timeline Pochita creates in Part 2 she is alive again. The anime has not reached her death yet.

chainsaw-man-power.about: Power is a Fiend, a devil that has taken over a human corpse, specifically the Blood Devil, and she works as a Public Safety Devil Hunter in Tokyo Special Division 4, where Makima assigns her as Denji's partner. She has small red horns and sharp teeth, and she shapes her own blood into weapons such as hammers and scythes. Arrogant, selfish and a habitual liar, she brags constantly about her own greatness, avoids baths, and blames others for anything she does wrong. Her one soft spot is her pet cat, Meowy. Her chaotic partnership with Denji and their shared apartment with Aki Hayakawa drive much of the comedy.

violet-evergarden.name: Violet Evergarden
violet-evergarden.role: Protagonist; former child soldier who becomes an Auto Memory Doll writing letters for clients

debut.episodeTitle: "I Love You" and Auto Memory Dolls

violet-evergarden.notes: Light novel volume 1 per the Violet Evergarden Wiki; she is the title character of the first volume (Wikipedia). Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
violet-evergarden.abilities: A former child soldier with formidable combat skills and mechanical prosthetic arms, who becomes an Auto Memory Doll writing letters for clients.

fate.detail: Violet survives the series and the 2020 film, which ends with her staying on Ecarte Island with Gilbert.

violet-evergarden.about: Violet Evergarden is a young woman who grew up on the battlefield as a soldier, knowing only how to carry out orders, and who lost both arms in the war that just ended. She now has mechanical prosthetic hands and no clear idea of who she is outside the army. The words 'I love you', spoken to her by her commanding officer, Major Gilbert Bougainvillea, stay with her, and she wants to understand them. So she takes a job at the CH Postal Company as an Auto Memory Doll, a professional writer who turns clients' feelings into letters. At first she writes with blunt literal precision, and each client teaches her something about human emotion.

edward-elric.name: Edward Elric
edward-elric.role: Protagonist; State Alchemist known as the Fullmetal Alchemist who searches for the Philosopher's Stone with his brother
edward-elric.abilities: The youngest State Alchemist, known as the Fullmetal Alchemist, who can transmute without a circle and fights with an automail right arm and left leg.

fate.detail: Edward survives; he gives up his ability to use alchemy to bring Al back (manga chapter 108; Brotherhood episode 63) and starts a family with Winry.

edward-elric.about: Edward Elric is a fifteen-year-old alchemist from Resembool and the youngest State Alchemist in the history of Amestris, known by his official title, the Fullmetal Alchemist. As children, he and his younger brother Alphonse tried to bring their mother back with forbidden human transmutation; the attempt cost Edward his left leg and Alphonse his entire body, and Edward gave his right arm to bind his brother's soul to a suit of armour. He now uses automail prosthetics and travels with Al in search of the Philosopher's Stone, hoping to restore them both. Brash, stubborn and extremely touchy about his height, he can transmute without drawing a circle.

sakura-matou.name: Sakura Matou
sakura-matou.role: Younger daughter of the Tohsaka family who has been adopted into the Matou family
sakura-matou.notes: Episode 1 is confirmed by the Wikipedia episode summary and a TYPE-MOON Wiki quote attributed to Fate/Zero episode 1. She first appeared in the Fate/stay night visual novel (2004); Fate/Zero light novel volume and chapter not confirmed.
sakura-matou.abilities: A young girl adopted into the Matou family of mages, which abuses her with crest worms to adapt her to its magic.

fate.detail: Sakura survives Fate/Zero; in the sequel Fate/stay night her fate depends on the route, and she survives the Heaven's Feel route's True End.

sakura-matou.about: Sakura Matou is a small, quiet girl in Fate/Zero who was born the younger daughter of the Tohsaka family of mages and given away to the rival Matou family to be raised as their heir. Separated from her mother and her older sister, Rin, she lives in the Matou house under its patriarch, Zouken, whose methods of training her are cruel, and she has learned to stop expecting anything. Her situation drives Kariya Matou, who walked away from his family's magecraft years ago and is a childhood friend of Sakura's mother, to enter the Fourth Holy Grail War, hoping to win and set her free. Sakura's blank, resigned manner makes her one of the darkest threads in the story.

jujutsu-kaisen-megumi-fushiguro.name: Megumi Fushiguro
jujutsu-kaisen-megumi-fushiguro.role: First-year student at Tokyo Jujutsu High who fights with shikigami summoned from shadows
jujutsu-kaisen-megumi-fushiguro.notes: Other relatives are left out to avoid spoilers.
jujutsu-kaisen-megumi-fushiguro.abilities: A first-year sorcerer who uses the Ten Shadows Technique to summon shikigami, such as his Divine Dogs, from shadows through hand signs.

fate.detail: Sukuna takes over his body during the Culling Game and keeps it until Yuji frees him in the Shinjuku Showdown; Megumi survives to the series' end (manga chapter 271, 2024).

jujutsu-kaisen-megumi-fushiguro.about: Megumi Fushiguro is a first-year at Tokyo Jujutsu High, the school that trains sorcerers to exorcise curses born from human negativity. He is sent to an ordinary high school to recover a dangerous cursed object, one of Sukuna's fingers, and that mission is how he meets Yuji Itadori. Serious, reserved and quietly principled, Megumi would rather save people he believes are good than try to save everyone, and he makes no secret of his irritation with recklessness. He fights with the Ten Shadows Technique, forming hand signs to summon shikigami from shadows, starting with his pair of Divine Dogs. His teacher is the famously powerful Satoru Gojo, and he cares deeply for his stepsister, Tsumiki.

joseph-joestar.name: Joseph Joestar
joseph-joestar.role: Protagonist of Part 2, Battle Tendency; Jonathan Joestar's grandson, living in New York
joseph-joestar.notes: Chapter 45 ("New York's JoJo") is the first chapter of Battle Tendency. He returns as an older ally in Part 3, Stardust Crusaders. His mother and descendants are left out to avoid spoilers.
joseph-joestar.abilities: A brash, cunning Hamon user who predicts his opponents' words ('Your next line is...') and wins through tricks and improvised weapons such as clackers.

fate.detail: In Part 3, Stardust Crusaders, DIO drains his blood and Joseph dies, but Jotaro revives him with a transfusion of DIO's blood; he lives on as an old man in later parts.

joseph-joestar.about: Joseph Joestar leads Battle Tendency, the saga's second part, as a cocky young Englishman who shares a home in 1930s New York with Erina, his grandmother. He is Jonathan Joestar's grandson and was born able to use the Ripple, the sunlight-charged breathing technique his grandfather had to be taught, though Joseph has never practised it properly. Where Jonathan was earnest, Joseph is a loudmouth and a trickster who wins with bluffs, traps and improvised weapons, and who loves to announce what his opponent is about to say before they say it. When his family's old friend Speedwagon goes missing in Mexico, Joseph sets out to find him.

shouto-todoroki.name: Shouto Todoroki
shouto-todoroki.role: Student in U.A. High School's Class 1-A who can create ice and fire

debut.episodeTitle: What I Can Do For Now

shouto-todoroki.notes: Chapter 6 is confirmed by both sources. Episode 5 rests on the My Hero Academia Wiki; the Wikipedia summaries of episodes 5 and 6 do not name him. His father is the pro hero Endeavor; other relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
shouto-todoroki.abilities: His Quirk, Half-Cold Half-Hot, creates ice from his right side and fire from his left, though at first he refuses to use his fire.

fate.detail: Todoroki survives the final war against Dabi and is alive at the series' end (manga final chapter 430, 2024).

shouto-todoroki.about: Shouto Todoroki is a first-year in U.A. High School's Class 1-A who won his place through an official recommendation. His Quirk, Half-Cold Half-Hot, lets him create ice from his right side and fire from his left, and his hair is split white and red to match, with a burn scar around his left eye. His father is Endeavor, the Number Two hero, who has pushed him relentlessly to surpass All Might. Cold, quiet and focused, Shouto resents his father so deeply that he refuses to use his fire in battle, relying on ice alone. That refusal and his growing rivalry with Izuku Midoriya come to a head at the U.A. Sports Festival.

megumin.name: Megumin
megumin.role: Crimson Demon archwizard who only uses Explosion magic; joins Kazuma's party

debut.anime: Kono Subarashii Sekai ni Shukufuku wo!

megumin.notes: Episode 2 is confirmed by both sources. Light novel volume 1 rests on the KonoSuba Wiki.
megumin.abilities: An Arch-wizard of the Crimson Demon clan who knows only one spell, Explosion, which she can cast once a day before collapsing.

fate.detail: Megumin is alive in the anime and at the end of the main light novel series (2020).

megumin.about: Megumin is a young archwizard from the Crimson Demon clan, a village of red-eyed mages with a taste for dramatic poses and strange names. She answers Kazuma Sato's call for party members with a theatrical self-introduction, eyepatch and all, and turns out to know exactly one spell: Explosion, the most destructive attack magic there is. She can cast it only once a day, after which she collapses and has to be carried home. Megumin refuses to learn anything else, because to her nothing compares to the beauty of a perfect blast. She is proud, stubborn, often hungry and quick to take offence at anyone who mocks her name. Kazuma ends up taking her on daily explosion walks.

rem-3.name: Rem
rem-3.role: Maid at Roswaal L. Mathers's mansion and twin sister of Ram
rem-3.notes: Episode 4 is confirmed by both sources. Light novel volume 2 rests on the Re:Zero Wiki; Wikipedia gives her web novel debut chapter, "The Road to Redemption Begins". Parents left out to avoid spoilers.
rem-3.abilities: A maid of the Roswaal mansion and an oni who fights with a flail called the Morning Star, uses water magic and can enter a powerful oni form.

fate.detail: Rem is killed in timelines that Subaru resets with Return by Death, and falls into a coma after Gluttony eats her name and memories (season 2, episode 1); she is not dead, and in the ongoing light novels she wakes at the end of Arc 6.

rem-3.about: Rem and her older twin sister, Ram, work as maids in the mansion of the eccentric margrave Roswaal L. Mathers. With short blue hair that falls over her right eye and a polite, formal way of speaking, she handles much of the household's cooking and cleaning and is far better at chores than her sister. Rem idolises Ram, believing her sister surpasses her in every way, and she quietly regards herself as the lesser twin. When Subaru Natsuki is brought to the mansion to recover from his injuries, she treats the strange newcomer with courteous but watchful suspicion. In a fight she wields a spiked flail on a chain and uses water magic.

gintoki-sakata.name: Gintoki Sakata
gintoki-sakata.role: Protagonist; silver-haired samurai who runs the Yorozuya odd-jobs business in Edo

debut.episodeTitle: You Guys!! Do You Even Have Gintama?!

gintoki-sakata.notes: Episodes 1 and 2 aired together as a one-hour anime-original special; the first manga chapter (Lesson 1, "Nobody with Natural Wavy Hair Can Be That Bad") is adapted in episode 3. Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
gintoki-sakata.abilities: A lazy, sweet-toothed freelancer who is secretly a legendary samurai from the Joui War, fighting with a wooden sword with superhuman skill.

fate.detail: Gintoki is alive at the end of the manga (2019) and the anime's final film, Gintama: The Final (2021).

gintoki-sakata.about: Gintoki Sakata is a lazy, silver-haired samurai in an alternate Edo that has been taken over by aliens, where swords are banned and the old warrior class has been pushed aside. He runs the Yorozuya, an odd-jobs business that accepts almost any request, with the earnest Shinpachi Shimura, the alien girl Kagura and a giant dog named Sadaharu. Gintoki has a sweet tooth, reads Weekly Shonen Jump as an adult, owes rent to his landlady, and carries a wooden sword engraved with the words 'Lake Toya'. Most of the time he is a slacker in a gag comedy, but when someone he cares about is threatened, the swordsman underneath comes out.

subaru-natsuki.name: Subaru Natsuki
subaru-natsuki.role: Protagonist; teenager suddenly transported to another world on his way home from a convenience store

debut.episodeTitle: The End of the Beginning and the Beginning of the End

subaru-natsuki.notes: Light novel volume 1 per the Re:Zero Wiki; Wikipedia gives his web novel debut in the prologue (2014). Relatives left out.
subaru-natsuki.abilities: He has no combat skills, but his power 'Return by Death' sends him back to an earlier checkpoint with his memories whenever he dies.

fate.detail: He dies many times starting in the first arc, each time returning to a checkpoint through Return by Death; he is alive in the anime and the ongoing light novels.

subaru-natsuki.about: Subaru Natsuki is a seventeen-year-old shut-in from modern Japan who, while walking home from a convenience store, suddenly finds himself in a fantasy world with nothing but the clothes he is wearing and his shopping. Loud, upbeat and eager to play the hero, he is quickly out of his depth, but he discovers a strange ability he calls Return by Death: each time he dies, he wakes at an earlier point in time with his memories intact, while nobody else remembers what happened. Unable to tell anyone about it, he must relive painful events again and again to find a better outcome. He devotes himself to Emilia, a silver-haired half-elf who helps him on his first day.

ichigo-f875b8ab-821d-4659-8d8e-5f79e5fd3.name: Ichigo
ichigo-f875b8ab-821d-4659-8d8e-5f79e5fd3.role: Leader of Squad 13 and pistil who pilots the Franxx Delphinium with Goro
ichigo-f875b8ab-821d-4659-8d8e-5f79e5fd3.notes: Darling in the Franxx is an original anime (the manga runs alongside it), so source is null. Episode 1 rests on the Darling in the Franxx Wiki; the Wikipedia summary of episode 1 does not name her. Code number 015 (both sources). Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
ichigo-f875b8ab-821d-4659-8d8e-5f79e5fd3.abilities: Squad 13's leader and a FRANXX pilot (Delphinium, partnered with Goro), a capable and level-headed pilot who coordinates the team in battle.

fate.detail: Ichigo survives the series; the final episode shows her married to Goro and expecting their first child.

ichigo-f875b8ab-821d-4659-8d8e-5f79e5fd3.about: Ichigo, code number 015, is the leader of Squad 13, a group of children raised in an isolated facility to pilot giant robots called FRANXX against monsters known as klaxosaurs. Each FRANXX needs a boy and a girl working as a pair, and Ichigo pilots the unit Delphinium alongside her partner Goro. She has short blue hair and a strong sense of duty, keeps the squad organised in combat, and takes her role seriously, sometimes to the point of bossiness. Ichigo has known Hiro, the squad's former prodigy, since they were small, and she becomes openly wary when the mysterious pilot Zero Two takes an interest in him. As leader, she feels responsible for holding everyone together.

kiyotaka-ayanokouji.name: Kiyotaka Ayanokouji
kiyotaka-ayanokouji.role: Protagonist; quiet, low-key student in Class 1-D at the Advanced Nurturing High School

debut.anime: Youkoso Jitsuryoku Shijou Shugi no Kyoushitsu e
debut.episodeTitle: What is Evil? Whatever Springs from Weakness.

kiyotaka-ayanokouji.notes: Light novel volume 1 per the Classroom of the Elite Wiki; Wikipedia's episode 1 summary introduces him joining Class 1-D. Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
kiyotaka-ayanokouji.abilities: A seemingly average student of Class D who deliberately hides his intellect, physical strength and skill at manipulating others, scoring exactly 50 points on every exam.

fate.detail: Ayanokouji is alive in the anime and in the ongoing light novels.

kiyotaka-ayanokouji.about: Kiyotaka Ayanokouji is a first-year at the Advanced Nurturing High School, a government-run school in Tokyo that promises its graduates almost any university or job they want. New students are sorted into classes, and Ayanokouji is placed in Class D, regarded as the weakest of them, after scoring exactly 50 points in every entrance exam subject. Quiet, expressionless and apparently unremarkable, he finds it hard to make friends and prefers to stay in the background. Yet he notices everything, and he quietly helps classmates such as the aloof Suzune Horikita while making sure someone else takes the credit. The gap between his bland surface and what lies underneath is the series' hook.

zero-two.name: Zero Two
zero-two.role: Horned pistil known as the "Partner Killer" who pairs with Hiro to pilot the Franxx Strelizia
zero-two.notes: Darling in the Franxx is an original anime (the Kentaro Yabuki manga runs alongside it), so source is null. Her code is 002. Relatives and affiliations left out to avoid spoilers.
zero-two.abilities: An elite FRANXX pilot with klaxosaur blood, nicknamed the 'Partner Killer' because no co-pilot had survived three rides with her, who pilots Strelizia with Hiro.

fate.detail: In the anime's final episode (24), Zero Two and Hiro sacrifice themselves to destroy the VIRM homeworld and are implied to be reincarnated on Earth much later; in the manga adaptation she survives.

zero-two.about: Zero Two is an elite pilot with pink hair and two small red horns who drives the FRANXX Strelizia. She has a frightening nickname, the 'Partner Killer', because the boys who pilot with her tend not to survive more than a few rides. Hiro, a former prodigy who washed out as a pilot, first meets her bathing in a lake in the forest, and she promptly decides he is her 'darling'. When a monster attack throws the base into chaos, she lets him climb into Strelizia with her, and the two prove a strong match. Zero Two is playful, impulsive, fond of sweets and openly scornful of the adults' rules, which makes her very different from other pilots.

hitagi-senjougahara.name: Hitagi Senjougahara
hitagi-senjougahara.role: Koyomi Araragi's classmate, afflicted by an oddity that has taken away her weight
hitagi-senjougahara.notes: Wikipedia titles episode 1 "Hitagi Crab, Part One". She debuts in "Hitagi Crab", the first story of the Bakemonogatari light novel; volume and chapter numbers not confirmed. Relatives left out.
hitagi-senjougahara.abilities: A sharp-tongued girl who has lost almost all her weight to an apparition, the Heavy Stone Crab; she defends herself with stationery such as staplers and box cutters.

fate.detail: Hitagi is alive throughout the Monogatari series and later appears as an adult.

hitagi-senjougahara.about: Hitagi Senjougahara is a third-year at Naoetsu Private High School who has spent years keeping to herself; classmates know her as a frail girl with some incurable illness, and Koyomi Araragi has barely heard her speak. When he catches her during a fall, he discovers she weighs almost nothing. In her first year she encountered a strange crab and lost her weight, and she has kept people at arm's length ever since to protect that secret, threatening Koyomi with a stapler and a box cutter once he finds out. Sharp-tongued, deadpan and alarmingly direct, she becomes the first person he helps with an oddity, and their verbal sparring sets the tone for much of the series.

shouyou-hinata.name: Shouyou Hinata
shouyou-hinata.role: Protagonist; short middle blocker with a huge jump on Karasuno High's volleyball team
shouyou-hinata.notes: Chapter 1 is "Endings and Beginnings" (both sources). Arc names follow the Haikyu!! Wiki.
shouyou-hinata.abilities: A short middle blocker with incredible jumping power, speed and stamina, known for the lightning-fast 'freak quick' attack with Kageyama.

fate.detail: Nobody dies in Haikyu!!; the epilogue shows Hinata playing beach volleyball in Brazil, then professionally for the MSBY Black Jackals in Japan's V.League and later Asas São Paulo.

shouyou-hinata.about: Shouyou Hinata is a short, endlessly energetic boy who fell in love with volleyball after watching a small player nicknamed the 'Little Giant' soar over the net for Karasuno High on television. His middle school had no boys' team, so he practised with whoever he could find, and his only official match ended in a crushing defeat by Tobio Kageyama, a gifted setter known as the 'King of the Court'. Hinata enrolls at Karasuno to get his revenge, only to find Kageyama joining the same club. Forced to work together, the rivals develop a lightning-fast attack built on Hinata's jumping and speed. His relentless enthusiasm carries the first season.

ichigo-kurosaki.name: Ichigo Kurosaki
ichigo-kurosaki.role: Protagonist; teenager who can see ghosts and gains the powers of a Shinigami

debut.episodeTitle: The Day I Became a Shinigami

ichigo-kurosaki.notes: Chapter 1 is "Death & Strawberry" (Wikipedia; the Bleach Wiki places it in volume 1). Other relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
ichigo-kurosaki.abilities: A teenager who can see ghosts and gains Soul Reaper powers from Rukia, fighting with his oversized Zanpakuto, Zangetsu.

fate.detail: In Hueco Mundo, Ulquiorra blasts a hole through his chest and kills him (anime episode 271), but he revives in a rampaging Hollow form when Orihime cries for help; he survives the series and is married to Orihime in the final chapter (686).

ichigo-kurosaki.about: Ichigo Kurosaki is a fifteen-year-old high school student in Karakura Town with spiky orange hair, a permanent scowl and little patience for people who pick fights with him. He has been able to see ghosts all his life and lives with his eccentric doctor father and two younger sisters at the family clinic. When a Soul Reaper named Rukia Kuchiki is wounded protecting his family from a Hollow, a monstrous evil spirit, she transfers her powers to him, and Ichigo takes over her duties of guiding lost souls and fighting Hollows. Stubborn, short-tempered and fiercely protective, he insists he only fights for the people he can reach, wielding a sword nearly as tall as he is.

asuka-langley.name: Asuka Langley Souryuu
asuka-langley.role: Pilot of Evangelion Unit-02 who transfers to Japan from Germany
asuka-langley.notes: Episode 8 is confirmed by both sources; the Wikipedia episode list renders its title "Asuka Arrives in Japan". Neon Genesis Evangelion is an original anime, so source is null; she first appears in volume 4 of the Sadamoto manga. Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
asuka-langley.abilities: A confident, highly trained Eva pilot who pilots Evangelion Unit-02 with aggressive skill and graduated from university at a young age.

fate.detail: In The End of Evangelion (1997), Unit-02 is torn apart by the Mass Production Evangelions, but Asuka is alive beside Shinji in the final scene.

asuka-langley.about: Asuka Langley Souryuu is the fourteen-year-old pilot of Evangelion Unit-02, who arrives in Japan from Germany aboard a United Nations fleet carrying her red Eva. Already a university graduate, she is brash, competitive and quick to show off, and she makes no secret of thinking she is the best pilot Nerv has, looking down on both Shinji Ikari and the quiet Rei Ayanami. Her first meeting with Shinji turns into an Angel fight at sea, where she drags him into her cockpit. Asuka has a crush on Ryoji Kaji, the man escorting her, and soon moves into Misato Katsuragi's apartment alongside Shinji. Her pride and temper set her sharply apart from the more withdrawn pilots around her.

spike-spiegel.name: Spike Spiegel
spike-spiegel.role: Protagonist; laid-back bounty hunter aboard the spaceship Bebop
spike-spiegel.notes: Cowboy Bebop is an original anime, so source is null. "Asteroid Blues" is session 1 in the series order; the 1998 TV Tokyo broadcast aired "Stray Dog Strut" first (Wikipedia). His past is left out to avoid spoilers.
spike-spiegel.abilities: A laid-back bounty hunter and former syndicate hitman, an expert in Jeet Kune Do, a sharpshooter, and the pilot of the Swordfish II.

fate.detail: After killing Vicious in the final session ('The Real Folk Blues Part 2'), Spike collapses on the stairs; the series leaves whether he dies deliberately ambiguous.

spike-spiegel.about: Spike Spiegel, a Mars-born bounty hunter of twenty-seven, roams the solar system in 2071 aboard the spaceship Bebop with his partner Jet Black. Tall and lanky, with a mop of dark green hair, he is laid-back to the point of laziness, nearly always broke and usually hungry. In a fight he becomes a different man: a master of Jeet Kune Do, a sharp shot with a handgun and an ace pilot in his small fighter craft, the Swordfish II. Spike hints at a violent past in a crime syndicate but rarely speaks about it, preferring to shrug off danger with the line 'Whatever happens, happens.'

shinobu-oshino.name: Shinobu Oshino
shinobu-oshino.role: Silent blonde girl who lives in the abandoned cram school with Meme Oshino
shinobu-oshino.notes: Episode 1 rests on the Monogatari Wiki episode page; the Wikipedia summaries first name her in later episodes. She first appears in the Bakemonogatari light novel ("Hitagi Crab"); volume and chapter not confirmed. Her past and relationship to Koyomi are left out to avoid spoilers.
shinobu-oshino.abilities: The weakened remnant of a once-powerful vampire, Kiss-shot Acerola-Orion Heart-Under-Blade, who lives in Koyomi's shadow and regains strength by drinking his blood.

fate.detail: Shinobu is alive in the anime and the ongoing Monogatari novels, bound to Koyomi.

shinobu-oshino.about: Shinobu Oshino is a small, pale, blonde girl who lives in an abandoned cram school with Meme Oshino, a laid-back specialist in apparitions known as oddities who helps Koyomi Araragi deal with them. She never speaks in Bakemonogatari, sitting silently in a corner of the ruined building while the others talk. Oshino gave her the name Shinobu, written with a character made of a heart beneath a blade. Araragi visits her regularly and clearly feels a heavy responsibility toward her, though the series only gradually explains why, and only later does she reveal a fondness for Mister Donut. Her silence and mystery make her stand out in a talkative series.

jujutsu-kaisen-kento-nanami.name: Kento Nanami
jujutsu-kaisen-kento-nanami.role: Grade 1 jujutsu sorcerer and former salaryman who works alongside Yuji Itadori
jujutsu-kaisen-kento-nanami.notes: Episode 8 and chapter 18 rest on the Jujutsu Kaisen Wiki; the Wikipedia summaries first name him in episode 9, "Small Fry and Reverse Retribution".
jujutsu-kaisen-kento-nanami.abilities: A Grade 1 sorcerer whose Ratio Technique creates a weak point at a 7:3 point on any target, and who grows stronger by working overtime under a binding vow.

fate.detail: During the Shibuya Incident, badly burned by Jogo, he is killed by Mahito (manga chapter 120; anime season 2 episode 18).

jujutsu-kaisen-kento-nanami.about: Kento Nanami, a Grade 1 jujutsu sorcerer, left the jujutsu world after graduating from Tokyo Jujutsu High, spent several years as an office worker, and then came back after deciding that sorcery was the slightly less miserable of two kinds of work. Dressed in a neat suit, patterned tie and tinted glasses, he treats exorcism like a job with fixed hours and hates overtime. Satoru Gojo, a senior he openly finds hard to respect, asks him to take Yuji Itadori along on a case, and Nanami makes it clear that he sees the teenager as a child he is responsible for. His cursed technique, Ratio, creates a weak point at the 7:3 mark of any target.

rimuru-tempest.name: Rimuru Tempest
rimuru-tempest.role: Protagonist; office worker reborn as a slime in another world who befriends the Storm Dragon Veldora
rimuru-tempest.notes: Light novel volume 1 per the Tensura Wiki; the series began as a web novel. In his previous life he was Satoru Mikami (Wikipedia episode 1 summary). Manga debut is chapter 1, "Death and Reincarnation" (wiki).
rimuru-tempest.abilities: A slime who can devour anything with his Predator skill and copy its abilities, aided by the analytical skill Great Sage.

fate.detail: Rimuru is alive in the anime and the ongoing light novels; his past life as Satoru Mikami ended when he was stabbed in episode 1, which is how he was reborn as a slime.

rimuru-tempest.about: Rimuru Tempest begins life as Satoru Mikami, a thirty-seven-year-old office worker in Tokyo whose life ends abruptly in the first episode. He wakes in a dark cave in another world as a small blue slime, with no eyes or mouth but with two unusual skills: Predator, which lets him swallow things and copy their abilities, and Great Sage, an inner voice that analyses everything. Deep in the cave he meets Veldora, a Storm Dragon sealed away for centuries, and the two become friends and share the surname Tempest. Rimuru then heads out into the Great Jura Forest, where his easygoing nature leads him to start protecting the monsters he meets.

sasuke-uchiha.name: Sasuke Uchiha
sasuke-uchiha.role: Member of Team 7 and one of the last of the Uchiha clan; Naruto's rival
sasuke-uchiha.notes: Chapter 3 ("Enter Sasuke!") is confirmed by both sources. Episode 1 rests on Narutopedia; the Wikipedia summaries first name him in episode 3, "Sasuke and Sakura: Friends or Foes?". Arcs listed are Part I arcs; later arcs and his own family left out to avoid spoilers.
sasuke-uchiha.abilities: A prodigy of the Uchiha clan and the top student of his class, skilled with fire-style ninjutsu, shuriken and taijutsu, who awakens his Sharingan in the Land of Waves.

fate.detail: Sasuke survives the series; in the final arc he is gravely wounded by Madara but saved, and the epilogue shows him married to Sakura with a daughter, Sarada.

sasuke-uchiha.about: Sasuke Uchiha belongs to the Uchiha clan, of which almost nobody else remains, and he is the top student of his year at Konoha's ninja academy. Brooding, aloof and fiercely competitive, he is placed on Team 7 with Naruto Uzumaki and Sakura Haruno under Kakashi Hatake, and at first he treats teamwork as a distraction from his own goals. Introducing himself, he states that his ambition is to restore his clan and to kill a certain someone. He is skilled with fire-style techniques, shuriken and hand-to-hand combat, and he awakens his clan's Sharingan during the mission to the Land of Waves. His rivalry with Naruto, part contempt and part kinship, anchors the series.

erwin-smith.name: Erwin Smith

debut.episodeTitle: To You, in 2000 Years: The Fall of Shiganshina, Part 1

erwin-smith.notes: Episode 1 and chapter 1 ("To You, 2,000 Years From Now") rest on the Attack on Titan Wiki; Wikipedia's episode 1 summary does not name him. Wikipedia confirms he succeeds Keith Shadis as commander.
erwin-smith.abilities: The 13th Commander of the Survey Corps, a brilliant strategist who created the Long-Range Scouting Formation that cut the Corps' losses outside the walls.

fate.detail: Erwin is mortally wounded leading a suicide charge against the Beast Titan in the Return to Shiganshina arc (anime season 3 part 2), and Levi chooses to give the Titan serum to Armin instead, letting him die.

erwin-smith.about: Erwin Smith leads the Survey Corps, the military branch that ventures beyond humanity's walls to study and fight the man-eating Titans. Tall, composed and persuasive, he inspires fierce devotion from his soldiers, including the elite fighter Levi, even though he sends them on missions where many of them die. Erwin designed the long-range scouting formation that lets the Corps spot Titans early and avoid them. When Eren Yeager's ability to become a Titan is revealed, Erwin argues to place Eren under the Survey Corps' protection. He also recruits new cadets with a speech asking them to dedicate their hearts to humanity. His readiness to make cold, calculated choices for humanity's sake defines him.

hachiman-hikigaya.name: Hachiman Hikigaya
hachiman-hikigaya.role: Protagonist; cynical loner at Sobu High School who is made to join the Service Club

debut.anime: Yahari Ore no Seishun Love Comedy wa Machigatteiru.
debut.episodeTitle: Youth Romantic Comedy Is Wrong, as I Expected

hachiman-hikigaya.notes: Episode title as in the Wikipedia episode list; the Oregairu Wiki calls episode 1 "And Thus Their Mistaken Youth Begins." Light novel volume 1, chapter 1 per the wiki.
hachiman-hikigaya.abilities: A cynical loner with sharp observational skills, who solves the Service Club's problems in unconventional and often self-sacrificing ways.

fate.detail: Hachiman is alive at the end of the light novels and the anime's third season (2020); the series is a romantic comedy with no character deaths.

hachiman-hikigaya.about: Hachiman Hikigaya is a second-year at Sobu High School, a sharp-witted loner with dull 'dead fish' eyes who insists that youth and its friendships are a lie told by hypocrites. Fed up with his cynical attitude, his teacher Shizuka Hiratsuka makes him join the Service Club, which helps students with their problems and is run by the brilliant, icy Yukino Yukinoshita. The cheerful Yui Yuigahama soon joins them. Hachiman resolves requests with unconventional and often self-sacrificing tactics, willingly taking blame or ridicule onto himself if it fixes the problem. He dotes on his younger sister Komachi, and his acerbic inner monologue narrates the series.

koyomi-araragi.name: Koyomi Araragi
koyomi-araragi.role: Protagonist; third-year at Naoetsu Private High School who helps girls afflicted by oddities
koyomi-araragi.notes: Wikipedia titles episode 1 "Hitagi Crab, Part One". First appears in the Bakemonogatari light novel (2006); volume and chapter not confirmed.
koyomi-araragi.abilities: A high-schooler who was once turned into a vampire and kept some vampiric traits, chiefly rapid healing, which he uses to help girls troubled by apparitions.

fate.detail: Izuko Gaen kills him in Owarimonogatari (Mayoi Hell), sending him to hell, where he meets Mayoi before coming back to life; he is alive afterwards.

koyomi-araragi.about: Koyomi Araragi, in his final year at Naoetsu Private High School, is barely passing anything except maths and claims he avoids making friends on principle. An encounter with a vampire during the previous spring break left him not quite human, with leftover traits such as healing from injuries at unnatural speed. When he catches the reserved classmate Hitagi Senjougahara as she falls down a staircase and finds she weighs almost nothing, he takes her to Meme Oshino, an expert in the supernatural problems called oddities. From then on he keeps getting involved in other girls' oddity troubles. He is talkative, self-mocking and quick with banter, and narrates the story.

akemi-homura.name: Homura Akemi
akemi-homura.role: Mysterious transfer student at Mitakihara Middle School who is a magical girl

debut.episodeTitle: I First Met Her in a Dream... or Something.

akemi-homura.notes: Madoka Magica is an original anime (the manga adapts it), so source is null. Her article renders the episode title "As If I Met Her in My Dream...". Her past is left out to avoid spoilers.
akemi-homura.abilities: A mysterious transfer student and magical girl who fights with guns and explosives and seems to know what will happen before it does.

fate.detail: Homura survives the TV series and the film Rebellion (2013), at the end of which she becomes a demon-like being who rewrites the world.

akemi-homura.about: Homura Akemi transfers into Madoka Kaname's class at Mitakihara Middle School the day after Madoka dreams of seeing her fight amid a ruined city. Elegant, top of the class in studies and sport, and coldly distant toward almost everyone, she draws instant attention, yet she behaves as if she already knows Madoka. She soon makes it clear, with unsettling intensity, that Madoka must never become a magical girl. Homura is a magical girl herself, but she fights with guns and explosives rather than conjured weapons, and she is openly hostile to Kyubey, the creature offering contracts.

saber.name: Artoria Pendragon
saber.role: Saber-class Servant summoned by Kiritsugu Emiya for the Fourth Holy Grail War
saber.notes: Episode 1 rests on the Wikipedia episode summary; the TYPE-MOON Wiki gives no episode. She first appeared in the Fate/stay night visual novel (2004); Fate/Zero light novel volume not confirmed. Usually called Saber.
saber.abilities: Saber-class Servant King Arthur, a master swordswoman wielding the invisible sword Excalibur, whose true name release unleashes a devastating beam of light.

fate.detail: She is a hero who is dying at the Battle of Camlann: at the end of Fate/Zero she is forced to destroy the Grail and returns to that moment, and in Fate/stay night's Fate route she finally accepts her death there.
